Abraham's (Ibrahim) seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. When it became clear that his father was an enemy of Allah, he immediately dissociated himself from him. This shows that supplication and seeking forgiveness for the enemies of Allah is not permissible. After Allah has guided a people, He does not leave them to go astray until He makes clear to them what they must avoid. For He knows all things. The dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah; there is no protector or helper besides Him.

Allah granted repentance to the Prophet and to the Emigrants (Muhajirun) and the Helpers (Ansar) who followed him in his hour of hardship. This took place especially during the distressing days of the Expedition of Tabuk. Great hardships were endured during that expedition, and the shortage of riding mounts and provisions reached an extreme level. There were those whose hearts nearly swerved. However, Allah, through His favor, enabled them to repent and accepted their repentance. Indeed, He is most compassionate and merciful.

Furthermore, Allah forgave the three individuals whose judgment had been deferred. These were Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah. They fell into such distress that the earth, vast as it is, became narrow for them, and their souls were constricted. They realized that there was no refuge from Allah except in turning to Him. Then Allah enabled them to repent and accepted their repentance. He is indeed the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.

Ka'b ibn Malik had not taken part in the Battle of Tabuk. Yet until that day, he had never stayed behind from any battle except Badr. During the Expedition of Tabuk, his financial situation was very favorable; he possessed two riding mounts. However, when preparations for the expedition began at a time when the fruits had ripened and the shade had become pleasant, he wished to prepare as well, but could not make up his mind. Constantly procrastinating by saying 'there is still time,' he was ultimately unprepared when the army moved out. Although he wanted to catch up with them later, he was unable to do so.

When walking among those who remained behind in Medina, he was grieved to see no one other than hypocrites and those with valid excuses. The Prophet (peace be upon him) asked about him in Tabuk, and some made up excuses. Upon returning, after the Prophet stopped by the mosque and prayed, those who had not joined the expedition began to present their excuses. When it was Ka'b's turn, he decided to tell the truth and said, 'By Allah, I had no excuse whatsoever; I stayed behind at a time when I was at my most prosperous.' Thereupon, the Prophet said, 'This one has spoken the truth; stand up and wait until Allah reveals His judgment.'

Muslims were forbidden from speaking with Ka'b and his two companions (Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah). People turned away from them, refusing even to return their greetings. Ka'b was resilient; he would go to the mosque and pray, but no one would speak to him. This isolation, which lasted for fifty days, weighed very heavily upon him. One day, he immediately burned an offer letter sent by the King of Ghassan. Later, by order of the Prophet, they were also separated from their wives. These distressing days lasted for exactly fifty nights.

On the morning of the fiftieth night, someone called out from Mount Sal', 'Glad tidings!' Ka'b immediately fell in prostration. Allah's acceptance of repentance had arrived. The Prophet (peace be upon him) had announced this glad tiding at the morning prayer. When Ka'b went to the mosque, the Prophet's face was shining like the moon. He said, 'Rejoice with the glad tiding of the best day you have had since you were born.' Ka'b wished to give some of his wealth as charity, but the Prophet told him to retain a portion of it. Ka'b then promised that he would speak only the truth from that point forward.

In the verses (119-123), the believers are commanded to fear Allah and be with the truthful. It is not permissible for the people of Medina and the desert Arabs around them to oppose the Prophet or fail to share in his hardships. Thirst, fatigue, hunger endured in the cause of Allah, and every strike taken against the enemy are rewarded. A reward is recorded for every expenditure, small or large, and for crossing every valley. It is not appropriate for all believers to go to war; a group from every tribe should deepen their understanding of religious sciences so that they may warn their people when they return from battle. One should first fight the disbelievers who are close at hand, so that they may find firmness in you. Allah is with the righteous.

In verses 124-127, the condition of the hypocrites is described. Whenever a surah is revealed, they mockingly ask, 'Which of you has this increased in faith?' The faith of the believers increases, and they rejoice. As for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds disbelief to their disbelief, and they die as disbelievers. They see that they are tried once or twice every year, yet they do not repent nor do they take heed. Whenever a surah is revealed against them, they look at one another and then slip away. Allah has turned their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.

In this section, the issue of faith increasing is addressed. The hypocrites mocked whenever a surah was revealed, saying, 'Which of you has this surah increased in faith?' Yet the increase of faith is possible both qualitatively and quantitatively. Qualitative increase is the elevation of the strength and degree of faith, whereas quantitative increase occurs through the multiplication of the matters to be believed. Abraham's desire for his heart to be at peace is an example of qualitative increase. Moreover, as the number of things believed in increases, quantitative increase takes place.

For believers, every surah increases faith and brings them joy. As for the hypocrites in whose hearts is a disease, with every surah they add a new measure to their disbelief and hypocrisy. They are afflicted with trials once or twice every year, yet they still do not repent and do not come to their senses. When a surah is revealed, they look at one another and sneak away; Allah has turned their hearts because they are a people devoid of understanding.

In verse 128, it is stated that Allah has sent to the believers a messenger from among themselves. That prophet possesses dignity; any hardship befalling the believers grieves him heavily, and he is deeply concerned for them and full of mercy. Here, the attributes 'ra'uf' (kind) and 'rahim' (merciful) are given to the Prophet, which are among the beautiful names of Allah. These attributes emphasize the Prophet's compassion and mercy toward the believers.

In verse 129, it is commanded to say against those who turn away: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him; in Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.' It is narrated that these two verses (128-129) were the very last verses of the Quran to be revealed. Furthermore, it is reported that during the compilation of the Mushaf, the written copy of these verses was found only with Khuzaymah ibn Thabit and was collected from him by Zayd ibn Thabit.

Finally, it is stated that these verses at the end of this surah remind the believers of the Prophet's compassion and the importance of reliance on Allah (tawakkul). In addition, in a hadith narrated by Abu al-Darda, it is mentioned that whoever recites the prayer 'Hasbiyallah' (Allah is sufficient for me) seven times in the morning and evening will attain Allah's help. Surah at-Tawbah is thus concluded.

The surah begins with disjointed letters (huruf al-muqatta'at) such as Alif-Lam-Ra. These letters are a secret known to Allah and demonstrate the miraculous nature of the Quran. There are different views regarding their meaning: some have stated that they signify meanings such as 'I am the Lord' or 'I am Allah, I see.' However, the most appropriate view is that these letters are ambiguous (mutashabih) and that their true meaning must be left to Allah. Furthermore, these letters serve as the name of the surah, draw attention to the power of deriving boundless meanings from limited letters, and indicate that the Quran is a divine book.

The annexation of the verses to the whole Book indicates that this surah is a part of that wise Book. The attribute 'Hakim' conveys the meanings that the Quran is full of wisdom, decisive (muhkam), giving judgment, and being governed by wisdom. The Quran is a book filled with divine wisdom, serving as a basis for judging with justice and goodness, and protected from corruption. This surah is also among the verses of that Book and contains divine secrets and wisdom that confound the disbelievers.

People found it strange that revelation should come to a man from among human beings and said, 'This is an evident magician.' Yet this is a grace from Allah. The 'qadam-i sidq' (footing of truth)—that is, the station of truthfulness—granted to the Prophet expresses his high rank in the sight of Allah and his authority of intercession. For the believers, this is great glad tidings. It is the disbelievers' viewing of this matter as strange and calling it sorcery that is truly astonishing, for choosing the prophet from among human beings is full of wisdom in terms of establishing familiarity with them.

Your Lord is Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne (istiwa) and directs all affairs. No one can intercede without His permission. Such is Allah, your Lord; so worship Him. And to Him is your return. Allah originates creation, then repeats it in order to reward with justice those who believe and do righteous deeds. As for the disbelievers, for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment.

Allah made the sun a radiant light (diya, a source of light) and the moon a reflected light (nur). He determined phases for the moon so that you might know the number of years and the calculation of time. He created these in truth; it is not in vain. In the alternation of night and day, and in all that is created in the heavens and the earth, there are indeed many signs for a people who are mindful of Allah. These signs point to Allah's existence, oneness, and power.

The word haqq is used in various meanings, such as the correspondence of thought to reality, and the conformity of word and deed to purpose. Allah Almighty, through His name 'al-Haqq,' is the supreme Being worthy of His own Essence, Whose existence is necessary, and Who is free from every deficiency. Everything other than Him cannot exist on its own; rather, they exist only through Allah's creation and for Him, and in this respect they are termed 'haqq li-ghayrihi' (true/real through another). It is stated that the heavens, the earth, and what is between them were created in truth and according to a specified term.

In the alternation of night and day and in everything created in the heavens and the earth, there are many signs for a people who fear disobeying Allah. Divine signs are understood by those endowed with knowledge, and these guide a person to reflect upon the reckoning of the Hereafter and to observe truth and justice. Allah explains His verses in detail for a people who know.

The destination of those who do not expect to meet Allah, who are pleased with the life of this world and content with it, and who are heedless of Our verses, is Hellfire on account of what they used to earn. As for those who believe and perform righteous deeds, their Lord guides them by virtue of their faith, and rivers flow beneath them in the Gardens of Delight (Jannat an-Na'im). Their supplication therein will be glorification (tasbih), their greeting will be peace (salam), and the end of their prayer will be: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

If Allah were to hasten the evil for people as they wish the good to be hastened, He would have brought their appointed term upon them immediately. But He leaves those who do not expect to meet Him wandering blindly in their transgression. When adversity touches a person, he supplicates Allah in every posture; yet when the adversity is removed, he behaves as if he had never supplicated Him. Earlier generations were also destroyed because they opposed their prophets; and you have been made successors after them so that it may be seen how you will act.

When the verses were recited, those who did not expect to meet Allah said, 'Bring a Quran other than this, or change it.' The Prophet declared that he could not change it of his own accord, but only followed what was revealed to him. Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses? Mankind was originally a single community, but then they fell into dispute; had a decree from your Lord not preceded, judgment would already have been passed between them. They demand a miracle; say, 'The unseen belongs only to Allah.'

Allah is the One Who enables you to travel on land and sea. When you are in ships, sailing along with a favorable breeze and rejoicing in it, a violent storm suddenly strikes, waves surround them from every side, and they think they are doomed. Then they cry out to Allah in complete sincerity, saying, "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful." Yet when Allah saves them, they commit injustice upon the earth. O people! Your insolence is only against yourselves. Enjoy the fleeting pleasure of worldly life; then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.

When Our verses are recited to them, those who dislike the truth say, "Bring a Quran other than this, or change it." This is because they wish to alter the verses they dislike. Say to the Prophet: "It is not for me to change it of my own accord; I follow only what is revealed to me. If I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of a tremendous Day."

If they say, "This is your own word," say: "Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I lived among you for a lifetime before this; I was entirely illiterate and composed no poetry. Will you not use your reason?" This is clear proof that the Quran is a revelation.

Who could be more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses? The criminals will never prosper. They worship idols that can neither harm nor benefit them, and say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say: "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.

Mankind was originally a single community, then they fell into dispute. Had a decree from your Lord not preceded, judgment would have been rendered among them immediately regarding that over which they differed. Those who do not expect to meet Allah say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "The unseen belongs only to Allah. So wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
When We let people taste mercy after adversity has afflicted them, they immediately plot against Our verses. Say: "Allah is swifter in scheming." Indeed, Our messengers are recording what you devise.

Allah is the One Who enables you to travel on land and sea, gives you mobility, and removes obstacles. While sailing in ships with a pleasant wind, suddenly a storm arrives and waves encompass you. It is then that you forget what you previously worshipped and plead only with Allah, promising that if He delivers you, you will certainly be among the grateful. This is an example of man turning to Allah in times of distress.

Yet when Allah delivers you from that distress, you immediately begin to commit injustice upon the earth. You forget your promise, transgress, and rebel. However, this insolence of yours harms only yourselves; you enjoy a temporary benefit in the world, then your return is to Us, and We will inform you of what you used to do.

The likeness of the life of this world is like this: We send down rain from the sky, with which the plants grow and the earth is adorned. While people think they have full power over it, Our command comes suddenly by night or by day, and We devastate it as if nothing had existed there yesterday. Thus do We explain the verses for a people who reflect.

Allah calls to the home of peace (Paradise) and guides whom He wills to a straight path. For those who do good is the best reward and even more; neither gloom nor humiliation will cover their faces. They are the people of Paradise, abiding therein eternally. As for those who earn evil deeds, they are recompensed with the like thereof, and humiliation covers them; their faces become like a dark night. They are the people of Hell, abiding therein eternally.

On that Day, We will gather the polytheists and those they associated with Allah. We will separate them, and their partner-gods will say, "You did not worship us; we were unaware of your worship." Right there, everyone will face what they did, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master (Mawla), and whatever they used to invent will vanish from them.

Say to them: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Who created and controls your senses of hearing and sight? Who brings out the living from the dead, and the dead from the living? Who regulates all affairs? They will say, "Allah." Will you not then fear Allah? That is Allah, your true Lord. So what is there after truth except error? How then are you turned away from the truth?

The word of your Lord has come true against the transgressors who strayed from the true religion: they will never believe. Say: Is there among your associate-gods any who originates creation and then reproduces it? Allah originates creation and then reproduces it. How then are you turned away? Who guides to the right path? Allah guides to the truth. Is, then, He who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed, or he who cannot find the way unless guided? Most of them follow nothing but conjecture, and conjecture can never take the place of truth in any way. Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what they do.

Regarding the question of creation, people of understanding must grasp this reality: it is impossible for contingent beings to create one another in an infinite chain. For every created thing requires a preceding cause to exist. One must find a power that breaks this chain and serves as the First Cause, which can only be Allah, who exists by His own Essence and has no need of anything. For this reason, searching for the first creator among created beings is futile. Allah originates creation from the very beginning and then reproduces it. He brings out the living from the dead and the dead from the living; He brings into being brand-new creations that transcend the laws of nature. In the face of this reality, falling into polytheism (shirk) is plain astraying.

The situation is the same regarding knowledge and discernment (marifah): no being other than Allah can independently guide to the truth. Reason and the senses are not creators of knowledge, but merely its perceivers. The harmony between subject and object is only possible through the guidance of Allah, who is above all things. In the history of philosophy, this issue has taken shape around three main views: those who argue for the impossibility of knowledge like the Sophists; those who absolutize reason like the idealists; and those who reduce everything to matter like the materialists. All of them failed to escape contradiction. The true judgment, however, is realized only through the guidance of Allah.

While these proofs are evident, most of the polytheists turn away from the truth and follow nothing but conjecture. Yet conjecture can never take the place of truth. Allah knows all that they do and will punish them. The proofs of existence and knowledge are clear demonstrations of Allah's knowledge and power.

And this Quran could not possibly be fabricated by anyone besides Allah. It confirms the scriptures before it and explains everything in detail. There is no doubt about it. If the polytheists say, "The Prophet fabricated it," challenge them: "Then bring forth a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah for help." They cannot do this, because this Book is divine speech.

They denied the Quran, whose knowledge they could not encompass and whose interpretation (ta'wil) had not yet reached them. Those before them did the same, and terrible was their end. Some of them will believe, and some will not believe. Your Lord knows best the corruptors. If they deny you, say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. What you do cannot harm me, and what I do cannot benefit you."

Among them are those who listen to you, but can you make the deaf hear? And among them are those who look at you, but can you guide the blind? Allah does not wrong people in the least; rather, people wrong themselves. On the Day when Allah gathers them, it will be as if they had remained in the world for only a very short time. Those who denied meeting Allah will suffer the greatest loss.

Every community has a messenger. When their messenger comes, judgment is delivered between them with justice. They seek to hasten the punishment. Say: "If His punishment should come to you by night or by day, what would you say?" Will you believe only after the punishment has fallen? By then, it will be too late. Then it will be said to the wrongdoers: "Taste the eternal punishment!" This is the recompense for what you used to earn.

The polytheists were asking our Prophet (peace be upon him) whether the punishment was real. Allah Almighty commands him to say that, by my Lord, the punishment is an absolute truth and none of them will be able to escape it. On that Day, everyone who did wrong, upon seeing the punishment, would want to ransom all that is on earth if they owned it, and they will feel remorse deep inside. Yet judgment will be delivered between them with justice, and none will be wronged. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah. His promise will surely come to pass, but most people do not know. He is the One who gives life and causes death, and to Him everyone will be returned.

Allah Almighty has sent down the Quran to humanity as an admonition, a healing for the hearts, and a guidance and mercy for the believers. Our Prophet is commanded to tell them to rejoice in Allah's grace and mercy, for this is better than all that they amass. The polytheists were determining lawful and unlawful from the provisions Allah sent down according to their own whims. Yet they had no permission from Allah in this regard, and indeed they were fabricating lies against Allah. Allah has bestowed immense bounty upon mankind, but most of them do not give thanks. Furthermore, whatever work a person engages in, or whatever they recite from the Quran, Allah is a witness over it. Not even an atom's weight on earth or in heaven escapes your Lord; all is recorded in a clear book.

For the friends of Allah (awliya Allah), there is no fear, nor shall they grieve. They are those who believe and remain conscious of Allah and guard against evil (ittaqaw). For them are glad tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah, and that is the supreme triumph. The miraculous gifts (karamat) of the friends of Allah are true; they are people who love one another for the sake of Allah and remind others of Allah when seen. They demonstrate their love through worship and obedience to Allah, and Allah demonstrates His friendship to them through miraculous gifts. In these verses, the definition of the friends of Allah is given, and it is emphasized that they are free from fear and sorrow.

The words of the polytheists should not grieve the Prophet (peace be upon him); for all honor belongs to Allah. He hears and sees all things. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth belongs to Allah. Those who worship others besides Allah do not truly follow their associate-gods; they follow only conjecture and they do nothing but lie. Allah created the night for rest and the day for seeing and working. In this, there are lessons for a people who listen. The polytheists ascribed offspring to Allah; He is exalted above this and is free of all need. They have no proof for this. Those who invent falsehood against Allah cannot attain salvation; their worldly pleasures will quickly end, then their return is to Allah, and they will taste the severe punishment for their disbelief.

The story of Noah (Nuh) is recounted: He told his people that he relied on Allah, that they and their associates could do whatever was in their power without giving him any respite, and stated that he asked no fee from them. When his people denied him, Noah and those with him in the ark were saved, while those who disbelieved were drowned. Afterwards, many prophets were sent with clear miracles, yet their peoples continued to deny them. Allah seals the hearts of the transgressors. Moses (Musa) and Aaron were sent to Pharaoh and his assembly, but they displayed arrogance against the truth and called it obvious magic. Moses confronted the magicians, and Allah nullified their magic. Out of fear of Pharaoh, only a small number of people believed in Moses; nevertheless, the Children of Israel were ultimately guided across the sea, and although Pharaoh professed faith as he was drowning, this faith was not accepted. His corpse was preserved as a warning for future generations.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) was told to ask those who read the scripture before him if he were in doubt concerning the revelation sent down to him; yet it was emphasized that the truth had come to him from his Lord and that he must not be among the doubters. Those who deny Allah's verses suffer loss. Those against whom the decree of their Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if all miracles were to come to them, until they see the painful punishment. However, when the people of Jonah (Yunus) believed, the humiliating punishment in worldly life was lifted from them, and they were granted comfort for a time. This is an exception showing that their faith benefited them.
Disbelievers do not believe until the punishment befalls them. However, believing once they see the punishment does not benefit them. For faith at the moment of despair is not acceptable.
The people of the prophet Jonah are the exception to this. They believed before seeing the punishment, and Allah lifted the worldly punishment from them. This shows that their faith was accepted.

If Allah had willed, He could have made everyone believe. However, compelling people to believe is not the prophet's duty. Faith occurs only by Allah's permission. And those who do not use their reason are condemned to punishment.

Looking at the signs in the heavens and the earth is useless for those who do not believe. They await disasters similar to those that befell earlier peoples. Allah will save His prophets and the believers.

The Prophet declares that he will not worship anything other than Allah and that he will remain devoted to the religion of monotheism (tawhid). Help is sought from Allah alone; none other than Him can cause either benefit or harm. Allah bestows mercy upon whomever He wills.

The truth has come to humanity. Whoever chooses the right path does so for his own good, and whoever goes astray does so to his own loss. The Prophet is not a guardian over them. Obeying the revelation and being patient have been commanded.

The letters 'Alif-Lam-Ra' at the beginning of Surah Hud, just like those at the beginning of other surahs in the Mushaf, point to the miraculous nature of the Quran. This surah is a book whose verses have been made decisive (muhkam) and clearly differentiated (mufassal). Muhkam means protected from corruption, sound, and full of wisdom; mufassal means explained, divided into sections, and detailed. These two qualities complement each other: the Quran is both utterly sound and explains every matter in detail.

In the first section of the verses, people are commanded to worship Allah alone and not to recognize any deity other than Him. Our Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent as a warner and a bearer of glad tidings. People are asked to seek forgiveness from their Lord and to turn to Him in repentance. Repentance (tawbah) and seeking forgiveness (istighfar) serve as a means for the pardon of sins and enable a person to lead a good life. Allah promises that He will grant a great reward to those who believe and perform righteous deeds.

Following this call to seeking forgiveness and repentance, glad tidings are given that those of virtue will be given the reward of their virtue. Virtue is not merely fulfilling obligatory duties (fard), but also drawing closer to Allah through supererogatory acts of worship (nafilah) and being beneficial to people. An increase in the number of those who repent in society contributes to the spread of a sense of virtue; thus, there is also a reward in this world, but the true reward is in the Hereafter.

If people turn away, the Prophet fears for them the punishment of a tremendous day. That tremendous day is the Day of Resurrection. The return of everyone is to Allah; whether they repent or not, they will ultimately arrive in Allah's presence. In the verse, the disbelievers' attempts to hide from Allah are described through figurative language; they fold up their chests and wrap themselves in their cloaks. Allah, however, knows all that is hidden in the breasts.

Allah declares that none other than Him provides sustenance for any living creature on earth. He knows both the dwelling places and the resting places of every creature. He created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water. The wisdom behind this creation is to test people and make manifest which of them will perform the best deeds. The disbelievers do not accept resurrection after death and describe it as plain magic.

When man tastes mercy from Allah and then loses it, he becomes despairing and ungrateful; and when he attains blessing after adversity, he grows boastful. But those who are patient and do righteous deeds are an exception; for them there is forgiveness and a great reward. Our Prophet should not be gripped by anxiety to leave aside a part of the revelation in the face of the polytheists' objections; he is only a warner. The polytheists claim that the Quran is fabricated. A challenge is issued to them: Come then, produce ten surahs like it, and call upon whomever you can call upon for help besides Allah. If they cannot accomplish this, know that the Quran was sent down with Allah's knowledge and that there is no deity except Him; it is now necessary to become Muslims.

The recompense of those who desire the worldly life and its splendor is given to them fully in this world according to their deeds; however, in the Hereafter nothing awaits them except the Fire. What they have done goes to waste and is worthless. For the worldly life is transient, and every deed not performed purely for Allah remains fruitless.

In contrast, those who stand upon a clear proof from their Lord, with this proof being supported by the witness of the Quran and earlier scriptures (such as the scripture of Moses [Musa]), cannot be considered equal to those deniers. These people believe in the Quran; as for those who deny it, their place is the Fire. This book is the truth, yet most people do not believe.

Human beings, when granted a blessing, fail to give thanks and become ungrateful; when that blessing is taken away, they fall into despair. And when they attain a blessing after adversity, they become boastful and arrogant. However, those who are patient and do righteous deeds are different from this; for them there is forgiveness and a great reward.

Our Prophet is commanded not to pay heed to the mockeries of the deniers or their words such as, 'Why has not a treasure been sent down to him, or an angel come with him?' but rather to convey what has been revealed to him. A challenge is also issued to those who claim that he fabricated the Quran: Come then, produce ten surahs, and call upon your helpers besides Allah. If they cannot do this, know that the Quran was sent down with Allah's knowledge and that there is no deity except Him.

The narrative of Noah begins: Noah is sent to his people as a clear warner. The notables of his people accuse him of lying and say that only the lowest rabble have followed him. Noah states that he stands upon a clear proof, asks no wealth from them, and will not drive away those who believe. His people, on the other hand, demand that he bring the punishment upon them.

Noah says that only Allah will bring the punishment and that his advice will be of no benefit if Allah desires to destroy them. It is revealed to Noah that none of his people will believe any longer; thereupon he begins to build the ark. His people mock him, and he tells them that he will respond to them in like manner.

When the command arrived and the 'tannur' (oven) began to boil over, Noah was commanded to load onto the ark a pair from every species and those who believed (along with his family). The ark sails and anchors in the name of Allah. Amid waves like mountains, Noah's son seeks refuge on a mountain, but he drowns. This shows that there is no escape from Allah's decree.

The Flood ends, and the ark comes to rest on Mount Judi. Noah pleads with Allah for the salvation of his son, but Allah informs him that because his son is not of righteous conduct, he is not considered part of his family. Noah repents and is forgiven. Then, after peace and blessings are invoked upon Noah and those with him, it is foretold that in the future certain nations will be granted enjoyment and then be subjected to punishment.

In the tafsir, the word 'tannur' is examined: most commentators agree that it refers to an actual hearth (oven), while some give it metaphorical meanings such as the surface of the earth, the break of dawn, or the intensification of the affair. According to one view, the tannur is the place on the ship where water collects (the boiler). These differing interpretations demonstrate the richness of the miraculous event described in the verse.

According to the narrations of tafsir scholars, it is understood that Noah's ark was a steamship. The word tannur means both a hearth and relates to the boiler where water gathers on a ship. The expression 'at-tannur' indicates that this was an oven belonging to the ship. In the verse, the boiling over of the tannur signifies the completion of the ship's construction and the commencement of the order to set in motion. In modern terms, this means 'when the ship is fired up.' There is no need to abandon the apparent (zahir) meaning of the verse and resort to allegorical interpretation (ta'wil). The completion of the ship's construction and its reaching full steam is a sign that the Flood is about to begin. Noah built the ship under Allah's revelation and supervision. Two pairs from every living creature were taken aboard; it is understood that a vessel bearing such a massive load was not a simple sailboat, but a miraculous ship.

In the 43rd verse, it is declared that there is no one who can protect from Allah's decree. From this, it is understood that the Flood was not regional, but universal. However, this universality covers the inhabited parts of the earth; it does not encompass the poles. The supplication in Surah Nuh also supports this. Whether Noah (peace be upon him) was sent to all humanity or only to his own people is a matter of disagreement. It is certain that the Flood was comprehensive in the region where Noah's people lived; anything beyond that is conjecture.

In verses 44–47, with the command for the earth to swallow its water and for the sky to withhold its rain, the waters recede, and the decree of punishment is fulfilled. The ark comes to rest on Mount Judi. Judi is a mountain in Mosul, al-Jazirah, or Amid. The wrongdoing people are destroyed.

In verse 48, addressing Noah, it is conveyed that he should disembark in peace and blessings, and that many nations will arise from those who are with him. This indicates that nations would also descend from the few believers who were with Noah. The view that humanity after the Deluge descended exclusively from Noah's three sons is not absolute. The other believers who were with Noah were also granted blessings.

Verses 50–60 recount the story of the prophet Hud, who was sent to the people of 'Ad. Hud calls his people to worship Allah, asks for no reward, and promises blessings through repentance and seeking forgiveness. Stating that he brought no miracle, his people refuse to abandon their idols and slander Hud. Hud declares that he puts his trust in Allah, and that the forelock of every living creature is in His grasp. He tells them that if they turn away, Allah will replace them with another people. When the punishment arrives, Hud and the believers are saved, and the people of 'Ad are cursed. This punishment was 'rih-i sarsar' (a fierce, roaring windstorm), which destroyed the disbelievers. Some commentators have stated that this salvation was from the punishment of both this world and the Hereafter.

Verses 61–68 relate the story of the prophet Salih, who was sent to the people of Thamud. Salih calls his people to worship Allah and reminds them that it is He Who created them from the earth. His people accuse Salih—in whom they had previously placed their hopes—of now barring them from the religion of their forefathers, and they state that they are in grave doubt about his call. Salih asks them to leave the she-camel, which is a miracle from Allah; he warns them that if they slaughter her, punishment will come upon them within three days. They slaughter the camel and are destroyed by an awful blast. Salih and the believers are saved.

Verses 69–80 turn to the story of Lot. The angels come to Abraham with glad tidings, and they greet each other with peace. Abraham serves them a roasted calf; seeing that they do not eat, he feels fear. The angels explain that they have been sent to the people of Lot, and Abraham's wife is given the glad tidings of Isaac and Jacob. Abraham pleads with the angels concerning the people of Lot; the angels inform him that the command of your Lord is final. When the angels arrive at Lot's home, Lot is deeply distressed; his people come rushing and make their wicked intentions known. Lot offers his daughters, but the people refuse. Lot wishes he had strength or could take refuge in a strong support.

The angels said to Lot, "We are the messengers of your Lord; they cannot harm you. Depart with your family in the night; your wife shall remain behind, for the punishment will strike her as well. The appointed time of their destruction is the morning." When Our command came, We turned that land upside down and rained upon them stones of layered baked clay. These stones were marked in the presence of your Lord, and they are not far from the wrongdoers. In recounting this story, the arrival of the angels to Abraham is narrated first; they had been sent to the people of Lot and had brought Abraham the glad tidings of a son.

And to Midian We sent their brother Shu'ayb. Shu'ayb said: "O my people! Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Do not give short measure and weight. I see you in prosperity, but I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing day." "O my people! Give full measure and weight in justice, do not defraud people of their possessions, and do not cause corruption in the earth. What Allah leaves for you of lawful gain is better for you, if you are believers."

His people said: "O Shu'ayb! Does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our forefathers worshipped or cease doing what we please with our wealth? Yet you are indeed a clement and sensible man." Shu'ayb said: "O my people! Have you considered? If I stand upon a clear proof from my Lord and He has granted me a good provision from Himself, what should I do? I do not wish to fall into the very things I forbid you from. I only desire reform to the best of my ability. And my success is only through Allah. Let not your opposition to me cause you to suffer disasters like those that befell the people of Noah, Hud, or Salih. And the people of Lot are not far off from you. Ask forgiveness of your Lord, and turn to Him in repentance. Truly, my Lord is Most Merciful, Most Loving."

His people said: "O Shu'ayb! We do not understand much of what you say. And we see you as weak among us. Were it not for your family, we would certainly have stoned you. You hold no superiority over us." Shu'ayb said: "O my people! Is my family more esteemed to you than Allah? You have cast Allah behind your backs. My Lord encompasses all that you do. Act according to your ability; I, too, am acting. You will come to know upon whom a humiliating punishment will fall, and who is a liar. Wait, then; I too am waiting with you." When Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and the believers by Our mercy; an awful blast seized the wrongdoers, and they lay fallen lifeless in their homes, as though they had never lived there. Midian was destroyed just as Thamud had been destroyed.

And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority to Pharaoh and his assembly. But they followed the command of Pharaoh, though the command of Pharaoh was not right-guided. On the Day of Resurrection, he will precede his people and lead them into the Fire. How wretched is the place to which they are led! They were pursued by a curse both in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. How wretched is the support given to them!

According to the tafsir of Abu Hayyan, Pharaoh was a materialist (dahri) who denied the Creator and the Hereafter. He claimed that there was no deity of the universe, and that the people of each realm owed obedience solely to their own ruler. For this reason, Pharaoh's command was far from mature judgment. As stated in Surah an-Nazi'at, he would say, "I am your most exalted lord," and did not acknowledge the existence of any Lord superior to himself. He gave no thought to whether the orders he issued were right, ruling solely according to his own whims. He considered himself the absolute authority, and his council and people complied with him. It is precisely such commands that disregard the sovereignty of the Truth that are termed "the command of Pharaoh." It is evident that such commands cannot be sound (rashid), for the laws governing the universe do not change by the will of an individual. Pharaoh did not deem it necessary to submit to the Truth; he attempted to establish right and law through his own dictate, and ultimately burned both himself and his partisans.

On the Day of Resurrection, Pharaoh will precede his people and lead them into the Fire. What they approach as if it were water is actually fire; what an evil arrival place that is! The outcome of Pharaoh's command is a devastating end. Those who followed him were made wretched for adhering to a command with such a dreadful conclusion. Moreover, both in this world and on the Day of Resurrection, they were made to be followed by a curse—that is, remembered with condemnation. This curse is sardonically depicted by likening it to an assigned gift or support (rifd).

These are significant parts of the accounts of those destroyed towns being related to you. Some of their remnants still stand, while others have been mown down and completely eradicated. Allah did not wrong them; rather, they wronged themselves. The deities they invoked besides Allah availed them nothing when the command of your Lord came; instead, they only increased their destruction and loss. When your Lord seizes the towns while they are doing wrong, His seizure is indeed painful and severe. In this there is surely a lesson for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a day on which all mankind will be gathered, and it is a day that will surely be witnessed. We delay it only for an appointed term.

When that day arrives, no soul shall speak except by His leave. Among them will be the wretched and the blessed. As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire; in it, they will be in zafir and shahiq (agonized sighing and wailing). They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Truly, your Lord is the Doer of whatever He intends. As for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. This is a bestowal uninterrupted.

So do not fall into doubt regarding what these polytheists worship. They worship only as their ancestors worshipped before them. And We shall indeed pay them their share in full, without any decrease. We certainly gave Moses (Musa) the Scripture, but disputes arose over it. And had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord, judgment would have already been passed concerning them. They are in disquieting doubt regarding it. Your Lord will surely pay each of them in full for their deeds. He is fully aware of all that they do.

Therefore, stand firm as you have been commanded! And let those who have repented along with you stand firm as well. Do not transgress; Allah sees everything you do. Do not lean toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you. You have no protectors besides Allah. Establish prayer at both ends of the day and during the fringes of the night. Good deeds drive away evil deeds. This is an admonition for those who reflect. Be patient; Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.

In this section, it is emphasized that Allah will fully recompense everyone for their deeds. In particular, it is stated that those who desire the life of this world and its adornment will receive their recompense in this world, but in the Hereafter they will find nothing but the Fire. Then, the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers who follow him are commanded to be steadfast as they were commanded. According to the narration of Ibn Abbas, this command is the heaviest verse in the Qur'an; our Prophet also stated, 'Surah Hud has made me grow old.' Attention is drawn to the difficulty and importance of being upon the straight path (istiqamah); the ummah is likewise asked not to depart from this uprightness.

Leaning toward those who act unjustly and supporting them is strictly forbidden. Believers must not appease the oppressors or form friendships with them; otherwise, they will be subjected to the Fire and will have no helpers besides Allah. This command emphasizes that believers must maintain an uncompromising stance in the face of every kind of injustice.

Performing prayer in five daily times is commanded. The expression 'the two ends of the day' is interpreted as the noon and afternoon prayers, while the expression 'the fringes (portions) of the night' is interpreted as the evening, night, and dawn prayers. This verse explains the times and virtues of the prayers; it is stated that good deeds remove evil deeds, and that prayer restrains a person from shameful acts. Moreover, prayer is an admonition and a reminder for those who reflect.

Patience is advised to the believers; it is recalled that Allah will not let the reward of the doers of good be lost. The reasons for the destruction of past nations are summarized: they perished because there was no virtuous group among them to prevent corruption, and because they plunged into luxury and pursued pleasure. Allah does not destroy a land unjustly while its people are righteous and reform-minded.

Had Allah willed, He would have made all people a single community, yet they were destined to continue differing. Those who are favored with mercy are an exception; they do not fall into dispute. Allah created humans for a test and informed that He will fill Hell with jinn and humans alike. This is a manifestation of Allah's justice.

The surah concludes by stating that the stories of the prophets are related in order to bring solace to the heart, and that truth and an admonition have arrived in this surah. The disbelievers are told to do whatever is in their power and wait; the believers are waiting as well. The unseen of the heavens and the earth belongs solely to Allah; every matter is returned to Him. For this reason, worship should be devoted to Him alone and reliance placed upon Him alone. Allah is never heedless of anything that is done.

Surah Yusuf begins with the letters Alif, Lam, Ra. These letters are the verses of the clear book. The word 'mubin' means that which is clear and distinct in its own essence, while at the same time clarifying to others. In this respect, the Quran is a book that clarifies everything.

There are four aspects to the Quran being 'mubin'. The first is that it is a miracle; no human or jinn has been able to produce the like of it. The second is that it explains the fundamentals and principles of religion, rulings, news of the unseen, and stories. The third is that it distinguishes truth from falsehood. The fourth is the beauty of its language and expression; it was revealed in the most eloquent dialect of Arabic, leaving men of letters powerless before its composition.

This surah, which comes after Surahs Yunus and Hud, emphasizes the clarificatory quality of the Quran. Allah states that He revealed the Quran in Arabic. This means that not only its meaning, but also its wording is in Arabic, so that people of understanding may comprehend it.

This surah narrates the best of stories: the story of Joseph (Yusuf). Allah informed our Prophet of this story through revelation; prior to this, he had no knowledge of it. This is proof that it came from Allah. The expression 'ahsan al-qasas' means both the best of stories and the finest manner of narration.

Joseph saw in his dream eleven stars, the sun, and the moon prostrating to him. His father, Jacob (Ya'qub), told him not to recount this dream to his brothers, lest they plot against him out of jealousy. Furthermore, he gave glad tidings that Allah would choose Joseph, teach him the interpretation of dreams, and bless him and the family of Jacob with prophethood.

His brothers were jealous because they found Joseph and his full brother Benjamin more beloved to their father than themselves. First they planned to kill him, then to cast him into a well. One of them suggested that he be thrown into a well so that a caravan might find him and take him away. They asked their father for permission to let Joseph go with them to play.

Jacob warned them of his fear of a wolf, but his brothers insisted. In the end, they took Joseph away and cast him into the well. Allah revealed to Joseph that he would eventually inform them of what they had done. His brothers returned to their father weeping, claiming that a wolf had eaten Joseph, and showed the shirt stained with false blood. Jacob took refuge in Allah with beautiful patience.

A caravan arrived and lowered their bucket into the well; they found Joseph, drew him out, and sold him for a few dirhams. An Egyptian minister (the Aziz) bought him and told his wife to take good care of him, thinking they might adopt him as a son. Allah established Joseph in Egypt and taught him the interpretation of dreams.

When Joseph reached the age of maturity, Allah granted him judgment and knowledge. Thus are the doers of good rewarded. Then, the lady in whose house he resided (Zulaikha) sought to seduce him; she locked the doors and invited him to herself. Joseph refused, taking refuge in Allah and stating that his master had treated him well and that wrongdoers would never prosper. She had truly resolved upon it, and Joseph would have inclined toward her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Allah turned indecency and evil away from him, for he was among the chosen servants endowed with sincerity. Here the concepts of 'mukhlas' and 'mukhlis' are explained; the former refers to one chosen by Allah, while the latter refers to a sincere servant.

Both raced to the door, and the woman tore his shirt from behind. When they encountered her husband at the door, the woman accused Joseph and demanded punishment. Joseph, however, said that it was she who had sought to seduce him. A member of the woman's household bore witness that if the shirt was torn from the front, the woman was truthful, but if it was torn from the back, Joseph was truthful. When it was seen that the shirt was torn from the back, the husband said that this was the plot of women; he told Joseph not to mention this matter and commanded the woman to seek forgiveness for her sin.

When the women in the city spread gossip, the wife of the Aziz invited them, prepared a lavish banquet, gave each of them a knife, and had Joseph come out before them. When the women saw him, they cut their hands and exclaimed, 'This is an angel!' The woman said, 'This is he about whom you blamed me; I sought to seduce him, but he remained chaste. If he does not do what I command him, he will be thrown into prison and will be among the disgraced.' Joseph prayed to Allah, stating that prison was dearer to him than that to which the women invited him, and asked to be protected from their snare. Allah answered his prayer. Nonetheless, the thought of imprisoning Joseph for a time prevailed.

Two young men also entered the prison. One of them dreamed that he was pressing wine, while the other dreamed that he was carrying bread on his head from which birds were eating. Joseph told them that he would inform them of the interpretation before their food arrived. First, he called them to believe in Allah and to abandon the religion of a people who deny the Hereafter. Then, he informed them that one would serve wine to his master, while the other would be crucified and birds would eat from his head. To the one he believed would be saved, he said, 'Mention me to your master.' However, Satan caused him to forget this, and Joseph remained in prison for years. Some commentators have noted that Joseph should have asked of Allah rather than relying on a mortal servant.

One day, the king recounted his dream in which seven lean cows were devouring seven fat cows, and he saw seven green ears of grain and seven dry ones. The notables said, 'These are confused dreams; we do not know their interpretation.' Here, Elmalılı explains at length the difference between ru'ya (a true dream) and hulum (a confused dream). While ru'ya carries a genuine and interpretable meaning, hulum consists merely of meaningless delusions. A dream can be a divine inspiration coming from Allah or brought by an angel. Islamic scholars divide dreams into three categories: divine inspiration, psychological imaginations, and satanic suggestions. In a hadith of the Prophet (peace be upon him), a dream is mentioned as one of the forty-six parts of prophethood.

Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır dwells upon the nature of dreams. According to him, a dream is an unveiling (kashfi) phenomenon, distinct from the mere association of ordinary memories. Whether in sleep or while awake, they are truths reflected onto the soul from the world of forms (alam al-mithal). The interpretation of dreams, on the other hand, is a scholarly, divinely bestowed, and intuitive knowledge; it cannot be resolved by formal logic. For this reason, distinguishing a true dream from ahlam (confused dreams) is difficult. In fact, those who are heedless of the secrets of the unseen consider all dreams to be ahlam. Pharaoh's counselors, too, in their ignorance, had said, 'We do not know the interpretation of ahlam.'

The cupbearer who was released from prison remembered Joseph after a long time and went to the prison to learn the interpretation of the king's dream. Joseph interpreted the dream of seven lean cows devouring seven fat cows and seven green ears of grain and seven dry ones: they would cultivate abundantly for seven years and leave what they reaped in its ear; then seven years of drought would follow, consuming what they had stored; thereafter would come a rainy year in which the people would find relief from distress.

When the king heard this interpretation, he ordered that Joseph be brought to him. However, when the messenger arrived, Joseph asked him to return to his master before he left prison and inquire what the intention of the women who cut their hands was. The king questioned the women; they all stated that they knew no evil of Joseph. The wife of the Aziz confessed, saying, 'Now the truth has come to light; it was I who sought to seduce him, and he is indeed of the truthful.' The woman added that she did not betray Joseph behind his back and did not absolve her own soul, for the soul surely enjoins evil, except for those upon whom her Lord has mercy.

The ruler summoned Joseph (Yusuf), wishing to make him his special advisor. When he spoke with him, he said, "Today, you are in our presence established in position and trusted." Joseph requested a post, saying, "Place me over the storehouses of this land; for I am indeed a skilled keeper and knowledgeable." Elmalılı notes here that the "Aziz" and the "King (Malik)" were different individuals; that the King was a ruler worthy of praise and did not use the title of Pharaoh.

Allah established Joseph in Egypt; he settled wherever he wished within it. This was a manifestation of divine mercy. The reward of those who do good is not lost, and the reward of the Hereafter is even better. During the years of famine, Joseph's brothers came to Egypt. Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him. While having their provisions prepared, he said, "Bring me your other brother from your father; if you do not bring him to me, there will be no grain for you." The brothers said that they would try to obtain permission from their father. Joseph commanded his servants to put his brothers' capital into their saddlebags so that they might return again.

Upon their first arrival in Egypt, Joseph recognized his brothers, yet they did not recognize him. Joseph asked them about their family, and they stated that in addition to their father Jacob (Ya'qub), they had another brother in place of the one who had died. Thereupon, Joseph meant Benjamin (Binyamin) when he said, "Bring me your other brother from your father." He treated them generously, saying, "I give full measure and I am the best of hosts," but he told them that if they did not bring their brother, it would not be possible for them to obtain grain again. In response to this persistent demand, the brothers stated that they would try to persuade their father.

As Joseph saw his brothers off, he instructed his servants to secretly place the price they had paid inside their saddlebags. He did this so that they would rejoice upon their return and be eager to come back. This precaution was to assist them in persuading their father to bring Benjamin.

When the brothers returned to their father Jacob, they said, "O our father! Measure has been denied to us, so send our brother with us that we may obtain grain. We will certainly guard him." Jacob expressed his distrust of them, saying, "Can I entrust him to you except as I entrusted his brother before?" However, when they opened their baggage and saw that their capital had been returned to them, they tried to persuade their father by explaining this situation to him.

Jacob consented to send Benjamin only after taking a firm oath from them. He said to his sons, "Give me an oath by Allah that you will bring him back to me unless you are completely overwhelmed." They gave their oath. In addition, he advised them to enter through separate gates upon entering Egypt; the reason for this was to avoid drawing attention and being envied as a group. However, he also emphasized that this precaution could not avert the decree of Allah.

When the brothers arrived in Egypt, they entered before Joseph. Joseph took Benjamin to himself, introduced himself, and said, "I am your brother, so do not grieve over what they have been doing." According to a narration, Joseph told him what his brothers had done to him in the past and instructed him not to be deceived this time. Then, formulating a plan, he had the drinking cup placed into Benjamin's saddlebag.

After the caravan set out, a crier called out: "O caravan! You are indeed thieves!" The brothers turned back and asked, "What are you looking for?" The officials replied, "We are looking for the King's drinking cup, and whoever brings it shall have a camel-load of grain." The brothers rejected the accusation, saying, "By Allah, we are not thieves, nor did we come to cause corruption." When the officials asked, "What shall be the penalty if you are found to be liars?", they answered, "The penalty is that he in whose bag it is found shall himself be the penalty."

A search was conducted, and the drinking cup was brought out from Benjamin's bag. In this way, Joseph retained his brother with him. The brothers made an insinuation against Joseph, saying, "If he stole, a brother of his stole before him." Joseph said within himself, "You are in a far worse position, and Allah knows best what you assert." Thereupon, the brothers pleaded with Joseph to consider their elderly father and retain one of them in his place, but Joseph did not accept.

This action of Joseph was intended to lead his brothers to regret their past mistakes and to repent. Moreover, it was to help them fulfill the oath they had made to their father. All these measures took place with the revelation and permission of Allah. No precaution can avert the decree of Allah; Jacob's advice in this regard also demonstrates the balance between taking precautions (tadbir) and trusting in Allah (tawakkul).

When asked what the punishment would be for the person who stole Joseph's drinking cup, the brothers stated that the thief himself would be seized and taken as property. This was the punishment for theft in the religious law (sharia) of the Prophet Jacob: the thief would serve the owner of the stolen property for a period of one year. By prompting them to issue this legal verdict (fatwa), Joseph secured the right to retain his brother Benjamin.

Joseph began the search with the bags of the other brothers first, and then took out the drinking cup from Benjamin's bag. There is an important point here: the object that emerged from the bag was not the King's drinking cup, but Joseph's own bowl. If it had been the King's cup, Joseph would have had to act according to Egyptian law and would not have been able to retain Benjamin. However, by placing his own bowl, he detained him based on the legal verdict his brothers had given. In this way, he neither violated Egyptian law nor failed to let them be judged according to their own religion.

Faced with this situation, the brothers, feeling helpless, angrily said, "If he stole, a brother of his committed theft before him." According to one narration, Joseph had broken his grandfather's idol as a child. Joseph concealed this remark within himself, did not reveal it to them, and was patient. Then the brothers pleaded with Joseph, imploring for mercy by addressing him, "O Aziz!"

When the brothers lost hope, their eldest, Judah (Yahuda), decided to stay in Egypt and told them to return to their father. Jacob did not believe the news they brought and said, "No, your souls have enticed you to something. So patience is most fitting for me. Perhaps Allah will bring them all back to me." Then he turned away, saying, "O grief for Joseph, this is too much!" and his eyes turned white from sorrow. Although his sons attempted to console him, Jacob stated that he complained of his grief and sorrow only to Allah, and he sent them to search for Joseph and his brother.

Jacob encouraged them, saying, "Do not despair of Allah's mercy; for no one despairs of Allah's mercy except the disbelieving people." Thereupon, the brothers went to Egypt once again and entered Joseph's presence. Joseph revealed his identity to them, saying, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has indeed favored us. Whoever fears Allah and remains patient, Allah never allows the reward of those who do good to be lost." When the brothers acknowledged their mistake, Joseph forgave them and told them to take his shirt to their father.

When they met Joseph for the third time, a great softening and awakening had taken place in the brothers' hearts. This softening, which had begun with Benjamin's detention, progressively deepened and matured them. Joseph's forbearance toward them, his humility, and his sincerity also influenced them. For this reason, Joseph realized that the time had come to reveal his identity, and he asked them, "Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?" With this question, what had been promised earlier when he was cast into the well was fulfilled.

Joseph's words struck their hearts like lightning, and they immediately realized that he was Joseph. In great astonishment and excitement, they said, "Are you really Joseph?" Joseph identified himself, saying, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother," and giving thanks to Allah, he said: "Indeed, Allah has favored us. Truly, whoever fears Allah and is patient, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost." Thereupon, his brothers confessed, saying, "By Allah, Allah has indeed preferred you over us. We were truly in the wrong."

Joseph said to his brothers, "There is no reproach against you today." The word 'tathrib' (tesrib) means censuring the wrongdoer and calling them to account. Accepting their apology, Joseph stated that he hoped Allah would also forgive them. He then gave them his shirt and said, "Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face so that his sight may return." It is noted that this shirt was a counterpart to the bloodstained shirt brought earlier. It is narrated that the shirt was a miraculous heirloom inherited from Abraham (peace be upon him).

Joseph tasked his brothers with conveying the glad tidings to his father and bringing his entire family to Egypt. When the caravan departed from Egypt, Jacob said, "I sense the scent of Joseph." Those around him accused him of senility. However, when the bearer of glad tidings arrived and placed the shirt over Jacob's face, his sight returned. Jacob said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?" This event is regarded as a miracle, and although attempts are made to explain it with concepts such as telepathy, it is emphasized that it was a divine intervention.

His sons came and said, "O our father, ask forgiveness for us from Allah." Jacob, however, postponed the prayer to a specific time, saying, "I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord later." It is noted that this was to wait until Joseph's forgiveness was ascertained. Finally, when the family arrived in Egypt and came before Joseph, Joseph embraced his parents and seated them upon a high throne. They all fell down in prostration before Joseph. Joseph expressed that the dream he had seen earlier had come true, saying, "This is the fulfillment of my dream."

Giving thanks to Allah, Joseph prayed: "O my Lord! You have granted me a share of worldly dominion and taught me the interpretation of dreams. Take my soul as a Muslim, and join me with the righteous."

Joseph took his mother and father up to his high mansion. Together with his brothers, they prostrated in gratitude to Allah. This prostration was not like the one in Joseph's dream, but a prostration of gratitude to Allah. Thus, the dream was fulfilled.

Turning to his father, Joseph said, "This is the interpretation of the dream I saw earlier. My Lord rescued me from prison and brought you here from the desert. Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers, but by the grace of Allah we have reached this fine end." In order not to embarrass his brothers, he made no mention of the incident of the well.

Joseph prayed to Allah as follows: "My Lord! You have given me dominion and knowledge. You are the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Take my soul as a Muslim and join me with the righteous." When he made this supplication, his soul was taken. His body was placed in a marble coffin and buried in the Nile River. Later, the rule changed in Egypt, and the Children of Israel became captives of the Pharaohs.

Allah informed Muhammad of these accounts of the unseen through revelation. He was not with Joseph's brothers. However much you may desire it, most people will not believe. You ask no reward for this conveyance; this Quran is but a reminder for the worlds.

How many signs there are in the heavens and the earth that people encounter, yet they turn away from them! Most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating partners with Him. Or do they feel secure from Allah's punishment or the Hour that comes upon them suddenly? The way of the Prophet is to invite to Allah upon clear sight; he is not of the polytheists.

The messengers before you were also men from among the people of the cities, to whom revelation was given. Have they not traveled through the earth and seen the end of those who came before them? The home of the Hereafter is far better for those mindful of Allah. When the messengers despaired, Our help came to them; those whom We willed were saved. Nor can Our punishment be averted from the criminal people.

There is certainly a lesson in their stories for people of deep understanding. This Quran is not an invented discourse; it confirms the scriptures before it and explains everything in detail. It is guidance and mercy for a people who believe. Following this surah comes Surah ar-Ra'd, which means 'Thunder'.

The surah begins with the letters Alif, Lam, Mim, Ra. Although these letters may seem meaningless on their own, they are the fundamental elements that constitute the verses of the Quran, the Book of Allah. When brought together properly, these letters become clear proofs that manifest the meanings of the Book of truth. What has been revealed to you from Allah is entirely the truth; yet most people do not believe.

It is Allah Who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see. Then He established Himself above the Throne (istiwa) and subjected the sun and the moon. Each runs its course for an appointed term. He governs all affairs and explains the verses in detail so that you may believe with certainty in the meeting with your Lord. In explaining the raising of the heavens without pillars in this verse, Elmalılı touches upon old and new astronomical views, ultimately drawing attention to divine power. Furthermore, he emphasizes that this verse constitutes proof of Allah's existence through observation and reason.

It is He Who spread out the earth far and wide, placed therein mountains and rivers, created pairs of every kind of fruit, and draped the night over the day. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect. And on the earth are neighboring tracts of land, vineyards, crops, and date palms, all watered with the same water, yet He makes some of their fruits superior to others. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who use their intellect.

If you are astonished, what is truly astonishing is the disbelievers' saying: 'When we have become dust, will we really be created anew?' These are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord; there are iron shackles around their necks, and they are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally. They challenge you to hasten the evil before the good, even though exemplary punishments have already passed before them. Your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing, but His punishment is also severe.

The disbelievers say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs lose or increase; everything with Him is by due measure. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Most High. It is all the same whether one conceals speech or speaks openly, and whether one hides by night or walks out by day. For each person there are angels following closely before and behind him, guarding him by Allah's command. Allah does not change the blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. When Allah wills adversity for a people, there is no turning it back, and they have no protector besides Him.

Allah raised the heavens without visible pillars and spread out the earth. The terrestrial globe was detached from the sun by Allah's command, and firm mountains, rivers, and pairs of every kind of fruit were created upon it. These pairs were created as male and female, bearing fruit through pollination. Although the science of botany discovered this only later, the Quran announced this truth centuries before. This fact is clear proof that the Quran is the Word of Allah.

Adjacent tracts of land on earth possess different characteristics; some are barren, while others are fertile. Vineyards, crops, and date palms watered by the same water produce yields of different flavors. This diversity demonstrates that it does not occur through nature on its own, but by Allah's power. Those who use their intellect realize from these proofs that Allah is capable of creating anew. The deniers, on the other hand, utter what is truly astonishing by saying, 'When we have decayed and turned into dust, will we really be created anew?' Yet it is not re-creation that is astonishing, but rather denying it.

The deniers demand a verse (miracle) from the Prophet. Yet the numerous verses sent to them were already sufficient. The Prophet is merely a warner; for every people there is a guide. Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs lose or increase. Everything with Him is by due measure. It is Allah Who knows all that is hidden and manifest, and Who is greater and more exalted than all things.

For every person there are guardian angels before and behind him, protecting him by Allah's command. Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when He wills adversity for a people, there is no turning it back, and they have no protector besides Allah.

Allah shows you the lightning to inspire fear and hope, and brings forth heavy, rain-laden clouds. The thunder glorifies Him with praise, and the angels glorify Him in awe of Him. He sends thunderbolts and strikes whom He wills. True supplication is to Him alone; those invoked besides Him cannot respond to anything at all. Whoever is in the heavens and on earth prostrates to Allah, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the mornings and afternoons.

In the thirteenth verse, it is recounted that thunder and lightning glorify Allah with praise, and that the angels glorify Him in awe of His majesty. Then, the account of Arbad ibn Rabi'ah and 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl seeking to assassinate the Prophet (peace be upon him) and Allah punishing them is mentioned: 'Amir contracted the plague and died while fleeing, while Arbad perished from being struck by a thunderbolt.

In the fourteenth verse, with the expression 'To Him alone is the true supplication,' it is emphasized that praying to anyone other than Allah is futile. Idols, saints (awliya), or other beings cannot respond to any prayer on their own. Through a philosophical explanation, it is noted that beings are distinct from one another, and that one can influence another only by Allah's leave. Just as a thirsty person reaches out for water, any supplication not directed to Allah is in vain.

In the fifteenth verse, it is reported that every being in the heavens and on earth prostrates to Allah, willingly or unwillingly, and that even shadows are included in this prostration. This demonstrates that everything submits to Allah's command.

In verses 16-17, the polytheists are asked: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth? It is certainly Allah. Taking others besides Him as protectors is sheer blindness. Then a parable is given: Allah sends down water from the sky, valleys flow with torrents, and the flood carries scum on its surface. A similar scum forms when metals are melted. This scum is cast away, while what is beneficial remains. Such is truth and falsehood; even if falsehood seems apparent, it vanishes, while the truth is enduring.

In the eighteenth verse, it is conveyed that for those who respond to their Lord is the best reward (Paradise), while those who do not respond would want to offer everything on earth as ransom, yet it will not be accepted; for them awaits a terrible reckoning and Hell.

Verses 19-22 enumerate the qualities of people of understanding (ulu al-albab): they fulfill Allah's covenant, maintain the ties of kinship (silat al-rahim), fear their Lord, dread the terrible reckoning, remain patient, establish prayer, spend in charity (infaq), and repel evil with good. These are the ones who attain the good outcome of the ultimate abode.

In verses 23-24, glad tidings are given that these believers will enter the Gardens of Eden ('Adn) together with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and offspring, and that the angels will enter upon them from every gate, saying, 'Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final home!'

In the twenty-fifth verse, it is stated that upon those who break the covenant of Allah, sever what He has ordered to be joined, and spread corruption on earth, there is a curse and the wretched home (Hell). Although this verse was revealed concerning the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), its ruling is general.

In the 26th verse, it is recalled that Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it, that the disbelievers rejoice in the worldly life, whereas the worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is nothing but a brief provision for a journey.

In verses 27–29, it is stated that the disbelievers say, 'If only a sign were sent down to him from his Lord,' to which it is answered that Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him. It is emphasized that for those who believe, whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah, and who perform righteous deeds, there is a good end (Paradise).

Turning to Allah and repenting in submission is called inabah. The prerequisite of guidance is to break free from the desires of the soul and submit to the will of Allah. Every human being is granted the opportunity to choose guidance throughout their lifetime. If a person does not choose guidance during this period, misguidance becomes an inevitable habit.

In the verse, it is stated: 'They are the believers whose hearts find satisfaction with the remembrance of Allah.' Here, zikrullah (remembrance of Allah) refers to the Quran, because the Quran is Allah's clearest proclamation. Hearts find peace only through the remembrance of Allah; since everything other than Him is transient, nothing else can provide satisfaction.

The remembrance of Allah is of two degrees: the first is actual guidance created directly in the heart; the second is reminding through verses and proofs. The Quran consists of rational verses valid for all times and everyone. Hearts that are not satisfied with it cannot find satisfaction in any miracle.
