Those who believe and perform righteous deeds are, as it were, the very heart of the entire universe. 'Tuba', the glad tiding given to them, is a tree in Paradise or a prayer meaning 'pleasantness and beauty.' This signifies a sweet life and continuous goodness.

O Muhammad! We have sent you to a community before whom many communities had passed away, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you of the Quran while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful (al-Rahman). Say: 'He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him; in Him I have put my trust, and to Him is my return.'

The Quran is such a miracle that if mountains were moved, the earth were torn asunder, or the dead were made to speak, it would be by this Quran. Yet its true wisdom lies in its being recited and contemplated upon. Indeed, the polytheists demanded that the Prophet (peace be upon him) move the mountains and resurrect their ancestors, whereupon this verse was revealed.

Messengers before you were also mocked; I granted them respite, then I punished them. It is Allah who oversees what every soul does. Yet they associate partners with Him; say: 'Name your partners! Or would you inform Allah of something He does not know?' The schemes of the disbelievers have been made alluring to them.

The description of the Paradise promised to the righteous (muttaqun): Rivers flow beneath it, its fruits and shade are everlasting. The end of the disbelievers is the Fire. Some of those who were given the Scripture rejoice in the Quran, while others reject parts of it. Say: 'I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate any partner with Him.'

Our Prophet (peace be upon him) conveys that he was commanded to worship Allah, not to associate any partner with Him, and that he invites only unto Him. He says: 'O People of the Book, come to a word common between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords besides Allah.' Thus, the Quran was revealed as an Arabic judgment (hukm) that both enables the People of the Book to unite upon fundamental principles and expounds the details. This Book prevails over previous scriptures and must not merely be recited, but acted upon accordingly. Moreover, the original Arabic text of the Quran is the source of rulings; legal judgments cannot be derived directly from its translations. If you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have neither protector nor defender against Allah.

The messengers before you also had wives and children. This does not pose an obstacle to prophethood. The disbelievers objected by using the Prophet's humanity and his multiple marriages as an excuse. Yet prophets such as David (Dawud), Solomon (Sulayman), and Abraham (Ibrahim) had also married and had children. This objection effectively amounts to denying the previous prophets as well. Furthermore, no messenger can bring a miracle except by Allah's leave. For every appointed term there is a decree (kitab); that is, there is a designated time for what has been promised, and people are granted an opportunity within this duration. For this reason, different scriptures were revealed for different eras.

Allah eliminates whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills. This is true both in creation and in legislation. Abrogation (naskh, alteration of a ruling) is a requirement of Allah's wisdom. In previous divine laws, certain rulings were repealed and new ones were introduced. The Quran likewise supports the fundamental principles of earlier scriptures while abrogating some of their rulings. All of this is recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), the immutable mother book. Therefore, abrogation does not imply ignorance or subsequent realization on the part of Allah.

O Muhammad! Whether We show you some of the punishment We have promised them or cause you to die, your duty is only to convey the message. Taking account belongs to Us. Do the disbelievers not see that We reduce the land from its borders? There is none who can hinder Allah's judgment, and He is swift in taking account. Those before them also plotted schemes, but all schemes belong to Allah. Every soul knows what it has earned. The disbelievers will come to know to whom the final outcome of this world belongs.

The disbelievers say, 'You are not a messenger sent by Allah.' Say: 'Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and so are those who have knowledge of the Scripture.' Allah bears witness to my prophethood through clear proofs. Furthermore, the coming of this prophet was also foretold in the Torah and the Gospel. Fair-minded scholars who possess knowledge of these scriptures and do not follow their desires have also testified to this.

The disjointed letters (huruf al-muqatta'at: alif-lam-ra) at the beginning of Surah Ibrahim are the sounds that constitute the miraculous composition of the Quran, and these letters manifest as evidence of tawhid and truthfulness. This book was revealed by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) so that he might bring people out of darkness into light, onto the path of Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. Allah is the owner of whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; He is the Lord not only of those in the heavens, but also of those on earth. This book is a light to rescue people from misguidance and wretchedness and lead them to the light of faith; however, this guidance is realized only by Allah's leave. There is good news for the believers, and a severe punishment for the disbelievers.

The disbelievers prefer the worldly life to the Hereafter, turn others away from the path of Allah, and seek to make it crooked. Disliking truthfulness, they strive to lead people astray, and thus they are in deep misguidance. In response to those who object to this book being in Arabic, Allah declares that He sent every messenger in the language of his own people. Messengers convey the message first to their closest kin, and then it spreads to other languages. There are many wisdoms behind it being revealed in Arabic; had it been revealed in different languages, unity could not have been achieved and the need for translation would have increased. Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills; He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.

Moses (Musa) was also sent with signs and was commanded to bring his people out of darkness into light. He was asked to remind them of the Days of Allah; in these days, there are lessons for everyone who is patient and grateful. Moses, reminding the Children of Israel of Allah's favor, told them that He had saved them from the oppression of Pharaoh, who slaughtered their sons and spared their women. Allah proclaims that if you give thanks, He will surely increase your blessings, but if you are ungrateful, His punishment is severe indeed. Moses stated that even if everyone were ungrateful, Allah is free of all needs and worthy of all praise.

Has there not reached you the news of previous nations—the people of Noah, Ad, Thamud, and many others? None knows them except Allah. When their messengers came to them with clear miracles, they put their hands to their mouths in denial and doubted the call. Their messengers asked, 'Is there any doubt concerning Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you so that He may forgive your sins and grant you respite until an appointed term.' The disbelievers said, 'You are nothing but human beings like us,' demanding clear proof. The messengers replied, 'We are indeed only human beings like you, but Allah bestows His grace upon whom He wills; we cannot bring you proof except by Allah's leave. And in Allah alone let the believers place their trust; they endure suffering.'

The disbelievers told their messengers that they would either expel them from their lands or force them to return to their religion. Allah, however, revealed that He would destroy the wrongdoers and settle the believers in the land after them. The messengers sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant met with ruin. Ahead of him is Hell, where he will be made to drink purulent water; he will try to sip it but will hardly be able to swallow it, death will come at him from every side yet he will not die. The deeds of those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful are like ashes blown away by the wind on a stormy day; they can gain nothing from what they have earned. That is deep misguidance.

Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth; if He wills, He can destroy you and bring forth a new creation. This is not difficult for Allah. On the Day of Resurrection, everyone will appear before Allah; the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'We were your followers, so can you avert from us anything of the punishment?' They will reply, 'Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you; it is all the same to us now whether we panic or remain patient, there is no place of escape for us.' When the matter is concluded, Satan will say: 'Allah made you a true promise, and I promised you and failed you; I had no power over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, blame yourselves. I cannot save you, nor can you save me.' For the wrongdoers, there is a painful punishment. As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be admitted to gardens, where they will be greeted with peace.

Allah compares a good word to a good tree whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches reach into the sky; it yields its fruit at all times by the leave of its Lord. An evil word, however, is like an evil tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability. Allah keeps the believers firm on the steadfast word in this worldly life and in the Hereafter; He leads the wrongdoers astray, and Allah does whatever He wills. Those who exchange the favors of Allah for ingratitude and cause their people to settle in the abode of ruin will enter Hell. To those who set up rivals to Allah in order to lead others astray from His path, it is said, 'Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire.' The believers are commanded to establish prayer and spend from the provision given to them.

Allah created the heavens and the earth, sent down water from the sky and brought forth fruits with it, subjected ships and rivers to your service, made the sun and the moon constant in their courses, subjected the night and the day to your service, and gave you of everything you asked of Him. If you were to count Allah's favors, you could never enumerate them; indeed, man is exceedingly unjust and ungrateful. Abraham (Ibrahim) prayed, 'My Lord! Make this city secure, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.' Idols have led many people astray; whoever follows Abraham is of him, and whoever disobeys, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Abraham settled some of his offspring near the Sacred House (Bayt al-Haram) and asked that they establish prayer, be provided with fruits, and give thanks.

Abraham praised Allah, stating that He knows both what is concealed and what is revealed, and that He had granted him Ishmael and Isaac in his old age. He prayed that his descendants would be among those who establish prayer, and asked for forgiveness for himself, his parents, and the believers on the Day of Reckoning. The Prophet was informed that Allah is not unaware of what the wrongdoers do, but only defers their punishment to a Day when eyes will stare in horror. On that Day, they will rush forward with their heads raised, their gazes never returning to them, and their hearts utterly void. The wrongdoers will plead, 'Grant us respite so that we may respond to Your call'; to them it will be said, 'Did you not swear before that you would never suffer demise?'

You dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and you saw how they were punished; and examples were presented to you. They devised their plots, but with Allah is the punishment for their plotting, even if their plot were such as to move mountains. Allah never breaks His promise to His messengers; He is Almighty, the Lord of Retribution. On that Day, the earth will be changed into another earth, and the heavens into other heavens; and everyone will be gathered before Allah, the One, the Irresistible. The criminals will be bound in chains, their garments of pitch, and fire covering their faces. Allah will recompense every soul according to what it earned; He is swift in reckoning. This Quran is a proclamation sent to mankind so that they may be warned, know that Allah is the One God, and that people of understanding may take heed.

Allah the Almighty declares that on the Day of Resurrection, the earth and the heavens will be changed. Scholars have put forward different views regarding the nature of this change. Some stated that the earth will be completely annihilated and a new earth created, while others stated that the attributes of the same matter will change—that is, it will be transformed into another form. Ibn Mas'ud narrated that the earth will become like white silver, whereas Ibn Abbas narrated that the earth will remain the same, but the mountains will be set in motion and flattened out.

The issue of the annihilation or transformation of matter has also been discussed from philosophical and scientific perspectives. Some philosophers, claiming that matter is eternal, considered its annihilation impossible and accepted only its transformation. However, experiments in modern science showing that matter can be converted into energy have suggested that absolute annihilation might also be possible. Nevertheless, definitive knowledge on this matter belongs to Allah, and for believers, accepting either possibility is sufficient.

On the Day of Judgment, the criminals will be seen brought close together and bound in chains. Their garments will be made of pitch. Pitch is a black, foul-smelling, and easily flammable substance. This depiction illustrates the misery in which the criminals find themselves and the severity of the punishment. Some exegetes have stated that this pitch is actually their evil deeds and beliefs in this world, and that in the Hereafter, these deeds will materialize and turn into torment. Furthermore, fire will envelop their faces, which shows that the punishment of Hell will encompass both the inside and the outside.

Allah will recompense everyone according to the deeds they have earned. This is the wisdom behind the changing of the heavens and the earth and the chaining of the criminals. Allah is swift in reckoning; being occupied with one matter does not distract Him from another. Everyone will receive good as a recompense for goodness and evil as a recompense for evil. This is a requirement of divine justice.

This surah is a proclamation, a warning, and an admonition to humanity. The purpose is for people to be warned, to know that Allah is One, and for people of understanding to reflect and take heed. The letter 'waw' at the end of the surah connects this verse both to the previous surah and prepares a transition to the subsequent Surah al-Hijr. In this respect, Surah Ibrahim is a summary emphasizing the principles of faith, while Surah al-Hijr serves as a message that complements it with an emphasis on warning and tawhid.

At the beginning of Surah al-Hijr, it is stated that the verses are the verses of the Book and a clear Quran. Those who disbelieve will at some point wish that they had been Muslims. Our Prophet (peace be upon him) stated that on the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Hell see the Muslim sinners coming out of Hell, they will say, "If only we had been Muslims."

Allah states that the disbelievers should be left to eat, drink, and indulge in worldly pleasures, and that in the end they will come to know. No community has ever been destroyed without having a decree known before Allah; no nation's appointed term can be advanced, nor can it be delayed.

The polytheists of Mecca mocked the Prophet Muhammad, calling him 'madman,' and demanded that he bring angels to them. Allah declares that He does not send down the angels except with truth, and that when they are sent down, the disbelievers will not be granted any respite. It is Allah who revealed the Quran and who will protect it. This protection has manifested in the preservation of the Quran from alteration.

Messengers were also sent to the nations before you, and they were mocked. Allah embeds disbelief into the hearts of the guilty in such a way that they do not believe. Even if a gate from heaven were opened for them and they were to ascend through it, they would still say, 'Our eyes have been dazzled; rather, we are a people bewitched.'

Allah created constellations in the heaven and adorned it for the onlookers. He protected the heaven from every stoned devil. If a 'rajim' (stoned) devil attempts to eavesdrop, a clear shooting flame pursues him. A shihab (shooting flame) is a divine projectile used to repel devils.

It is Allah who created the earth smoothly and placed firm mountains upon it, brought forth various plants, and created means of livelihood both for humans and for creatures whom they cannot sustain. The treasuries of all things are with Him. He sends the winds to pollinate, sends down water from the sky, and keeps it in reservoirs.

It is Allah alone who gives life and causes death. He knows those among you who wish to advance in Islam and those who wish to lag behind. Your Lord will gather them on the Day of Resurrection; He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

In al-Qurtubi's tafsir, it is debated whether the shooting flames (sparks) kill the jinn devils. Ibn Abbas stated that the shooting flames wound, burn, and strike down, but do not kill. Al-Hasan and a group, however, stated that they do kill. The correct view is the first one. As for the flaming columns repelling human devils, it is either metaphorical or pertains to jinn devils, because it is the hidden devils who first attempt to eavesdrop. This analogy is meant to explain that the Quran is like the heaven; just as the heaven is adorned with stars and protected from devils, the Quran is adorned with verses and surahs and protected.

As for the earth: Allah spread the earth, set firm mountains upon it, and produced everything therein in due measure. There We provided livelihoods for you and for those whom you cannot sustain. The treasury of everything is with Allah; He sends it down according to a determined measure. Worldly wealth comes to an end, but Allah's power never ends.

We sent the winds as fertilizing agents. 'Lawaqih' means fertilizing or pollinating. This verse is a scientific miracle. Ibn Abbas stated that the winds pollinate trees and clouds. Al-Razi records this explanation but notes that he did not know how trees are pollinated. Yet modern science has revealed that plants have male and female flowers and that the wind pollinates them. By blowing suitably, winds fertilize plants, and thus Allah's grace becomes manifest. Had there been no winds, there would be no pollination, no rain, and no life.

Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death. The wealth of the deceased passes to heirs, but the ultimate inheritor is Us. We know those who have passed before you and those who are yet to come. Those who lead in faith or disbelief and those who fall behind are all within Our knowledge. Your Lord will surely gather them together. So leave the disbelievers to eat, drink, and amuse themselves; your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

We created man from sounding clay, from molded mud. 'Salsal' is dried clay that makes a sound, while 'hama' masnun' is molded, altered, smelling mud. There are various interpretations regarding 'masnun': it carries the meanings of altered, rubbed, poured, or shaped into a form. Man was created from this lowly substance. And before that, We created the jinn from the scorching fire (samum). Samum means poisonous or penetrating the pores of the skin.

Your Lord commanded the angels that He was going to create a human being from dried clay, and that when He breathed into him of His spirit, they should fall down in prostration. The angels prostrated, except Iblis. Iblis said that he would not prostrate to one created from dried clay. Allah expelled him and cursed him until the Day of Judgment. Iblis asked for respite to mislead humanity and was granted it. However, he admitted that he could not mislead the sincere servants. Allah declared that Iblis has no authority over His sincere servants. Hell has seven gates; for each gate, a designated group is assigned.

The righteous will be in gardens and springs. It will be said to them, 'Enter them in peace.' We will remove whatever rancor is in their hearts; as brothers, they will sit facing each other on couches. No fatigue will touch them there, nor will they ever be removed from it.

Allah informs His servants that He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful, but that His punishment is also a most painful punishment. Then it is requested to give news of the guests of Abraham. The angels came to Abraham and greeted him with peace, but Abraham said he felt fearful of them. When the angels gave him good tidings of a knowledgeable son, Abraham was astonished at these glad tidings despite his old age, but the angels told him that they were giving him good tidings in truth and that he should not despair of the mercy of Allah.

Abraham stated that none despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray. The angels informed him that they were sent to punish a guilty people, that they would save the family of Lot, but that Lot's wife would be destroyed. When Lot saw the angels, he felt dread, but the angels told him that they had brought the punishment about which his people doubted, and instructed him to set out with his family by night. When Lot's people saw the angels, they came with evil intentions; Lot warned them regarding his guests. Despite Lot offering his daughters, the people persisted. Finally, at sunrise, a dreadful blast seized them, their city was turned upside down, and stones of baked clay were rained down upon them. In this event, there are surely lessons for those who reflect.

Then the people of al-Aykah are mentioned; they too were wrongdoers, and retribution was taken against them. The people of al-Hijr also rejected the messengers, turned away from Our verses, and carved out secure homes from the mountains. But a blast seized them in the morning as well, and nothing of what they had earned availed them. Aykah means a densely wooded place; like the people of Midian, they were a community to whom Shu'ayb was sent. As for the people of al-Hijr, they were the people of Thamud who rejected Salih.

Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth; the Hour will surely come. The Prophet is commanded to treat the polytheists gently and act graciously toward them. Your Lord is the Supreme Creator, the All-Knowing. Then, with reference to Surah al-Fatihah, it is stated that 'the seven often-repeated verses' and the great Quran have been given. Al-Fatihah consists of seven verses repeated in every prayer and is the essence of the Quran. The Prophet is told not to covet the worldly possessions of the disbelievers, not to grieve over them, and to act mercifully toward the believers.

The Prophet will say that he is a clear warner. Just as punishment was sent down upon those who divided the Quran (such as the Jews and Christians), they too will suffer punishment. By your Lord, they will all be questioned about what they did. Then, the Prophet is instructed to openly proclaim what he is commanded, to turn away from the polytheists, and that Allah is sufficient against those who mock. The Prophet is commanded, whenever his breast is constricted, to glorify his Lord with praise, to be among those who prostrate, and to worship until death comes. Here, 'yaqin' means death; that is, because death is certain, worship must be continued.

The coming of Allah's command has two meanings: The first is the singular of 'amr' meaning the divine acts of Allah, in which case the punishment promised to the disbelievers or the Day of Resurrection is meant. The second is the singular of 'amr' meaning Allah's decree and commandment. Both meanings have been interpreted in exegesis. The expression 'do not seek to hasten it' indicates that this command has not yet arrived, but is about to come. For if it had already arrived, seeking to hasten it would be meaningless.

In the second verse, it is commanded that Allah sends down the angels with a spirit (revelation) of His command upon whom He wills among His servants, and that they convey to mankind the message: 'There is no deity except Me, so fear Me alone.' This is a definition of revelation: Revelation is a spiritual matter from Allah's commands. All revelations are summarized in two fundamental principles: Tawhid (intellectual perfection) and taqwa (practical perfection).

Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth; everything has a reality. He created man from a sperm-drop, yet man became an open adversary against his Lord. He also created livestock; in them there is warmth, benefits, and food. Riding animals such as horses, mules, and donkeys were created both for riding and for adornment. Allah has taken upon Himself to guide to the right path; had He willed, He would have guided everyone.

Allah sends down water from the sky, and with it He produces drinking water and plants. The night, the day, the sun, the moon, and the stars have been subjected to the service of man. Fresh meat and ornaments are extracted from the sea. Mountains have been set firm upon the earth, and rivers and roads have been created. All of these are lessons for people who reflect and take heed.

The Creator and the non-creator cannot be equal. The blessings of Allah cannot be counted. The idols that the polytheists worship cannot create anything; they are dead. Your God is One God. The hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are denialist. The disbelievers will be disgraced on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be asked: 'Where are My partners?' Those who possess taqwa (the God-conscious), on the other hand, will enter the Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, and the angels will greet them.

To every nation a messenger was sent, saying, 'Worship Allah and shun false gods.' Allah guides whom He wills and leaves astray whom He wills. The disbelievers swear that Allah will not resurrect the dead. Yet, this is a true promise of Allah. When He intends a thing, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.

To those who emigrated after suffering oppression, a good abode will be granted in this world. Men were also sent as messengers before you. The Quran was sent down so that you may clarify to the people what has been revealed to them. Let not those who devise insidious plots feel secure from Allah's punishment. Even the shadows of everything Allah created prostrate, submitting to Him. The angels, too, prostrate to Allah and do as they are commanded.

Allah commands: 'Do not take two gods; fear Me alone.' Whatever is in the heavens and on earth belongs to Him. Every blessing is from Allah. The polytheists allocate a portion of their provision to idols; they attribute daughters to Allah, while they themselves bury female children. For those who do not believe in the Hereafter are evil attributes, whereas for Allah are the most exalted attributes. Allah does not immediately punish people for their wrongdoing, but defers them until an appointed term.

The honeybee was inspired to take for itself dwellings in the mountains, trees, and hives, then to eat from all the fruits and follow the ways made smooth by its Lord. From the belly of the bee comes forth a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for mankind. In these verses there are great lessons for a people who reflect. From date palms and grapevines you obtain both an intoxicant and wholesome nourishment; this indicates that intoxicants had not yet been forbidden.

Allah Almighty states in verse 69 of Surah an-Nahl that He inspired the honeybee. The commentators have interpreted this revelation as inspiration (ilham), since it is not the revelation of prophethood. However, the fact that the art of making honey was bestowed upon the bee with unerring necessity evokes the power and precision of the revelation that came to the prophets. That is to say, this innate disposition (fitrah) given to the bee was instilled into its spirit through nurture and instruction.

In verses 70–74, Allah's power to create, cause death, and cause some to live to the most decrepit age of life is described. Although He has favored some over others in provision, those who are favored do not hand over their provision to those under their possession so that equality is achieved. Allah granted you spouses from your own kind, along with sons and grandsons, and sustained you with lawful provisions. In spite of this, the polytheists believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of Allah, worshiping idols that possess no provision from the heavens or the earth. Do not set up partners with Allah, for He knows and you do not know.

In verses 75–76, two parables are presented. The first: an enslaved servant incapable of doing anything, and a free person whom We have provided with good provision, who spends from it secretly and openly. They cannot be equal. Thus, those who worship other than Allah are like slaves, whereas those who believe in the oneness of Allah are free. The second parable: a mute man incapable of doing anything, who is a burden to his master, and a man who commands justice and is on a straight path. These two are not equal either. The disbeliever resembles the former, and the believer resembles the latter.

In verses 77–79, the knowledge of the unseen (ghayb) in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah. The Day of Resurrection will occur as swiftly as the blink of an eye; Allah is capable of all things. He brought you out from the bellies of your mothers while you knew nothing, and granted you hearing, sight, and hearts so that you might give thanks. Have they not looked at the birds held suspended in the air of the sky, obeying Allah's command? In this there are signs for a people who believe. This verse seems to support that experience and habituation are effective in acquiring knowledge.

In verses 80–83, Allah's blessings are enumerated: He made your homes places of rest, and provided you with light houses (tents) from the hides of livestock, and from their wool and hair furnishings and trade goods for a time. He created shelters in the mountains, garments to protect you from heat, and coats of armor for battle. He completes His favor upon you so that you may submit to Him. If they turn away, your duty is only conveyance. They recognize the blessing of Allah, then they deny it; most of them are disbelievers.

In verses 84–89, it is explained that on the Day of Resurrection a witness will be brought from every community, the disbelievers will not be permitted to speak, nor will their punishment be alleviated. When the polytheists see their idols, they will say, 'Our Lord, these are our partners,' but the idols will reply, 'Indeed, you are liars.' On that day, they will surrender to Allah, and all that they fabricated will vanish from them. For those who disbelieved and prevented others from the way of Allah, We will increase punishment upon punishment. We shall bring from every community a witness from among themselves, and We will bring you as a witness over them. We have sent down the Book as an explanation of all things, a guide, a mercy, and glad tidings.

Verse 90 is of utmost importance: Allah commands justice, benevolence, and giving to relatives; He forbids indecency, wickedness, and oppression. Justice means placing everything in its proper place and believing in the oneness of Allah. Ihsan means doing work excellently and doing good to people. Fahsha refers to sins of excessive lust such as adultery/fornication; munkar refers to evils unrecognized by the Shariah and sound custom; and baghy is oppression and injustice. This verse encompasses good and evil in the most comprehensive manner. Among the Companions, Uthman ibn Maz'un and Ibn Mas'ud emphasized the significance of this verse.

In verses 91–97, fulfilling the covenant of Allah and not breaking oaths are commanded. Do not make oaths a means of deceit for the sake of one community being more numerous than another, and do not be like the woman who untwists her yarn after spinning it strongly. Had Allah willed, He would have made you all a single community; He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. Do not use oaths for deceit lest your foot slip. Do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price; the reward with Allah is far better. Whatever is with you will be exhausted, while what is with Allah is everlasting. Whoever does righteous deeds—whether male or female—while being a believer will certainly be granted a good life and the finest reward.

Verses 98–100 command that when one wishes to recite the Quran, one should first seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Satan has no authority over those who believe and place their trust in their Lord. Satan's authority applies only to those who take him as an ally and associate partners with Allah. Uttering the formula 'a'udhu' (seeking refuge) orally is not obligatory (wajib), but recommended (mustahabb).

In verses 101–105, the subject of abrogation (naskh) is addressed: When We replace one verse with another, the disbelievers say, 'You are only a fabricator.' Allah knows best what He reveals. Abrogation occurs with knowledge and wisdom; both the prior and subsequent verses serve the welfare of the servants. Gabriel (the Holy Spirit / Ruh al-Qudus) brought down the Quran in truth, to grant steadfastness to those who believe and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims. The disbelievers said, 'A human is teaching him.' Yet the tongue of the person they allege is foreign, while the Quran is in clear Arabic. Allah does not guide those who do not believe in the verses of Allah, and for them is a painful punishment. Only those who do not believe in the verses invent falsehood.

The deniers slandered the Prophet by saying, 'A human is teaching the Quran.' This claim is rationally inconsistent; for if the person assumed to be teaching was not an Arab, how could he teach such exquisite Arabic? And had he been an Arab, he would have had to come forward and issue a challenge. Yet no such person is known. This claim amounts to accepting a twofold extraordinary feat and is contradictory.

Those who do not believe in the verses of Allah cannot find the right way, and for them there is a painful punishment. Only these deniers invent lies; the Prophet is not a liar. The Quran is the true Book brought down by Gabriel from the Lord's presence. Believers must not be deceived by the words of the deniers and fall into disbelief.

Those who revert to disbelief after having believed incur the wrath of Allah, except for those who are coerced while their hearts remain full of faith and utter disbelief only with their tongues. The family of 'Ammar ibn Yasir was killed under torture, and when he was coerced, he uttered words of disbelief with his tongue, and the Prophet granted him permission. This is a dispensation (rukhsah); however, as a matter of resolute steadfastness ('azimah), risking death and resisting is more virtuous. Those who open their hearts to disbelief are the ones who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter.

Allah is the helper of those who emigrated after being wronged, who strove, and who were patient. Allah sets forth the parable of a city that was secure and abundantly provided for; when its people were ungrateful, hunger and fear befell them. Eat from the lawful and wholesome provisions, and be grateful for the blessing of Allah. What has been forbidden are: carrion, blood, swine flesh, and animals slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. Whoever is compelled by necessity, without desiring it or exceeding limits, may eat.

Do not say with your own tongues, 'This is lawful, and that is unlawful,' for this is fabricating lies against Allah. There is brief enjoyment in this world, and in the Hereafter a painful punishment. Certain things had previously been forbidden to the Jews; they wronged themselves. Allah forgives those who commit a sin out of ignorance, then repent and mend their ways.

Abraham (Ibrahim) was an upright leader (hanif), obedient to Allah, and he was not of the polytheists. Allah chose him and guided him to a straight path. We granted him good in this world, and in the Hereafter he is among the righteous. It was revealed to the Prophet to follow the upright religion of Abraham. The Sabbath observance was made obligatory only for the Jews who differed concerning it; it does not exist in the religion of Abraham. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will judge regarding their disputes.

Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and goodly exhortation, and debate with them in the best manner. Allah knows best who strays from His path and who is guided. If you punish, then punish with an equivalent of that with which you were afflicted; but if you are patient, it is certainly better. Patience is only with the help of Allah. Let the Prophet not grieve over them, nor be distressed by their plotting. Allah is with those who have taqwa (God-consciousness) and those who do good.

The surah begins with the expression "Subhan". This word means to declare Allah free and exalted above any imperfection. Commentators have stated that tasbih is a verbal noun and expresses the sanctity of Allah's essence. Furthermore, this expression is also used in moments of astonishment and helplessness. The hadiths concerning the splendors (subuhat) of Allah's Countenance show that this concept points to the manifestations of divinity.

There are several wisdoms behind the surah beginning with this tasbih: First, to glorify the astonishing event of the Isra (the Night Journey) and to prepare hearts for it. Second, to proclaim the greatness of Allah's power and forgiveness. Third, to draw attention to the importance of declaring Allah's transcendence (tanzih) in connection with the destruction of the al-Aqsa Mosque mentioned below. Fourth, to point to the connection between the overall theme of the surah and Allah's perfection.

Then, Allah informs that He carried His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) to the Farthest Mosque (al-Masjid al-Aqsa). The al-Aqsa Mosque is Bayt al-Maqdis in Jerusalem; its surroundings have been endowed with religious and worldly blessings. The purpose of this journey was to show the Prophet His great signs. Following the Isra, the Mir'aj (Ascension) took place; the Prophet was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis upon Buraq, and from there he was ascended to the heavens via the Mir'aj. In each of the heavens, he met with prophets, saw Paradise and Hell, and reached the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha).

It is reported that during the Mir'aj, the prayer was made obligatory for the Prophet. The prayer, which was initially commanded as fifty times a day, was reduced to five times through appeals made upon the recommendation of Moses (Musa). However, it was conveyed that these five daily prayers would be counted as fifty in terms of reward. In addition, the Prophet witnessed various scenes in the heavens; he observed the punishments of sinners such as those who consume usury and those who commit adultery.

When the Prophet returned to the Sacred Mosque in the morning and informed Quraysh of this event, the polytheists were astonished, and some believers apostatized. However, Abu Bakr affirmed the Prophet and received the title "al-Siddiq" (the Truthful). The polytheists asked questions about Bayt al-Maqdis and the caravan; even though the answers given by the Prophet turned out to be correct, they still did not believe. The miracle of Isra is a divine sign that surpasses the measures of human reason; yet indications such as Buraq traveling at the speed of lightning open a door for contemplation.

Following the account of the Isra, the surah addresses the giving of the Scripture to Moses and the warnings directed at the Children of Israel. Allah made the Torah a guide for the Children of Israel and required them not to take any trustee besides Him. Then, addressing the descendants of those carried with Noah, it is recalled that he was a grateful servant, and they are warned against ingratitude.

It was revealed to the Children of Israel in the Torah that they would cause corruption on earth twice and rise to great arrogance. At the time of the first corruption, mighty servants were sent against them, who entered Bayt al-Maqdis and wrought destruction. Afterwards, the Children of Israel were granted victory over them once more and aided with wealth and children. At the time of the second corruption, enemies would be sent again, who would bring sorrow to their faces and destroy the mosque. Nonetheless, it is hoped that their Lord will have mercy; but if they return to spreading corruption, Allah will also return to punishing them. Hell has been prepared as an encompassing prison for the disbelievers.

Allah had informed the Children of Israel in the Scripture that they would cause corruption twice and display great tyranny. When the time for the punishment of the first corruption arrived, upon their killing of Isaiah (peace be upon him), Allah set His mighty and warrior servants (Nebuchadnezzar) over them. These servants searched through the homes and slaughtered the Children of Israel, and this became the promised retribution. This event is illustrated with a parable given by Allah: A piece of land with an owner was developed with a sturdy mansion, a river, and trees; yet despite the watchman, when the trees yielded wild carob pods, its owners willed the demolition of the land. In this parable, the wall represents Allah's protection, the mansion the Sharia, the river the Scripture, the watchman the prophet, the trees the Children of Israel, and the carob pods their evil deeds. Allah judged them according to the judgment they had passed against themselves.

When the time for the punishment of the second corruption arrived, upon their killing of John (peace be upon him) and their attempt to kill Jesus (peace be upon him), the Romans were sent to disgrace their faces, enter the Mosque (Jerusalem), and destroy everything completely. This can be considered the outcome of three tragedies. Allah stated that if you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, it is against yourselves. After the first punishment, the Children of Israel repented and reformed, and their kingdom was restored to them; but when their second corruption began, the final punishment arrived.

Then, Allah stated: It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you if you take the path of reform; but if you return, We shall return—meaning, We will punish you again. Thereafter, the glad tidings were given that the Quran guides to what is most upright, that there is a great reward for the believers who do righteous deeds, and that a painful punishment has been prepared for those who do not believe in the Hereafter. Indeed, this mercy was realized through the sending of the Prophet of the end of times.

It is stated that man is hasty, praying for evil just as he prays for good. Allah has made the night and the day two signs (proofs); He erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day illuminating, so that you may seek bounty from your Lord and know the number of years. Every person's record of deeds is fastened to their neck, and on the Day of Resurrection, a book will be brought forth which they will find wide open, and it will be said: 'Read your book; today your own soul suffices as an accountant against you.' Whoever is guided is only guided for himself, and whoever goes astray only goes astray against himself; no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and We never punish until We have sent a messenger.

When We wish to destroy a city, We command its affluent elite; but they disobey and commit wickedness, so the word is justified against it and it is utterly destroyed. How many generations have been destroyed in this manner after Noah! Whoever desires the immediate world, We hasten for them therein whatever We will, then We prepare Hell for them. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it while being a believer, their striving will be appreciated. The bounty of your Lord is not restricted. The Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction. Do not set up another deity with Allah, lest you sit condemned and forsaken.

Almighty Allah informs that He has made the night and the day two signs, erasing the sign of the night and making the sign of the day illuminating. It is understood that the moon was previously illuminating and warming like the sun, and was later effaced and extinguished. As a trace of this effacement, the dark markings on the surface of the moon and the phases of its light are pointed out. According to narrations, Abdullah ibn Salam asked the Prophet about the dark markings on the moon, and referring to the verse 'We erased the sign of the night,' he stated that this was the erasure. This event serves as an example of occurrences such as the folding up and extinguishing of the sun on the Day of Resurrection, and is also significant from a scientific perspective. Allah made the distinction between night and day so that people might seek bounty from their Lord and know the number of years and reckoning.

The verses stating that every human being's deeds are tied to their neck, that on the Day of Resurrection they will encounter an open book, and that it will be said, 'Read your book; today you yourself are sufficient to take account of yourself,' call humanity to responsibility. In a noble hadith, it is also said: 'Take account of yourselves before you are called to account.' Whoever follows the right path does so for his own good, and whoever goes astray does so only to his own detriment. Allah does not punish anyone until He sends a messenger; guidance and error are made known through messengers, and whether to accept or reject is left to the individual's own free will.

When We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones to obey, but they commit evil deeds therein; thus, they justly incur the punishment. Whoever desires the transient worldly life, We give him promptly whatever We wish, and then We prepare Hell for him. But whoever desires the Hereafter, strives for it as it should be striven for, and is a believer, their striving will be appreciated. Allah bestows His blessings upon both groups; those who strive for the world are not deprived in this world, and those who strive for the Hereafter can also benefit from worldly blessings.

See how We have favored some people over others; yet the ranks of the Hereafter are greater and higher in distinction. O human being! Do not invent another deity alongside Allah, lest you find yourself condemned and forsaken. Associating partners with Allah is the greatest injustice. Tawhid (monotheism) is the first condition of faith and the foundation of morality and action. Allah commands kindness to parents, giving relatives, the needy, and the traveler their due, not squandering wealth, not approaching adultery, not taking life unjustly, not approaching the orphan's property, fulfilling pledges, honesty in measure and weight, not pursuing that of which one has no knowledge, and not acting arrogantly.

These are among the wisdoms your Lord has revealed to you. Do not invent another deity alongside Allah, or you will be cast into Hell. The polytheists utter a monstrous claim by saying that Allah has singled out sons for Himself and taken daughters from among the angels. Various warnings have been explained in the Quran, but this has only increased their aversion. Say: 'If there were other deities alongside Allah as they claim, they would certainly have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.' Allah is transcendent and exalted far above what they say. The seven heavens, the earth, and all who are in them glorify Allah; yet you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Most Forgiving.

When the Quran is recited, a veil is drawn between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter; coverings are placed over their hearts and heaviness in their ears. When your Lord is mentioned as One, they turn their backs and flee in aversion. They whisper to one another while listening to you, saying: 'You are only following a bewitched man.' Look at the comparisons they make for you, and so they have fallen into error. They say, 'When we have become bones and dust, will we really be resurrected?' Say: 'Be you stones or iron, or any other creation that seems impossible in your minds, you will certainly be resurrected.' The One who created you the first time will resurrect you. On a near day, Allah will summon you, you will respond by rushing to Him, and you will think that you stayed only a short while.

Tell My believing servants to speak the best words; Satan sows discord among them. Your Lord knows you best; if He wills, He will have mercy on you through your repentance, or if He wills, He will punish you. We have favored some prophets over others; and We gave David the Psalms (Zabur). This refutes the Jews' claim that 'there is no prophet after Moses (Musa).' Those whom the polytheists worship seek a means of nearness to their Lord; they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. There is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with severe torment. This is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

What prevented Us from sending signs is that the earlier peoples denied them. We gave the people of Thamud the she-camel, but they wronged it. We send signs only to frighten and warn. The sights We showed you on the night of the Ascension (Mi'raj) and the cursed tree mentioned in the Quran are a trial for the people. We frighten them, but it only increases them in greater transgression. Your Lord encompasses humanity; He knows everyone through His knowledge.

In the Quran, the cursed tree refers to the Zaqqum tree. This tree was made a means of trial (fitnah) for the polytheists. Indeed, in Surahs as-Saffat, ad-Dukhan, and al-Waqi'ah, it is explained that the Zaqqum tree is the food of torment in Hell. Polytheists such as Abu Jahl and Ibn al-Ziba'ra mocked the Zaqqum by eating dates and clotted cream, thus deceiving the public. However, Allah's power is fully capable of making a tree grow in the midst of fire. These verses drove the obstinate even further into curse and transgression.

When the angels were commanded to prostrate to Adam, they all prostrated except Iblis, who arrogantly refused. Iblis asked Allah for respite to mislead most of Adam's descendants; Allah granted him permission, but declared that he has no authority over sincere servants. To deceive humanity, Satan makes promises with his cavalry and infantry forces, becoming a partner in wealth and children, but his promise is nothing more than deception.

Allah has granted people the ability to seek His bounty by making ships sail across the sea. When a disaster strikes at sea, people forget everyone other than Allah, but when He delivers them to safety, they turn away. Indeed, man is ungrateful. One cannot feel safe against being swallowed up by the earth on land or being struck by a violent sandstorm. The children of Adam have been honored, carried on land and sea, provided with pure provisions, and favored above many of the created beings.

On the Day of Resurrection, every community of people will be summoned with their leaders. Whoever is given their record in their right hand will read it without suffering any injustice. Whoever is spiritually blind in this world will also be blind in the Hereafter. The Prophet was pressured to utter something other than revelation, but Allah granted him steadfastness. The disbelievers attempted to drive the Prophet out of his homeland, but they were able to remain only for a short time. This is also the established way of Allah (Sunnah) regarding previous prophets.

Prayer should be performed from the declining of the sun until the darkness of the night (noon, afternoon, evening, and night prayers), along with the dawn prayer. The angels of the night and day witness the dawn prayer. The night prayer (tahajjud) was commanded as an extra voluntary (nafilah) prayer specifically for the Prophet, and he was given the glad tidings that he would attain the Praised Station (al-Maqam al-Mahmud) through it. When truth arrives, falsehood perishes. The Quran is a healing and mercy for the believers; for the wrongdoers, it increases only loss. Everyone acts according to their own disposition and intent, and Allah knows best who is on the right path.

To those who ask about the soul (ruh), it was said: The soul is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given but little knowledge. There are different narrations regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse; it is said to have been revealed in Mecca or in Medina. The nature of the soul is examined from three perspectives: as the origin of motion, life, and perception. The word 'command' (amr) denotes creation through Allah's command 'Be.' The knowledge given to humans is limited; the true reality of the soul is known only to Allah.

In response to what the Prophet (peace be upon him) told them regarding knowledge, when those who asked, "Is this address directed to us?" were told by the Prophet, "Nay, both us and you," they were astonished and said, "At times you say, 'Whoever is granted wisdom has indeed been granted abundant good,' and at other times you say this. Even though you recite from the Quran that the Torah was given to us, how can you say that the knowledge given to us is little?" The Messenger of Allah replied, "It is little compared to the knowledge of Allah. Allah has given you so much of it that if you act upon it, you will benefit," and for this reason the verse, "If all the trees on the earth were pens and the sea were ink..." was revealed. This address is not part of the previous command, but a general address that begins anew. All of human knowledge is little compared to the knowledge of Allah; it is limited and transient. Allah's knowledge, on the other hand, belongs to His essence, encompasses all things, and is infinite. The entirety of knowledge is only possible through knowing Allah's essence, which only He knows.

The important points here are as follows: 1) The verse, "Allah taught Adam all the names," does not mean that the reality of everything having a name was taught; this, too, is little knowledge compared to Allah's knowledge. 2) Verses such as "...to explain all things" encompass everything that human beings need in terms of religion and legal rulings; that is, it is relative, not absolute. 3) The deficiency of human knowledge is not limited solely to knowing the spirit (ruh); our other knowledge is also little because it is based on the spirit. 4) In this address, there is an honor that grants humanity a share of knowledge, and at the same time, a blow that shatters intellectual pride. In the face of the infinity of Allah's knowledge, man must be humble and realize that the possibility of progress in knowledge is endless, yet must never become arrogant. It should not be forgotten that the knowledge granted to man can also be taken away by Allah.

While Allah explains that the knowledge given to His Prophet is exempted from being little, He expresses this truth above all with an oath and emphasis: "And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you." That is, We could even erase from memories the Quran that We sent down with the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus). Then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper. Except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, your Lord's favor upon you is very great. This warning is very important to avoid pride.

By oath, even if all humans and jinn were to come together to produce the like of this Quran, even if they backed each other up, they could not produce the like of it. The Quran is such a great miracle. The reason for the revelation of this verse is as follows: A group from among the Jews objected, not seeing the Quran ordered like the Torah, and the Prophet stated that they knew it was from Allah's presence. When they said, "We too can bring you the like of it," this verse was revealed. A group from Quraysh also made a similar claim. Ever since that day, despite all attempts, this verse has proven its truth.

The pretext of those who do not believe in the Prophet is this: "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?" If there were angels walking on earth, an angel messenger would have been sent down to them from the heaven. Allah is sufficient as a witness. Whomever Allah guides is rightly guided. On the Day of Resurrection, the disbelievers will be gathered on their faces—blind, deaf, and mute—and will suffer torment in Hell. They do not believe that they will be resurrected after becoming bones and dust. They do not realize that Allah has the power to create them anew. Even if man possessed the treasures of his Lord's mercy, he would still be stingy. Allah gave Moses (Musa) nine clear signs; Pharaoh thought he was bewitched, while Moses knew him to be doomed to destruction. Pharaoh wanted to drive Moses and the Children of Israel out of the land, but Allah drowned him and those with him, then commanded the Children of Israel to dwell in that land, and announced that He would gather them all together on the Day of Resurrection.

We have sent down this Quran in truth, and with truth it has descended. We have sent you only as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner. We have revealed the Quran in sections so that you may recite it to the people at a deliberate pace. Those who were given knowledge before it fall down in prostration when the Quran is recited, and say, "Glory be to our Lord, His promise has been fulfilled." They fall down in prostration weeping, and it increases their humility. Say: "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful (al-Rahman); whichever name you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names." Neither raise your voice too loud in your prayer nor recite it too softly, but seek a middle course. Praise be to Allah; He has not taken a son, He has no partner, and He has no need of an ally out of weakness. Magnify Him with magnification (takbir). This verse establishes a beautiful harmony between the tasbih (glorification) at the beginning of the surah and the hamd (praise) and takbir (magnification) at its end.

Praise be to Allah; He revealed the Book to His servant. This Book is upright, containing no crookedness. Its purpose of revelation is to warn the disbelievers of a severe punishment in the Hereafter and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a fair reward. The believers will abide in Paradise forever.

Among those who are warned are also those who ascribe children to Allah: the Arab polytheists consider the angels to be daughters of Allah, the Jews say Ezra (Uzayr) is the son of Allah, and the Christians say Jesus is the son of Allah. The Christians are the most persistent in this matter. Yet neither they nor their forefathers possess any knowledge regarding this claim; they merely imitate. This is a grave utterance coming out of their mouths and a monumental slander against Allah.

O My Messenger! You would almost consume yourself with grief because those who do not believe in this Book might perish. Do not grieve over them; carry out your duty. For We have made everything on the earth an adornment in order to test people: which of them will perform the best deeds? In the end, We will turn those adornments into dry, barren soil. One must not be deceived by the transient adornments of the world, but must turn toward what is eternal.

The story of the Companions of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf) and al-Raqim is not a greater miracle than the other miracles of Allah. Those youths were valiant young men who believed in their Lord. Allah increased them in guidance. Rising up against the idolatrous king, they declared tawhid (the oneness of God): 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will never call upon any deity besides Him.' Their people took deities besides Allah; they have no clear proof. The wrongdoers are those who invent lies against Allah.

The youths separated themselves from their people and their idols and took refuge in the cave. They implored Allah: 'Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us a right way out in our affair.' Thereupon, Allah caused them to sleep for years and blocked the entrance of the cave. When they awoke, they could not tell how long they had stayed; they said a day or less. Some left off disputing, saying, 'Your Lord knows best.' They sent one of their number to the city to buy food, cautioning him to be discreet and not let anyone become aware of them.

Allah caused the people of the city to discover them so that they might know that the Hereafter is true. The people disputed about building a structure over the cave; the believers, however, decided to build a place of worship (masjid). Disputes arose concerning the number of the Companions of the Cave: figures such as three, five, and seven were suggested. It is Allah who knows them best; you should not enter into deep disputes regarding this matter.

Do not say concerning the future, 'I will do such-and-such tomorrow,' except [by adding], 'If Allah wills.' When you forget, remember Allah and say, 'I hope my Lord will guide me to what is right.' They remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine more. Say: 'Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How well He sees, and how perfectly He hears! They have no protector besides Him, and He associates no one in His judgment.'

Elmalılı conveys various views regarding the length of time the Companions of the Cave stayed in the cave: 300 years according to solar years, and 309 years according to lunar year calculation. While some exegetes state that this duration is Allah's own explanation, others point out that it is the statement of those who disputed over the number. Elmalılı emphasizes that this period represents the duration during which the supporters of the Companions of the Cave remained in hiding until achieving victory, and that it indicates that Islam would achieve victory in a shorter time.

In verses 26–31, it is recalled that only Allah knows the duration of the Companions of the Cave, that His words cannot be altered, and that there is no refuge other than Him. Believers are commanded to be patient alongside those who implore their Lord morning and evening, and not to turn away from them seduced by the adornments of the world. It is explained that once the truth has arrived, whoever wills may believe and whoever wills may disbelieve; that the punishment of Hell has been prepared for the wrongdoers; and that those who believe and do righteous deeds will be rewarded in the Gardens of Eden ('Adn).

In verses 32–44, the story of the two men is recounted: one of them was given two vineyards of all kinds of grapes, surrounded with date palms, with a river flowing between them. The man who was superior in wealth and manpower claimed that his vineyard would never perish and that the Hour would not come. His companion, however, warned him that he should not disbelieve in Allah, who created him from dust and then from a drop of fluid. In the end, the arrogant man's wealth is destroyed, his vineyard collapses upon its trellises, and he feels remorse, saying, 'Would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord!'

In verses 45–53, the life of this world is likened to water sent down from the sky; the vegetation intermingles, then turns into dry debris which the winds scatter. Wealth and children are the adornment of worldly life, whereas enduring good deeds are better in terms of reward and hope. On the Day of Judgment, mountains are made to move, the earth becomes completely flat, and everyone is presented before their Lord in ranks. The records of deeds are laid open, leaving nothing uncounted. Furthermore, it is recalled that Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam, that he was of the jinn, and that his offspring should not be taken as allies.

In verses 54–59, it is stated that people are contentious in most things, and that what prevents them from believing when a prophet comes is nothing other than waiting for the fate of past nations to befall them. Prophets are sent only as bearers of glad tidings and warners. There is none more unjust than those who associate partners with Allah and turn away even when admonished with the verses. Allah places coverings over their hearts and deafness in their ears. Your Lord's mercy is vast; He does not punish immediately, but grants respite until an appointed term. The cities that committed injustice have been destroyed.

In verses 60–66, the journey of Moses (Musa) with his young companion Joshua son of Nun (Yusha' b. Nun) to the junction of the two seas is recounted. When they forgot their fish and took shelter by a rock, the fish made its way into the sea and disappeared. Upon this, Moses realized that this was the place they were seeking and retraced his steps. There, they found a servant of Ours upon whom We had bestowed mercy and knowledge from Our presence (al-Khidr). Moses wished to follow him, but al-Khidr told him that he would not be able to have patience. This story is cited as evidence that esoteric divine knowledge (al-'ilm al-ladunni) cannot be acquired through effort alone and that hidden knowledge (al-batin) truly exists.

Rushd (spiritual maturity and right guidance) is finding what is good and remaining on the right path. In this statement, there is an indication of the necessity of humility before a scholar, that the primary aim of acquiring knowledge is to attain rushd, and that modesty, proper manners (adab), courtesy, devotion, and service are prerequisites for learning knowledge. By telling Moses, "You will never be able to bear with me in companionship," al-Khidr revealed his insight into Moses's psychological state and indicated that through this request Moses would receive a lesson in patience. Moses replied, "If Allah wills, you will find me patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter." Al-Khidr then stipulated the condition, "If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention its explanation to you."

The two set out and boarded a ship. Al-Khidr scuttled the ship by making a hole in it. Moses said: "Did you scuttle it in order to drown its passengers? You have certainly done a dreadful thing!" The reason for rendering the ship defective was that ahead of them was a king who seized every sound ship by force. Al-Khidr damaged the ship to prevent this king from confiscating it. This was an act of assistance under the principle of choosing the lesser of two evils.

Afterwards, they encountered a boy, and al-Khidr killed him. Moses (Musa) said: "Did you kill an innocent soul without [it being in retaliation for] a soul?" The status of the boy has been debated in the commentaries: while the majority (jumhur) say he was a child who had not yet reached puberty, some narrations report that he was a young man of twenty years of age. Al-Khidr explained that the boy's parents were believers, and it was feared that the child would burden them with transgression and disbelief, and so it was desired that Allah grant them in exchange one better and more merciful. If the youth was a mature disbeliever, his killing might be in accordance with the Shariah; however, if he was a child, does this situation create a discord between the Shariah (religious law) and haqiqah (inner truth)? As Imam Rabbani also stated, the Shariah and haqiqah are one and the same; the fact that al-Khidr was commanded through special revelation explains this difference.

Finally, they reached the people of a town. The people of the town refused to host them as guests. There they found a wall on the verge of collapsing, and al-Khidr restored it. Moses said: "If you had wished, you could surely have taken a wage for it." Al-Khidr stated that beneath the wall was a treasure belonging to two orphan boys and that their father had been a righteous man; therefore, his Lord willed that those children should reach maturity and extract their treasure. Al-Khidr indicated that he did not do all these things of his own accord, but by the command of Allah. The story demonstrates that things which appear harmful on the surface are beneficial when their inner reality is known, and that there is no contradiction between the Shariah and haqiqah. Moses raised no further objection, and the parting between them took place.

After this story, it is reported that Dhu'l-Qarnayn was asked about. According to some narrations, those who posed the question were the polytheists, and according to others, the People of the Book. Dhu'l-Qarnayn is an epithet meaning possessor of two horns or possessor of the east and the west. There are varying opinions regarding who he was: some identify him as Sa'b or Shammar Yur'ish from among the Himyarite rulers of Yemen, while others say he was Afridun or Alexander. It is understood that the figure mentioned in the Qur'an was an eminent personage possessing the station of prophethood. Historical debates aside, it is emphasized that Dhu'l-Qarnayn was a ruler renowned for justice and faith.

Elmalılı transmits various narrations regarding the identity of Dhu'l-Qarnayn. Some say that he was one of the rulers of Yemen, specifically Afrikish, titled Dhu'l-Manar, or an individual from his lineage. However, historical records are mixed; a connection is also made with the name Shammar. Elmalılı notes that amidst these debates, the soundest verdict is the statement narrated from Ali: "Dhu'l-Qarnayn was a righteous servant; he loved Allah, and Allah loved him." According to him, the style of the Qur'an also aims not so much to specify names and identities as to recount the narrative concerning his qualities.

Dhu'l-Qarnayn was granted power on earth and the means to attain everything. First, he directed his way to the west and reached the setting place of the sun. There, he saw the sun as if setting in a dark muddy spring or a hot spring. This sight serves as a reminder that worldly grandeur is limited and transient. He found a people there, and Allah gave him authority either to punish them or to treat them with kindness. Dhu'l-Qarnayn, on the other hand, promised punishment to whoever commits wrong, and a fine reward to whoever believes.

Having completed his affairs in the west, Dhu'l-Qarnayn set out this time towards the east. He reached the rising place of the sun and found a people for whom He had not provided any shelter against the sun. This was an uncovered community possessing neither buildings nor clothing. In contrast, Dhu'l-Qarnayn possessed countless means and resources; yet this people had none of them. Allah encompassed everything he had with His knowledge.

Then Dhu'l-Qarnayn took a path toward the north and reached a place between two mountains. There, he encountered a people who could scarcely understand speech. Stating that Gog and Magog (Ya'juj and Ma'juj) were causing corruption in the earth, this people offered tribute to Dhu'l-Qarnayn so that he would build a barrier between them. Elmalılı relates that there are narrations indicating this people were the Turks. Dhu'l-Qarnayn, however, told them that the wealth Allah had granted him was better, and rather than material aid, he requested strength and manpower support.

Dhu'l-Qarnayn had blocks of iron brought, leveled the two sides, and melted the iron by blowing upon the fire with bellows. He poured molten copper over it and built a sturdy barrier. This barrier became an obstacle that Gog and Magog could neither scale nor pierce. Elmalılı emphasizes that this process was realized not through ordinary matter alone, but through a divine power. Dhu'l-Qarnayn stated that this barrier was a mercy from Allah, but that it would be destroyed when the appointed time of the Day of Resurrection arrived.

Elmalılı points out that the construction method and solidity of the barrier do not match historical structures such as the Great Wall of China or the Iron Gate (Demirkapı). According to him, this barrier represents both a material and spiritual obstacle; perhaps it was a unity and order formed by the people (the Turks) who assisted Dhu'l-Qarnayn. The collapse of this barrier is a sign of the emergence of Gog and Magog and of the Day of Resurrection. Furthermore, some Sufis have interpreted this story as a symbol of man's psychological and spiritual journey.

When Dhu'l-Qarnayn reached between the two barriers, he found a people who could understand almost nothing. Saying that Gog and Magog were causing corruption in the earth, they asked Dhu'l-Qarnayn to build a barrier, offering him their wealth in return. Dhu'l-Qarnayn, however, asked them for help with strength and exertion, instructing them to bring blocks of iron. When the two sides were level, he ordered them to kindle a fire, and then to pour molten copper over it. Thus, by completing the barrier, he provided protection against the deception of Satan.

As Allah's promise, on the Day of Resurrection people will surge over one another in waves, the Trumpet (Sur) will be blown, and everyone will be gathered together. On that day, Hell will be displayed to the disbelievers; in this world, their eyes were veiled from Allah's signs/verses, so they did not see, nor could they bear to hear. These disbelievers took servants as allies and protectors instead of Allah; Hell has been prepared for them as hospitality.

Those whose deeds are most in vain are those who strive in the life of this world thinking they are doing good deeds, but who disbelieve in the signs/verses of their Lord and in meeting Him. Therefore, their deeds have come to naught, and on the Day of Resurrection no weight or scale will be assigned to them. Their recompense is Hell because they disbelieved and took the signs/verses and the messengers in mockery.
As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will dwell eternally in the gardens of Firdaws, and they will not desire to depart from there. This is Allah's promise, and it will come to pass.

The words of Allah are boundless; even if the oceans were ink, the ocean would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if the like of it were brought to replenish it. Our Prophet (peace be upon him) is but a human being; what is revealed to him is that your God is one God. Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord. This is sincere servitude, free from ostentation (riya) and hidden polytheism (shirk).
This final section of Surah al-Kahf forms a solid foundation and a beautiful preparation for the transition to Surah Maryam.

The letters Kaf, Ha, Ya, Ayn, Sad at the beginning of the surah are allegorical (mutashabih), and their definitive meaning is known only to Allah. Although there are narrations suggesting that these letters point to the names of Allah or to individuals mentioned in the surah, they are not sound. These letters, from which no literal dictionary meaning can be derived linguistically, are open to countless possibilities through rational deduction; however, their primary benefit is to demonstrate the incapacity of the human intellect to comprehend lofty objectives.

In the story of Mary, Gabriel appears in human form to Mary, who had withdrawn from her family to an eastern place. Mary seeks refuge in Allah, while the angel tells her that he is a messenger from her Lord to bestow upon her a pure boy. When Mary states that no human has ever touched her, the angel informs her that this is easy for Allah, and that the child will be a sign (miracle) and a mercy for mankind. Mary becomes pregnant, and with the pains of childbirth, she clings to the trunk of a date palm; the angel tells her not to grieve, that a stream flows beneath her, that ripe dates will fall when she shakes the palm, that she should eat, drink, and be comforted, and that since she has vowed a fast, she should speak to no one.

When Mary brings Jesus to her people, they accuse her; she then points to Jesus in the cradle. Jesus speaks, saying that he is a servant of Allah, that He has given him the Scripture and made him a prophet, commanded him prayer and zakat, made him dutiful to his mother, and that peace was upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he will be raised alive. These words emphasize that Jesus is merely a servant and that it is unthinkable for Allah to take a child. The factions (Jews and Christians) fell into dispute concerning Jesus and became disbelievers; they will regret it on the Day of Resurrection. Allah will inherit the entire earth, and everyone will be returned to Him.

In the story of Abraham, he tells his father not to worship idols, not to follow Satan, and that he fears the punishment of Allah. When his father threatens to stone him, Abraham bids him peace and seeks forgiveness for him, then withdraws from everything besides Allah and supplicates to his Lord. Thereupon, Allah bestows upon him Isaac and Jacob as prophets. Then the story of Moses is recounted: Moses was a sincere servant who was called from the right side of Mount Sinai (Tur), and Aaron was granted to him as a prophet. Ishmael was a prophet true to his promise; he used to enjoin prayer and zakat upon his family. Idris was a most truthful prophet, and Allah raised him to a high station.

These prophets were the distinguished ones whom Allah blessed with favor. After them came a generation that neglected prayer and pursued their lusts; they will be cast into the Valley of Ghayya. However, those who repent, believe, and perform righteous deeds will enter Paradise and will not be wronged. This Paradise consists of the Gardens of Eden ('Adn) that will be given to the righteous. Following this, it is reported that Gabriel said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'We descend only by the command of your Lord; to Him belongs whatever is before us, whatever is behind us, and whatever is in between; and your Lord has never been forgetful.' This verse is an answer to a question seeking the reason for Gabriel's descent.

Man denies that he will be resurrected after death, whereas Allah created him from nothing. Allah will gather the disbelievers along with their devils on the Plain of Resurrection, then bring them to their knees around Hell, and separate the most rebellious from each group. Everyone will approach Hell, after which the God-fearing will be saved, while the wrongdoers will remain in Hell. The disbelievers mock the believers, claiming that they are superior in status and company. Yet Allah increases guidance for those who are guided; righteous deeds are better in reward and outcome.
