The case of al-'As ibn Wa'il is described, who denied the verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'; he had told his creditor Khabbab that he would pay him with his wealth once resurrected after death. Allah will record what he says, strip him of his wealth, and increase his punishment. In the end, the God-fearing will be gathered before the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), the criminals will be driven thirsty into Hell, and only those who have taken a covenant will be able to intercede. Those who worship others besides Allah will regret it, and on the Day of Resurrection, each person will come before Him alone. The Most Merciful will bestow affection upon those who believe and do righteous deeds; the Quran has been made easy to give glad tidings and warnings. It is then recalled that earlier generations were destroyed.

The letters Tā, Hā are like the disjointed letters (huruf al-muqatta'at) at the beginning of similar surahs; Allah knows best their meaning. While some commentators state that these are an oath by one of the beautiful names of Allah, others have narrated that it means 'ya rajul' (O man). It has also been explained that the expression 'Tā Hā' is a command addressed to the Prophet (peace be upon him) meaning 'put your foot down' or 'tread upon the ground.' For the Messenger of Allah would stand on one foot because he became very weary in the tahajjud prayer; with this command, he was asked to worship comfortably on both feet. 'Sirr' (secret) is what you say to yourself within; 'akhfa' (more hidden) is that which will happen but has not yet happened. Or, sirr is what is whispered secretly to another, while akhfa is what a person conceals within oneself. In addition, 'akhfa' has been interpreted as a past-tense verb meaning 'He concealed.'

Moses (Musa) had told his family that he saw a fire and wanted to bring an ember or a guide from it. When he reached the fire, He decreed: 'O Moses! Indeed, I am your Lord; remove your sandals, for you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed. Indeed, I am Allah; worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance. The Hour is certainly coming—I keep its time hidden so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives. Let not the one who disbelieves in it and follows his desires turn you away from it, lest you perish.' Then He asked Moses about his staff and his hand; the staff turned into a snake, and his hand came out shining white. These are among the greatest miracles. When he was commanded to go to Pharaoh, Moses said: 'My Lord! Expand for me my breast, ease my task for me, and untie the knot from my tongue so that they may understand my speech; appoint for me a minister from my family, my brother Aaron; reinforce my back through him, and make him an associate in my mission so that we may glorify You much and remember You much.' Allah said: 'O Moses! What you requested has been granted to you. We had already bestowed favor upon you once before: We inspired your mother to put Moses into a chest and cast it into the river, and the river would cast it onto the bank, where an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his would take him. And I cast over you love from Me. Your sister offered to find someone who would nurse him, and thus We returned you to your mother. You had killed a man, and We saved you from sorrow; We tested you with various trials, you stayed in Midian for years, and then you arrived at a designated time. I have chosen you for Myself. Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me. Go to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed. Speak to him with gentle words, perhaps he may take heed or fear.' When (Moses and Aaron) said they feared, Allah said: 'Do not fear, I am with you both, hearing and seeing.' Say to them: 'We are the messengers of your Lord; let the Children of Israel go with us and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. Peace be upon those who follow guidance. It has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon whoever denies the truth and turns away.' Pharaoh said: 'Who is your Lord?' Moses said: 'Our Lord is the One who gave everything its form, then guided it.' Pharaoh said: 'What is the state of the past generations?' Moses said: 'Knowledge of them is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets. It is He who made the earth a cradle, opened pathways therein, and sent down water from the sky; with that water We produced pairs [of various plants]. Eat, and pasture your cattle. Indeed, in that are signs for people of understanding.'

From the earth We created you, into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth once more. And We certainly showed Pharaoh all of Our signs, but he denied and refused to accept. Pharaoh said: 'O Moses! Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic? Then we will surely come to you with magic like it; appoint a meeting between us at an agreed time and place.' Moses said: 'The day of the festival (day of adornment), and let the people be assembled at mid-morning.' Pharaoh went away, gathered his schemes and resources. Moses said to them: 'Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He eradicate you with a punishment. Whoever invents a falsehood is surely ruined.' The magicians disputed among themselves secretly: 'These two are surely magicians; they want to drive you out of your land and destroy your exemplary way of life. Gather your schemes together, then come forward in line; whoever prevails today has won.' The magicians said: 'O Moses! Either you cast, or we will be the first to cast.' Moses said: 'No, you cast.' Due to their magic, their ropes and staffs seemed to him as though they were moving; Moses felt a fear within himself. We said: 'Do not fear; you are the one who is superior. Cast what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is merely a magician's trick. And a magician will not succeed wherever he may go.' Thereupon the magicians fell down in prostration, saying: 'We believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron.' Pharaoh said: 'Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? He must be your chief who taught you magic. I will certainly cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees; then you will surely know which of us is more severe and enduring in punishment.' They said: 'We will never prefer you over the clear signs that have come to us and the One who created us. So decree whatever you will decree; you can only decree over this worldly life. We have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive our sins and the magic you forced upon us. Allah is better in reward and more enduring in punishment.' Whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. But whoever comes to Him as a believer having performed righteous deeds, for such there will be the highest ranks, the Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein. Such is the reward of those who purify themselves.'

We revealed to Moses (Musa): 'Travel by night with My servants, strike for them a dry path across the sea; do not fear being overtaken, nor be apprehensive of drowning.' Pharaoh pursued them with his armies, and the sea engulfed them completely. Thus Pharaoh led his people astray. O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, made an appointment with you on the right side of Mount Tur, and sent down upon you manna and quails. Eat from the pure provisions We have provided for you, and do not transgress, lest My wrath descend upon you; and whomever My wrath descends upon has surely perished. Yet surely I am All-Forgiving toward whoever repents, believes, works righteousness, and then remains steadfast on the true path. Allah said: 'O Moses! What made you hasten ahead of your people?' Moses said: 'They are following in my footsteps, and I hastened to You so that You might be pleased.' Allah said: 'Indeed, We have tested your people after your departure, and the Samiri has led them astray.' Moses returned to his people, angry and sorrowful: 'O my people! Did your Lord not make you a good promise? Did the time seem too long to you, or did you desire that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?' They said: 'We did not break our promise to you of our own accord; rather, we were laden with burdens of ornaments of that people, so we cast them away, and the Samiri likewise threw his.' Finally, the Samiri brought out for them the statue of a calf that lowed. The Samiri and his followers said: 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.' Did they not see that it could not return a word to them, nor could it bring them harm or benefit? Indeed, Aaron had previously said: 'O my people! You have only been tested by this; your true Lord is the Most Compassionate (al-Rahman); so follow me and obey my command.' They said: 'We will continue worshipping it until Moses returns to us.' When Moses arrived, he said: 'O Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray? Why did you not follow my way? Did you disobey my command?' Aaron said: 'O son of my mother! Do not seize me by my beard or by my head. I feared that you would say, "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not heed my word."' Moses said to the Samiri: 'O Samiri! What is this you have done?' The Samiri said: 'I saw something they did not see: I took a handful of dust from the track of the divine messenger and threw it into the molten ornaments; thus did my soul entice me.' Moses said: 'Then begone! Your lot in this life is to say, "Touch me not"; and indeed, you have an appointed punishment from which you cannot escape. Now look at your god to which you remained devoted; we will surely burn it, reduce it to ashes, and scatter it into the sea.' Your only God is Allah, besides Whom there is no deity; His knowledge encompasses all things. O Muhammad! Thus do We relate to you the accounts of the past; and We have granted you from Our presence a Reminder (the Quran). Whoever turns away from it will bear a burden of sin on the Day of Resurrection, remaining under its punishment perpetually. On the Day the Trumpet (Sur) is blown, We will gather the criminals with their eyes turned blue. They will whisper among themselves: 'You stayed in the world for only ten (days).' The one most perceptive in judgment among them will say: 'You stayed for only a single day.'

They ask you about the mountains; say: 'My Lord will crumble them to dust and scatter them, leaving their places as a level, barren plain; you will see in it neither depression nor elevation.' On that Day, they will follow the summoner without deviation; voices will be hushed before the majesty of the Most Compassionate (al-Rahman), and you will hear nothing but a faint whisper. On that Day, no intercession will benefit except from one whom the Most Compassionate has permitted and whose word He is pleased with. Allah knows what lies ahead of them and what is behind them, but they cannot encompass Him in knowledge. All faces will be humbled before Allah, the Ever-Living, the All-Sustaining; and whoever bears a burden of wrongdoing has surely ended in ruin. Whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer will fear neither injustice nor deprivation. Thus have We sent it down as an Arabic Quran and varied warnings in it, so that perhaps they may fear Allah or it may serve as a reminder for them. Exalted is Allah, the True Sovereign whose decree prevails over all. Do not hasten with reciting the Quran before its revelation is completed to you, and say: 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge!' We had previously commanded Adam, but he forgot, and We found no firm resolve in him. When We said to the angels: 'Prostrate before Adam,' they all prostrated except Iblis; he refused. We said: 'O Adam! Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife; so let him not drive you both out of Paradise, lest you become wretched. Truly, it is granted to you that you will neither go hungry nor go naked in Paradise; nor will you thirst there or suffer the blazing heat.' Then Satan whispered to him, saying: 'O Adam! Shall I show you the tree of eternity and a kingdom that never decays?' They both ate from that tree, and their nakedness became visible to them, so they began to fasten the leaves of Paradise over themselves. Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him. Allah said: 'Descend from it, all of you, enemies to one another; then whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor suffer hardship. And whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a constricted life, and We will gather him blind on the Day of Resurrection.' He will say: 'My Lord, why have You gathered me blind when I used to see?' Allah will say: 'Thus it is; Our verses came to you and you forgot them; and so today you are forgotten.' Thus do We requite whoever exceeds the bounds and does not believe in the verses of his Lord; and the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and enduring. Has it not guided them to see how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Surely in that are signs for people of understanding. Had it not been for a prior word from your Lord and a term already fixed, the punishment would have overtaken them immediately. So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and glorify Him during hours of the night and at the ends of the day, so that you may attain contentment. Do not extend your eyes toward that which We have bestowed upon various groups of disbelievers as the splendor of worldly life to test them; the provision of your Lord is far better and more enduring. Enjoin prayer upon your family and patiently persevere in it; We do not ask you for provision, We provide for you. And the good end is for the righteous. Those who disbelieve say: 'Why does he not bring us a miracle from his Lord?' Has there not come to them clear proof of what was in the earlier scriptures? If We had destroyed them with a punishment before this, they would surely have said: 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we could have followed Your verses before being humiliated and disgraced?' Say: 'Each is waiting, so wait; you will surely know who the companions of the even path are and who is rightly guided.'

At the beginning of Surah al-Anbiya, the secret whisperings of the polytheists against our Prophet are recounted. In order to belittle prophecy, they put forward various claims, such as: 'This is a muddled dream,' 'it is a fabrication,' 'it is the word of a poet.' When our Prophet informed them of their secret conversations through the revelation he received from Allah, they were utterly bewildered. Thereupon, they said, 'Let him bring us a miracle.' Yet the prophets were not lifeless statues; they were human beings who ate food. This denier attitude of theirs stemmed from their hearts being in heedlessness.

Next, it is recalled that many towns that were oppressive in the past were destroyed. Even if they tried to flee when they felt the punishment, it is told that they must return to their dwellings and be questioned. They cry out, 'Woe to us, we were truly wrongdoers!' This punishment continues until it turns them into reaped harvest and a heap of ashes. Allah emphasizes that He did not create the heavens and the earth in vain, that had He wished to take an amusement He would have taken it from His own presence, but He did not create anything as a plaything. The truth strikes against falsehood and obliterates it. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah; the angels never grow weary of worshipping Him.

The polytheists taking gods besides Allah is questioned. If there were gods in the earth and heaven besides Allah, both of them would be corrupted and destroyed. For if there is more than one god, there would be disagreement and conflict between them, which would disrupt the order of the universe. Yet the earth and the heavens stand firm, and this is a clear proof of Allah's oneness. Allah cannot be questioned about what He does, but the servants will be questioned. The disbelievers are told, 'Bring your proof'; they have neither rational nor textual evidence. Yet the Quran and the previous scriptures set forth the belief in tawhid (the oneness of God).

The common message revealed to all prophets is this: 'There is no god but Me, so worship Me.' The polytheists, on the other hand, slander by saying, 'The Most Merciful has taken a child.' Yet the angels are not Allah's children, but honored servants. They do not precede Allah in speech; they act by His command. Allah knows what is before them and what is behind them; they do not intercede except for someone with whom He is pleased. Whoever says, 'I am a god besides Him,' his recompense is Hell.

Do the disbelievers not see that the heavens and the earth were joined together and then separated, and that every living thing was created from water? Mountains have been placed on the earth lest it shake with the people, and pathways have been made between them. The sky, meanwhile, has been made a protected canopy. It is Allah Who created the night, the day, the sun, and the moon; each travels along an orbit. No human being before you was granted immortality; every soul shall taste death, and will be tested with good and evil. The disbelievers mock the Prophet and ask, 'When is this promise?' Yet the punishment will come upon them suddenly, and they will neither be able to repel it nor will they be granted respite. Messengers before were also mocked, and in the end, the punishment engulfed those who mocked.

Every soul shall taste death. Allah tests human beings with good and evil. Everything does not end with death; everyone will ultimately be returned to Allah, and their deeds will be weighed. The disbelievers mock the Prophet. Who can protect you night and day from the Most Merciful? The entities they have taken as helpers besides Allah cannot even benefit themselves. Allah granted the disbelievers and their forefathers long lives, yet He diminishes their land from all its borders. The Prophet warns only by revelation; the deaf cannot hear the call. If even a slight touch of the punishment reaches them, they say, 'Woe to us, we were truly wrongdoers!' On the Day of Judgment, scales of justice will be set up; even an act of goodness the weight of a mustard seed will be repaid.

Moses (Musa) and Aaron (Harun) were given the Criterion (al-Furqan, the Torah) as a light and a reminder for the righteous. They fear their Lord unseen and tremble before the Day of Resurrection. The Quran is also a blessed reminder. Earlier, Abraham (Ibrahim) had been granted his right guidance. He asked his father and his people what these idols were that they devoted themselves to. When they said they were following their forefathers, Abraham accused them of being in plain error. He said, 'Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them.' He broke the idols, leaving only the biggest of them. When his people questioned him, he demonstrated the futility of worshipping idols that cannot speak. They wanted to burn him, but Allah said to the fire, 'Be cool and peaceful.' He delivered Abraham and Lot (Lut) to the holy land. He bestowed upon Abraham Isaac (Ishaq) and Jacob (Ya'qub), and made them leaders. Lot was granted sound judgment and knowledge, and He saved him from the town that practiced vile deeds. Noah (Nuh) had also prayed earlier; his prayer was answered, and he was saved along with his family, while his people were drowned.

Remember David (Dawud) and Solomon (Sulayman). They gave judgment regarding the sheep that strayed and grazed at night in a field. David judged that the sheep should be given to the owner of the field, whereas Solomon deemed it appropriate for the owner of the field to benefit from the sheep's milk until the crops returned to their original state. Allah made the correct judgment known to Solomon. He subjected the mountains and the birds to David, and taught him the art of making coats of mail. To Solomon, He subjected the raging wind and the devils who dived. Job (Ayyub) prayed, 'Affliction has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.' His prayer was answered, his afflictions were removed, and his family was restored to him along with the like of them besides. Ishmael (Isma'il), Idris, and Dhul-Kifl were among the patient; they attained mercy. Jonah (Yunus, Dhu'n-Nun) had departed in anger, but in the darknesses he glorified Allah and confessed that he had been wrongful. His prayer was answered and he was delivered from distress. Zechariah (Zakariyya) pleaded, 'My Lord! Do not leave me alone.' His prayer was answered and he was granted John (Yahya), and his wife was made capable of bearing children. They used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in fear and hope.

Mary (Maryam) guarded her chastity; We breathed into her from Our spirit, and made her and her son a sign for all the worlds. Truly this community of yours is a single community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me. But people divided their religion among themselves; all shall return to Us. Whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer, his effort will not be denied, and We record it. It is impossible for the people of any town We destroyed not to return to Us. When the barrier of Gog and Magog (Ya'juj and Ma'juj) is opened, they will descend from every height. When the true promise draws near, the eyes of the disbelievers will stare in horror: 'Woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this; we were wrongdoers,' they will say. You and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will enter it. If these had been true gods, they would not have entered it; all will abide therein permanently. There they will sigh and groan, and they will hear nothing. Those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us will be kept far away from Hell; they will not hear even its slightest sound, and they will abide eternally in whatever their souls desire. That supreme terror will not grieve them, and the angels will welcome them, saying, 'This is your Day which you were promised.'

When We roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll, We will recreate it just as We began the first creation; this is Our promise. After the Torah, We also wrote in the Psalms that My righteous servants shall inherit the earth. In this Quran there is sufficient counsel for those who worship. O Muhammad! We have sent you only as a mercy to the worlds. Say: 'It is revealed to me that your God is only one God; will you now become Muslims?' If they turn away, say: 'I have declared it to you openly; I do not know whether that which you are threatened with is near or far. Allah knows both the open and the secret. I do not know; perhaps this delay is to test you and to grant you enjoyment for a time.' The Prophet said: 'O my Lord! Judge with truth; and the Most Compassionate (al-Rahman) is the One whose help is sought against what you ascribe.'

The earthquake of the Day of Resurrection is a tremendous event. Describing the dread of that day, this surah informs us that some people dispute concerning Allah without having any knowledge and follow every rebellious devil. It has been decreed concerning that devil: Whoever takes him as an ally, he will surely mislead him and lead him to the punishment of Hell.

O people! If you are in doubt about the resurrection after death, do not doubt. For We created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid (nutfah), then from a clinging clot (alaqah), then from a lump of flesh—formed and unformed. We cause whom We will to remain in the wombs for an appointed term, then We bring you forth as infants, and then [foster you] that you may reach your prime of maturity. Some of you die, and some of you are brought back to the feeblest old age, so that after having known something they know nothing at all. And you see the earth barren and dry; but when We send down water upon it, it stirs, swells, and brings forth every kind of delightful pair of plants. These demonstrate that Allah is the Truth, that He gives life to the dead, and that He is capable of all things. The Hour is surely coming, and Allah will resurrect everyone in the graves.

And among people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge, without guidance, and without an illuminating book, turning away in arrogance to mislead others from the path of Allah. For him in this world is disgrace, and on the Day of Resurrection We will make him taste the punishment of the Burning Fire. It is said: 'These are on account of the sins your hands have earned.' Undoubtedly, Allah is never unjust to His servants.

And among people is he who worships Allah as if on the edge of a cliff: if good befalls him, his heart is at ease with it; but if a trial strikes him, he turns around on his face. He loses both this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss. Instead of Allah, he calls upon things that can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the straying far astray. He calls upon one whose harm is closer than his benefit; what an evil protector and what an evil companion!

There is no doubt that Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Allah does whatever He wills. Whoever thinks that Allah will not help the Prophet in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the ceiling, then strangle himself and see whether his scheme will remove what enrages him. Thus have We sent down the Quran as clear verses. Allah guides whom He wills to the right path.

Indeed, those who believe, the Jews, the Sabians, the Christians, the Magians (fire-worshippers), and those who associate partners with Allah—Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. For Allah is a witness over all things. Have you not seen that whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the beasts, and many among mankind prostrate to Allah? And upon many the punishment has become due. And whomever Allah humiliates and demeans, none can honor him. Allah does whatever He wills.

These two are two adversaries who dispute concerning their Lord: for those who disbelieve, garments of fire have been cut out, and boiling water will be poured over their heads, melting whatever is in their bellies as well as their skins. For them are maces of iron. Whenever they try to get out from there on account of anguish, they are driven back: 'Taste the burning punishment!' Allah will admit those who believe and do good deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments will be of silk. They have both been brought to a state where they hear the best of speech and guided to the path of Allah, the Praiseworthy.

Those who disbelieve and bar others from the path of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram)—which has been made equal for both the resident and the traveler—whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment. And remember when We prepared the site of the Ka'bah for Abraham: 'Do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who perform tawaf, those who stand in prayer, and those who bow and prostrate.' Announce to mankind the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean mount, crossing every deep valley, so that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on appointed days over the cattle He has provided for them as sustenance. Eat from them yourselves, and feed the destitute. Then let them end their untidiness, fulfill their vows, and perform tawaf around the Ka'bah.

This is the command. Whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah, that is good for him in the sight of his Lord. All animals have been made lawful to you, except what has been announced to you. So avoid the filth of idols and avoid false speech. Be people who associate no partners with Allah and believe in His oneness. Whoever associates partners with Allah is like something that has fallen from the sky and birds have snatched it away, or the wind has swept it into an abyss. Whoever honors the symbols of Allah (the sacrificial animals), that is undoubtedly from the piety of hearts. For you in them are benefits until an appointed term; then their final destination is at the Ancient House (Bayt al-'Atiq, the Ka'bah).

For every community We have appointed a place of worship so that they may mention the name of Allah over the sacrificial animals He has provided for them as sustenance. Your God is One God; so submit to Him. Give glad tidings to the humble: those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, who are patient over what befalls them, who perform prayer, and who spend in the way of Allah out of the sustenance We have given them. We have made the sacrificial camels and cattle among the symbols of Allah for you; in them is good for you. Mention the name of Allah over them as they are slaughtered, and when their flanks rest on the ground, eat from them and feed both the content who do not ask and the needy who ask. Thus has He subjected them to you so that you may be grateful. Their meat and their blood do not reach Allah; rather, what reaches Him is your piety. He has subjected them to you in this manner so that you may magnify Allah. Give glad tidings to the doers of good.

There are various interpretations regarding the expression Bayt al-'Atiq. First, the word 'atiq, like 'itaq, means brand-new and precious, which indicates that the Ka'bah is an honorable and venerable house. According to the second view, 'atiq means emancipated and free; the Ka'bah was given this name because it has been protected from the attacks of tyrannical despots. Indeed, it has been reported in a hadith that Allah protects the Ka'bah from the malice of tyrants. The fate of aggressors such as Tubba' and Abrahah serves as an example of this. A third interpretation states that 'atiq means 'fundamentally free' because it is the property of no one. Since it is impossible to express all these meanings in a single word, the term 'Bayt al-'Atiq' should be preserved as it is.

Honoring the things made sacred by Allah is good for a person. Eat from the livestock (an'am) that have been made lawful to you; however, carrion, blood, and animals slaughtered in the name of anyone other than Allah are forbidden. Beware of idols and false speech; reject pre-Islamic pagan customs of the Jahiliyyah such as Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasiylah, and Ham. Avoid associating partners with Allah; shirk (associating partners with Allah) destroys a person just like an object falling from the sky that birds snatch away or that the wind scatters.

Honoring the symbols of Allah is from the piety of hearts. The sacrificial animals slaughtered during Hajj provide benefits for you until an appointed term, and then they reach the Ancient House (Bayt al-'Atiq, the Ka'bah). For every community We have appointed a place of sacrifice so that they may mention the name of Allah. Therefore, submit to Allah, the One God. Give glad tidings to the humble whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, who are patient over what befalls them, perform prayer, and spend out of what they have been provided.

The badana (large sacrificial animals) are among the symbols of Allah; mention the name of Allah over them as they are slaughtered. Camels are slaughtered standing while tied, and small livestock are slaughtered lying down. Once they have fallen lifeless, eat from them, and feed both the contented one and the beggar. Allah has subjected them to you so that you may give thanks. Neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah; rather, it is only your piety (taqwa) that reaches Him. Thus has He subjected them to you so that you may glorify Allah for having guided you.

Allah defends those who believe; He does not love any treacherous, ungrateful person. Permission [to fight] has been given to the oppressed against whom war is waged; they were expelled from their homes merely for saying, 'Our Lord is Allah.' Had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques would have been demolished. Allah surely helps those who help His cause. Those believers are such that when given authority in the land, they establish the prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.

In verses 67–70, it is emphasized that a sacred law (sharia—a system of worship and legal order) has been prescribed for every community, and that they should not dispute with the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding this matter. It is stated that inviting people to their Lord is upon true guidance. If they dispute, they should be told that Allah knows best what they do, and it is reminded that their disagreements will be resolved by Allah on the Day of Resurrection. It is expressed that Allah knows all that is in the heavens and the earth, and that all of this is recorded in a Book (the Preserved Tablet / al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

In verses 71–72, it is related that the polytheists worship, besides Allah, things for which He has revealed no authority and about which they have no knowledge, and that the wrongdoers have no helper. The denial of the disbelievers is recognizable upon their faces; they are on the verge of attacking those who recite the verses to them. They are informed of the Fire, which is even worse than this, and it is stated that it is an evil destination for the disbelievers.

In verses 73–74, a parable is presented: the things worshipped besides Allah cannot create even a single fly; and if a fly were to snatch something away from them, they could not rescue it. Both the seeker and the sought are helpless. They have not appraised Allah with the appraisal due to Him; whereas Allah is indeed All-Powerful, Almighty.

Verses 75–76 state that Allah chooses messengers from the angels and from mankind, and that He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and all matters are returned to Allah.

In verse 77, the believers are commanded to bow down (ruku), prostrate (sujud), (that is, perform the prayer), worship their Lord, and do good. According to a narration, until this verse was revealed, bowing and prostrating were performed separately in prayer; with this verse, it was commanded that the two be united within a single prayer. The prostration mentioned here is not a prostration of recitation (tilawah), but rather one of the essential pillars of prayer. Imam al-Shafi'i held that a prostration of recitation is required at this verse. The command to 'do good' encompasses voluntary acts of worship alongside obligatory duties, maintaining ties of kinship, displaying noble character, and benefiting others. Salvation can only be hoped for through the grace of Allah.

Verse 78 commands striving (jihad) in the cause of Allah with the striving due to Him. Jihad is of three kinds: striving against the open enemy, against Satan, and against the lower self (nafs). Most correctly, it encompasses all three. Allah has chosen this community and has not placed any hardship upon you in religion; He has granted ease. As was the case in the religion of your father Abraham, He named you 'Muslims' both previously and in the Quran, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over mankind. So establish the prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector and your Helper.

In the surah, which begins with the glad tidings that the believers will attain salvation, the word falah (salvation) is explained. Falah means attaining one's desire and everlasting good. The first characteristic is faith. The second characteristic is being in a state of khushu (reverence and humility) in prayer. Khushu is feeling deep reverence in the heart before the majesty of Allah, and a state of tranquility in the body. With the revelation of this verse, the Companions cast their eyes down in prayer and attached great importance to khushu.

The third characteristic is turning away from vain and useless speech and deeds. The fourth is paying the zakah. The fifth is guarding one's chastity, abstaining from unlawful relations outside of spouses and concubines. The sixth is being faithful to trusts and covenants. The seventh is observing the prayers, that is, performing them on time and in accordance with their proper conditions. The believers who possess these qualities will inherit the Firdaus paradise. Firdaus is the highest of paradises.

Then Allah demonstrates His power by recalling the stages of human creation. Man was first created from an extract (sulalah) drawn out of clay. Then this extract was made into a drop of fluid (nutfah) in a secure dwelling—the womb—followed by a clinging clot (alaqah), a lump of flesh (mudghah), bones, and the clothing of these bones with flesh, and then he was brought forth as an entirely new creation. This shows that Allah is the best of creators.

The word sulalah means to draw out or extract from something. In the creation of man, this expresses a stage preceding the first human, Adam. Some scholars have interpreted sulalah as foodstuffs. In any case, man was created from clay stage by stage. This creation is not the work of nature, but of a conscious creator. Indeed, death and resurrection are also requirements of this divine power.

Allah has created seven paths (seven heavens) above us. These paths have been interpreted as the ascending pathways of angels or as seven systems. Allah is not unaware of creation; He knows all needs and creates everything according to a measure. He sends down rain from the sky in due measure, and with it He grows date-palm groves, vineyards, and olive trees. Benefits such as milk and meat are obtained from livestock. Cargo is also transported by ships. All of these are blessings of Allah.

Almighty Allah states that He sends down rain in due measure and settles it in the earth. This shows that He is not unaware of His creation. Rain is not like water distilled in a laboratory; within it lies divine will and artistry. For this reason, one should not deny the prayer for rain nor be astonished when such prayers are answered. Allah has sent water as a blessing; had He willed, He has the power to take it away. The drying up of waters during times of drought is a reminder of this.

Through water, Allah has grown for you gardens such as date-palm groves and vineyards. In these gardens, there are many fruits and benefits. He also created the olive tree originating from Mount Sinai (Tur Sina), which yields both oil and a condiment for food. By pointing to the blessed mountain where Moses (Musa) communed with Allah, this draws attention to the blessing of the olive. There are also lessons in livestock; the emergence of pure milk from between blood and dung is a proof of divine power. From them you derive benefits such as meat and transport.

The Prophet Noah (Nuh) told his people to worship Allah and to recognize no deity other than Him. However, the notables of his people saw him merely as a human being and rejected his prophethood. They said, "Had Allah willed, He would have sent down angels," and accused him of madness. Noah implored his Lord, asking for help. Allah then revealed to him to build an ark and take the believers aboard. In the end, the disbelievers were drowned in the deluge.

After the people of Noah, a new generation was brought forth. A prophet was sent to this generation as well. Yet once again the disbelievers denied prophethood, saying, "He is only a human being like you; he eats of what you eat, and drinks of what you drink." They denied the Hereafter and claimed that the life of this world was the only life. The prophet sought refuge in Allah, and they were destroyed by a terrible blast. This also resembles the discourse of modern disbelievers.

Then Moses and his brother Aaron were sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Pharaoh grew arrogant and rejected them. In the end, they were destroyed. Allah gave Moses the Scripture. Jesus, son of Mary, and his mother were also made a sign, and He sheltered them on a high ground with running water. Later, addressing the messengers, it was commanded that they eat of pure and lawful things and perform righteous deeds. The community of all the prophets is a single community, and Allah is their Lord.

People divided their religion into fragments, each group rejoicing in what they had. But true believers tremble with reverence before their Lord, believe in His verses, associate no partners with Him, and perform good deeds while their hearts tremble with awe. They hasten to good deeds. Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. In His presence is a record that speaks the truth.

The hearts of the disbelievers are in heedlessness. When they are seized with affliction while living in luxury, they cry out, but at that moment they will not be helped. For when the verses were recited to them, they would turn away and act arrogantly. They did not ponder this Quran; they did not recognize their Messenger. If the truth had conformed to their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted. They turned their backs on the Quran, which brought them their honor.

Allah is the One Who created hearing, sight, and hearts. It is He Who created you on the earth and to Whose presence you will be gathered. It is He Who gives life and causes death, and to Him belongs the alternation of the night and the day. In spite of this, the deniers say, "Resurrection after death is nothing but tales of the ancients." Ask them to whom the earth belongs, and they will say, "To Allah." Yet they still do not reflect. Allah has not taken a son, nor is there any partner with Him. The sovereignty over all things belongs to Him.

In this section, Elmalılı notes that the deniers characterize religion as "asatir"—that is, fables of the ancients. Yet Islam is far removed from unfounded stories. The Quran refutes this claim by recalling the creation of the eyes, ears, and hearts.

To prove the oneness of Allah, the argument of "temanu'" (mutual prevention) is presented: If there were more than one deity, each would have governed what it created, and inevitably one would have overcome the other. This argument also appears in verse 22 of Surah al-Anbiya.

The Prophet is reassured that he will surely be shown the threat directed at the polytheists (worldly distress and the punishment of the Hereafter). Furthermore, it is commanded that evil be repelled in the best manner, and that refuge be sought in Allah from the incitements of devils and from their presence.

It is recounted that at the moment of death, the polytheists plead, "My Lord, send me back to the world so that I may do good deeds." But this statement is futile; a barzakh (intermediate realm) awaits them, lasting until the Day of Resurrection. When the Trumpet (Sur) is blown, there will be no claims of lineage between them, nor will they ask after one another.

In the scale (mizan) where deeds are weighed, whoever's scales are heavy will attain salvation, while those whose scales are light will have ruined themselves and will abide in Hell forever. The Fire will scorch their faces. Allah reminds them that His verses were recited to them, but they rejected them. The polytheists confess that their transgression overcame them and beg to be brought out; however, Allah condemns them to remain abased and silent.

The believers' prayer, "Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us," is recalled. Because the polytheists mocked them, they forgot the remembrance of Allah. Today, Allah has rewarded the patient believers and truly granted them their desires. When the deniers are asked how many years they stayed on earth, they say, "A day or part of a day"; Allah, however, tells them that they stayed only a short while.

Allah declares that He did not create humanity in vain and that they will return to His presence. Allah is Exalted; there is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Throne. Whoever worships another deity alongside Allah—for which he has no proof—his reckoning is with his Lord; the disbelievers will not attain salvation. At the end of the surah, the Prophet is commanded to say, "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the best of the merciful."

This surah contains rulings strictly ordained by Allah and clear verses. It delineates the legal framework and fundamental duties of Islamic civilization. First, it addresses issues of chastity, honor, and family law.

It is commanded that the woman and man guilty of unlawful sexual intercourse (zina) be flogged with a hundred stripes. Here, a distinction is made between 'zaniya' (an active female fornicator) and 'mazniyya' (a woman subjected to unlawful intercourse); a woman forced into unlawful intercourse is not subject to the hadd penalty. The manner of striking: the stick should be as thick as a finger, it should not be struck against a bare body, and vulnerable organs must be avoided. The punishment must be carried out in the presence of a group; this group should consist of at least four people. This both ensures justice and serves as an admonition.

A man or woman guilty of zina may only marry someone who is likewise guilty of zina or a polytheist (mushrik). This is forbidden to the believers. The occasion of revelation of the verse was the brothels in Medina. Some scholars state that this ruling applied to a specific situation, while others maintain it is general. Companions such as Aisha and Ibn Mas'ud maintained that marrying those guilty of zina is forbidden, while others stated that it is permissible.

Those who slander chaste women with accusations of zina and fail to produce four witnesses are to be flogged with eighty stripes, and their testimony is never to be accepted again. However, those who repent and reform themselves are excluded from this ruling. In the Hanafi school, repentance does not drop the hadd penalty; only the sin concerning the right of Allah is forgiven; repentance is not sufficient for their testimony to be accepted.

A man who accuses his wife of zina and has no other witnesses swears four times in the name of Allah, and on the fifth invokes the curse of Allah upon himself if he is lying. The woman likewise saves herself from punishment by taking similar oaths. This is the process of lian (mutual imprecation). The verse reminds what the condition would have been were it not for Allah's grace and mercy.

The requirement of four witnesses is stipulated for the crime of zina. However, if a person catches his own wife in the act of zina, finding four witnesses is almost impossible. In this situation, lian (mutual imprecation) was legislated. According to narration, Sa'd ibn Ubadah and Asim ibn Adiyy requested clarification on this matter; subsequently, Hilal ibn Umayyah reported that he had seen his wife with another man, whereupon revelation came to the Messenger of Allah and the verses of lian were revealed.

According to the verses of lian (An-Nur 24:6-10), when a husband accuses his wife of zina and has no four witnesses, he swears four times by Allah that he is speaking the truth. On the fifth, he invokes the curse of Allah upon himself if he is lying. The woman defends herself in the same manner by swearing four times, and on the fifth invoking the wrath of Allah upon herself if he is telling the truth. When lian is completed in this manner, the husband is spared the penalty of slander (qadhf), the woman is spared the punishment for zina, and a separation takes place between them.

The Incident of the Slander (Ifk) befell Aisha. On the return from an expedition, she lost her necklace, became separated from the army while searching for it, and Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal found her, helped her mount his camel, and brought her to the army. Thereupon, the hypocrites and some gullible individuals spread slander about Aisha. Aisha remained in grief for a month until Allah Almighty revealed the verses exonerating her.

In the verses of the Ifk (An-Nur 24:11-20), important lessons are imparted to the believers: upon hearing the slander, they should immediately have thought well of their own people and said, 'This is a clear slander.' Because they could not produce four witnesses, the slanderers were deemed liars. For each of those who spread this slander, there is punishment in proportion to their sin, while for the ringleader, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, there is a tremendous punishment. In this world as well, the hadd penalty was inflicted upon those who spread this slander.

In the continuation of the verses (An-Nur 24:21-25), people are warned against following the footsteps of Satan, and those of virtue are commanded not to swear off giving help to the poor. Those who slander chaste, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and it is proclaimed that a great punishment awaits them. On that Day, their tongues, hands, and feet will testify against them.

In An-Nur 24:26, it is stated that 'vile things are for vile people, and good things are for good people'—that is, bad women are for bad men, and pure women are for pure men. The pure family of the Prophet (peace be upon him) is free from what the slanderers say. For them, there is forgiveness and a noble provision.

In the subsequent verses (An-Nur 24:27-31), seeking permission and extending greetings of peace when entering homes are commanded. Believing men are commanded to lower their gaze from what is unlawful and guard their chastity; believing women are likewise commanded to lower their gaze, not display their adornment, draw their veils over their bosoms, not display their adornment to anyone other than their mahrams (unmarriageable kin), and not strike their feet on the ground to draw attention to their hidden adornments. These rulings are aimed at preserving chastity and privacy in society.

The verses command believers to ask permission when entering others' homes and to make their presence known to the occupants. Isti'nas is notifying the household through sounds such as coughing or pronouncing the takbir. Asking for permission is done three times: at the first, attention is drawn; at the second, preparations are made; and at the third, permission is either granted or denied. If no answer is received after the third time, one must leave. Banging loudly on the door or shouting is unlawful.

Places that are uninhabited but in which a person has a right of use (such as shops, inns, or public baths) may be entered without permission. This ruling was revealed upon Abu Bakr's inquiry regarding entering inns for trade. However, if such places are rented, the ruling of the preceding verses applies.

Believing men are commanded to lower their gaze from the unlawful and to guard their private parts. Guarding the private parts (furuj) also includes covering the awrah (intimate parts). For men, the awrah extends from below the navel to the knees; Allah is fully aware of all that they do.

Believing women are also commanded to lower their gaze, guard their private parts, and not reveal their adornment. Adornment includes both jewelry and the attractive parts of the body. Necessarily exposed parts, such as the face and hands, are exempt. The head covering must be drawn over the collars, concealing the hair, neck, and bosom. This command of covering does not apply in the presence of mahrams—such as a husband, father, son, brother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, father-in-law, or stepson—nor before elderly male attendants or children who have not yet reached puberty. Different rulings apply to female slaves.

Women should not strike their feet on the ground as they walk so that their hidden ornaments may be heard. The primary responsibility for societal corruption lies with men; therefore, both men and women must repent and turn to Allah.

Arranging marriage for the single and for slaves is encouraged. Marriage should not be avoided out of fear of poverty; Allah grants provision to whom He wills. Those who cannot find the means to marry must maintain their chastity. Entering into mukataba (a contract of emancipation) with slaves is recommended, and compelling female slaves who desire to remain chaste into prostitution is forbidden. For female slaves who are coerced, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
These verses contain clear proofs, lessons from previous nations, and admonitions for the God-fearing.

Verse 34 connects the preceding part of the surah with what follows by recalling matters such as the rulings revealed up to this point, the exemplary story of the Ifk, and the lights of deliverance for the God-fearing (muttaqin). It also states that this story was not the first of its kind, that great figures such as Joseph and Mary were likewise subjected to similar slanders, and that this was not an evil for them, but rather a good.

In verse 35, Allah is described as the light of the heavens and the earth. This parable is like a niche in which is a lamp; the lamp is within a glass, and that glass is like a pearly star. Its oil comes from a blessed olive tree that is neither of the east nor of the west, almost giving off light even if untouched by fire. This is light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills, and He sets forth such parables for mankind.

In verses 36–38, it is stated that this lamp is found in houses (mosques and masjids) which Allah has allowed to be exalted and in which His name is remembered. Mentioned therein are people who glorify Allah morning and evening, whom neither commerce nor buying and selling distracts from the remembrance of Allah, performing prayer, and giving zakat. These are individuals who fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be overturned, and whom Allah will reward with the best of recompense; Allah provides without measure to whom He wills.

In verse 39, the deeds of the disbelievers are likened to a mirage in a desert; a thirsty person thinks it is water, but when he reaches it, he finds nothing, and instead finds Allah there, Who pays him his account in full. In verse 40, their condition is like deep darkness in a vast sea, covered by waves upon waves, over which are clouds. If one stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And whoever Allah does not grant light has no light.

In verses 41–46, it is emphasized that all who are in the heavens and the earth, as well as the birds flying in ranks, glorify Allah, each knowing its prayer; and that the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah. Allah drives the clouds, sends down rain, brings down hail from the sky, and causes lightning to flash. He alternates the night and the day. He created every living creature from water; some crawl on their bellies, some walk on two legs, and some walk on four. Allah has sent down clear verses, and He guides whom He wills to the straight path.

One of the proofs demonstrating Allah's power is that He drives the clouds, brings them together, produces rain from them, sends down hail from the sky striking whom He wills with it, while the flash of its lightning almost takes away the eyesight. Moreover, His alternating of the night and the day, and His creating every living creature from water—bringing some into existence crawling on their bellies, some walking on two legs, and some on four—also point to His power. Allah does whatever He wills; He has power over all things. He has sent down clear verses, and He guides whom He wills to the straight path.

Faith is not merely a matter of verbal utterance; one must believe sincerely from the heart and prove this faith through actions. One of the proofs of faith is to be pleased with and obey the judgment of Allah and His Messenger in the event of a dispute. The hypocrites, on the other hand, come to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah when the truth is in their favor, but turn away when it is against them. According to a narration, a hypocrite named Bishr had a land dispute with a Jewish man; while the Jewish man accepted the Messenger of Allah as an arbitrator, the hypocrite, anticipating an unfavorable outcome, wanted to go to the chief rabbi of the Jews. This incident is an indication of the disease in the hearts of the hypocrites; they are indeed the wrongdoers themselves.

When the believers are called to Allah and His Messenger so that he may judge between them, they say, 'We hear and we obey.' These are the ones who attain salvation. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah, it is they who are the truly prosperous. The hypocrites, however, swear by Allah their most solemn oaths, pretending that if you commanded them, they would surely march forth. Yet what is required of them is not false swearing, but sincere obedience. Allah is fully aware of what they do.

Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is commanded. Obedience to the Prophet means obedience to Allah. If they turn away, the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message clearly, while your duty is to obey. Allah has promised those who believe and do good deeds that He will grant them succession on the earth just as He granted succession to those before them, establish and protect the religion He has chosen for them, and grant them security after their fear. Establish prayer, give zakat, and obey the Prophet so that you may receive mercy. Those who disbelieve cannot escape Allah; their destination is Hell, and what an evil arrival it is!

O you who believe! Let those whom your right hands possess and those children among you who have not yet reached puberty ask your permission before entering your presence at three times: before the dawn prayer, when you take off your garments at midday, and after the night prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. Outside of these times, they may come and go without permission. When your children reach puberty, let them ask permission at all times, just as the elders ask permission.

There is no blame upon elderly women past childbearing age who have no hope of marriage if they lay aside their outer garments, provided they do not display their adornments. Yet for them to remain modest—that is, to prefer remaining covered—is better for them. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. Furthermore, there is no blame on the disabled, such as the blind, the lame, or the sick; nor is there any blame on you if you eat in your own homes or in the homes of your relatives. When you enter homes, greet one another with peace. Thus does Allah make clear His verses to you so that you may reflect.

The true believers are only those who genuinely believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with the Prophet on a communal matter, they do not leave without asking his permission. Those who ask his permission are the true believers. The Prophet may grant permission to whomever of them he wills, and he should ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Do not treat the call of the Prophet among you like the call of an ordinary person; let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment afflict them. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah; He knows your condition and will inform you of what you did.

The word 'Tabāraka' expresses the exaltation of Allah in His essence and attributes, and the permanence of His goodness and blessing. This word derives from the root 'barakah' and describes the continuity and increase of divine good, much like water gathering and rising in a pool. When used regarding Allah Almighty (Allah Ta'ala), it must be understood as transcending all doubts of createdness or alteration. Exegetes have interpreted this word in two primary senses: first, that His existence is eternal without beginning and without end; and second, that His goodness and favor abound. By combining these two meanings, it is expressed that Allah is the highest and most consummate in His essence, attributes, and actions.

The word 'Furqan' derives from the roots 'farq' and 'tafriq', meaning to distinguish, to separate truth from falsehood. Furqan, which is one of the names of the Quran, emphasizes that it is a miraculous and inimitable book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Along with the expression 'Tabāraka' mentioned in the verse, it is stated how exalted and blessed is Allah, who sent down this Furqan. The purpose of sending down the Furqan is to be a warner to all worlds; that is, to warn people and caution them against Allah's punishment. This warning also contains good tidings and mercy for the believers.

Allah Almighty possesses the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; He has neither partner nor offspring. He created everything and determined for it a precise measure. For this reason, nothing created can be a partner to Him. Despite this, the disbelievers have taken as deities created idols that can bring them neither benefit nor harm. Yet, they possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection. This state is a clear demonstration that they cannot be deities.

The disbelievers claimed that the Quran was not revealed by Allah, that the Prophet fabricated it, and that he received assistance from others. Furthermore, they said, 'These are the legends of the ancients; he has had them written down, and they are read to him morning and evening.' Thereupon Allah responds by declaring: 'He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down.' Truly, He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful; which is why He does not immediately inflict punishment upon the disbelievers.

The Prophet's eating food and walking in the markets as a human being was criticized by the disbelievers. They said, 'What kind of messenger is this? Would it not have been better if an angel had been sent down to us, or if a treasure had been given to him, or if he had a garden?' Allah, however, proclaims: 'Exalted is He who, if He willed, could grant you better than that—gardens beneath which rivers flow, and palaces.' Yet the disbelievers also denied the Hour; and Allah has prepared a blazing fire for them.

In the Hereafter, when the disbelievers see the fire of Hell from afar, they will hear its raging and roaring. When they are cast into a narrow space with their hands bound to their necks, they will plead for annihilation not once, but repeatedly. They are told: 'Do not plead today for a single destruction, but plead for many destructions!' As for Paradise promised to the righteous (the God-conscious, muttaqun), it is a reward where they will abide eternally and find whatever they desire. This is a binding promise from Allah that shall be fulfilled.

On that Day, Allah will gather together those they worshipped besides Him and those who worshipped them, and He will ask the worshipped beings: 'Did you lead these servants of Mine astray, or did they themselves lose the way?' This is an interrogation that exposes the futility of idolatry and the deviance of the disbelievers.

The polytheists say: 'Glory be to You! It was not proper for us to take protectors besides You; but You bestowed upon them and their forefathers such bounties that in the end they forgot the Remembrance and became a ruined people.' Thereupon they are told that the ones they worshipped have called them liars, and that they can neither avert the punishment nor find help. Allah sent every prophet as a human being who ate food and walked in the markets, and He tested people through one another. The outcome of those who persevere in patience rests upon their Lord being All-Seeing of everything.

If Allah wills, He could grant the Prophet gardens and palaces in this world as well, but the disbelievers deny the Hour. The particle 'bal' here indicates idrab (digression to a new assertion); that is, they actually know the Quran is not fabricated, but they deny it because they do not believe in the Hereafter. A fierce fire has been prepared for those who deny the Hour. When Hell sees them from a distance, it boils with rage and emits a roar; this represents an attribution of perception to the Fire. In some narrations, it is reported that Hell has eyes and is depicted in this manner on the Day of Resurrection.

On that Day, the wrongdoer will bite his hands, saying, 'Woe to me! If only I had taken a path with the Messenger; if only I had never taken so-and-so as a friend! He led me astray from the Remembrance (the Quran) after it had come to me.' Satan leaves man utterly forsaken. And the Prophet laments, 'O my Lord! Indeed, my people have treated this Quran as an abandoned thing.' Enemies from among the wicked have been appointed for every prophet, but your Lord is sufficient as a guide and helper.

The disbelievers demand that the Quran be revealed all at once. Allah, however, aims by revealing it piecemeal to firmly anchor it in the Prophet's heart and to grant him strength in struggle with every newly revealed verse. Moreover, against every argument they bring, He provides the truth and the best explanation. Those who will be gathered face down into Hell have the worst dwelling and the most astray path.

Allah gave Moses (Musa) the Scripture, appointed his brother Aaron (Harun) as a helper, and utterly destroyed the people who denied His verses. When the people of Noah denied the messengers, they were drowned and made a warning sign for humanity. 'Ad, Thamud, the people of al-Rass, and many generations between them were also destroyed. There are various reports concerning the people of al-Rass; most state that they were destroyed because they threw their prophet into a well. The polytheists of Mecca have seen the town upon which the people of Lot were destroyed, yet they drew no lesson, because they did not expect resurrection after death.

They mock the Prophet, saying, 'Is this the one whom Allah has sent?' and remark, 'He almost led us astray from our gods had we not stood firm by them.' When they behold the punishment, they will know who is truly astray. It is impossible for the Prophet to be a guardian over anyone who takes his own whims and desires (hawa) as his god. Most of them neither listen nor understand; they are like livestock—in fact, even further astray.

After describing the deviance of those who worship their own desires and impulses, Allah directs attention to the evidences of His Lordship. It is explained how the shadow is lengthened, that had He willed He could have made it stationary, and then how the sun was made an indicator for the shadow. The shadow is a blessing between light and darkness, symbolizing Allah's protection. Exegetes have interpreted the shadow in various ways: the morning shadow, the canopy of the sky, the entire cosmos, or divine protection. What is essential is recognizing that it is Allah who extends the shadow and worshipping Him accordingly. The sun, as the counterpart of the shadow, is evidence of its existence; were there no light, the shadow could not be known.

The night has been made a covering, sleep a rest, and the daytime a time for rising and going about to work. Sleep suspends activity much like death, while waking in the morning resembles resurrection. This is a sign pointing to resurrection after death. The winds are sent as harbingers of glad tidings before His mercy, and pure water is sent down from the sky. Through that water, life is restored to dead soil, and drink is provided for livestock and humans. Allah recounts these blessings in various ways so that people may take heed, yet most persist in ingratitude.

If Allah had willed, He would have sent a warner prophet to every town; however, He sent the Prophet alone. Therefore, one must not yield to the disbelievers and must strive against them in a great jihad with the Quran. This jihad is not a combat fought with one's life, but a struggle waged through the proofs and evidences of the Quran. Then, the fact that two seas—one sweet and the other salty—remain without mixing with each other is a sign of Allah's power. Humankind was also created from water and related through the bonds of lineage and marriage.

Despite all these proofs, the deniers worship things besides Allah that can neither benefit nor harm them. The Prophet is only a bringer of glad tidings and a warner; he asks for no reward for conveying his message, desiring only that people turn toward Allah. The believers must rely upon Allah, the Ever-Living Who does not die, and glorify Him with praise. Allah is fully aware of the sins of His servants; this knowledge is sufficient for punishment.

Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne (Arsh). He is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman); He knows all things. When the polytheists are told, 'Prostrate before the Most Merciful,' they deny it, saying, 'And what is the Most Merciful?' and this command only increases their aversion. It is then that the qualities of the true servants of the Most Merciful are described: They walk humbly upon the earth, and when the ignorant address them with insolence, they say, 'Peace' and pass on. They spend their nights in prostration and standing before their Lord.

The servants of the Most Merciful pray to be saved from the punishment of Hell, for indeed it is an evil settlement and resting place. In their spending, they are neither extravagant nor miserly, but maintain a middle course. They do not associate partners with Allah, nor do they take a life without just cause, nor do they commit adultery. Whoever does these shall meet with multiplied punishment on the Day of Resurrection and abide therein humiliated. But as for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, Allah transforms their evil deeds into good; Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Whoever repents and acts righteously turns to Allah with an accepted repentance. These servants do not bear false witness, and when they come across vain matters, they pass by with dignity. When reminded of the verses of their Lord, they do not react as if they were deaf and blind. They pray: 'Our Lord! Grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us leaders for the righteous.' Such are those who will be rewarded with the highest stations of Paradise for their patience, welcomed therein with greetings of peace, and abide there eternally.

At the end of the surah, the Prophet is commanded to say: 'What value would my Lord attach to you if not for your supplication?' The deniers rejected what Allah revealed; therefore, the punishment will inevitably cling to them.

Allah, the Most Merciful, created constellations in the sky. These constellations (buruj) are towering mansions or star clusters. Their number and order demonstrate the power of Allah. Moreover, He placed within them the sun as a radiant lamp and an illuminating moon. It is also He Who made the night and the day follow each other in succession. This alteration is for those who wish to take heed or offer thanks.

The servants of the Most Merciful walk humbly upon the earth. When the ignorant accost them with words, they say 'Peace' and do not engage with them. They spend their nights prostrating and standing before their Lord, that is, performing prayer. They constantly pray to be saved from the punishment of Hell, for Hell is indeed an evil settlement and resting place.

In their spending, these servants are neither extravagant nor miserly, but hold to the exact middle course. They do not associate partners with Allah, take a life without just cause, or commit adultery. These are major sins, and their punishment is severe. However, Allah replaces the sins of those who repent and believe with good deeds; He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

They do not bear false witness, and when they encounter vain talk, they pass by with dignity. When the verses of their Lord are reminded to them, they do not react as if deaf and blind; rather, they listen with understanding. Furthermore, they pray: 'Our Lord! Grant us spouses and offspring who will be the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous.'

Those who possess these attributes will be rewarded with the highest chambers in Paradise for their patience. There they will be welcomed with greetings of well-being and peace. Say: 'What significance would my Lord attach to you were it not for your supplication? You have denied (the divine message); hence, the punishment for your denial will inevitably be bound to you.'

The letters 'Ta-Sin-Mim' at the beginning of the surah convey a severe warning. These letters are the clear verses of the Quran. Rather than sending down a compelling sign from the sky, Allah wills to bring human beings to maturity through willing acceptance. The diverse, beautiful plants grown on the earth are evidence of Allah's oneness and power. Yet most people do not believe despite these signs. Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful; He does whatever He wills and shows mercy.

Moses (Musa) was tasked with going to Pharaoh and his people. When Moses expressed his fears and stated that his tongue was tied, Allah also appointed Aaron (Harun) as a helper. Pharaoh asked, 'What is the Lord of the worlds?' Moses replied, 'He is the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and everything between them.' Pharaoh said to those around him, 'This messenger of yours is mad.' Moses answered by saying, 'He is the Lord of the east, the west, and all that is between them.' Pharaoh threatened that he would throw him into prison. Moses cast his staff, and it turned into a serpent, and drew out his hand, showing a radiant white light.

Pharaoh accused Moses of sorcery and gathered the magicians. The magicians threw their ropes and staffs, but Moses' staff swallowed them up. Thereupon, the magicians fell down in prostration and believed. Pharaoh threatened to crucify them. Afterwards, Allah revealed to Moses that he should set out by night with the Children of Israel. Pharaoh assembled soldiers and pursued them. When Moses struck the sea with his staff, the sea parted; the Children of Israel were saved, while Pharaoh and his soldiers were drowned. In this there is a lesson, but most of them did not believe.

The story of Abraham is related: he questioned his father and his people regarding their worship of idols. They said that they had found their fathers doing so. Abraham stated that he had taken the Lord of the worlds as his friend, that He created him, guides him to the right path, feeds him and gives him drink, heals him when he falls ill, will cause him to die and then bring him back to life, and from whom he hopes for forgiveness of his faults on the Day of Judgment. He prayed, 'Grant me wisdom, join me with the righteous, grant me an honorable mention among later generations, and make me an inheritor of the Garden of Delight (Jannat al-Na'im).' In this story too there is a sign.

The people of Noah considered their prophet a liar. Noah invited them to fear Allah, but they refused to believe, saying, 'Only the lowest people have followed you.' Noah told them that their reckoning rested with Allah alone. In the end, they were destroyed by the flood. The people of 'Ad rejected Hud as a liar. Hud criticized them for building ostentatious monuments on every hill and seizing people with tyranny. They were destroyed. The people of Thamud rejected Salih as a liar. Salih brought the she-camel as a miracle, yet they slaughtered the camel and suffered the punishment.

The people of Lot rejected their prophet as a liar. Lot forbade them from turning to men, but they threatened him with exile. Lot and his family were saved, while the rest were destroyed, except for an old woman. The people of Aykah rejected Shu'ayb as a liar. Shu'ayb commanded them to give full measure, not to depreciate people's goods, and not to cause corruption. Instead, they demanded that he cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them. They were destroyed by the punishment of the Day of the Shadow. All these stories are lessons for the disbelievers.

The Quran has been sent down by the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit (Gabriel) brought it down. It was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue. It is mentioned in the earlier scriptures as well. The scholars of the Children of Israel know it. Had it been sent down to someone who did not know Arabic, they still would not have believed. It has been made to penetrate the hearts of the sinners, yet they will not believe until they behold the painful punishment. The punishment will strike them suddenly. At that moment they will plead for respite, whereas while in the world they sought to hasten it. Even if they were granted enjoyment for years, it will be of no avail to them once the punishment arrives.

Warning prophets were certainly sent to every destroyed land. They were duly cautioned, and Allah did not wrong them in any way. The devils did not bring down the Quran. It is neither fitting for them nor within their capability, for they are kept far away from hearing revelation. They are forbidden from listening to the discourse in the Exalted Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la).

This Quran has been sent down by the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril) brought it down. The Trustworthy Spirit is the angel entrusted with Allah’s trust, who faithfully conveys the revelation to the prophets. The Quran was sent down into the Prophet's heart, placed in his memory, and ingrained as a faculty in him. As stated in the tafsir of Najm al-Din al-Kubra, had the Torah also been revealed directly to the heart in this manner, Moses would not have cast down the tablets nor gone to al-Khidr.

The Quran was sent down in a clear Arabic language. It was also mentioned in the earlier scriptures. The fact that the scholars of the Children of Israel knew it is evidence against the deniers. Had the Quran been sent down to someone who does not know Arabic, they still would not have believed. This stems from the stubbornness of the deniers. They understand it, yet because they are sinners they do not believe—until they see the punishment.

Beware of supplicating and worshiping anyone other than Allah. Warn your nearest kinsfolk. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet climbed Mount Safa, summoned his relatives, and warned them. Be humble toward the believers. If they disobey you, say, "I am free of what you do." Put your trust in Allah, the Almighty, the Merciful. He sees you when you rise for prayer at night and observes your movements among those who prostrate. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

The devils descend upon every sinful, slanderous liar. They lend their ears to the devils, and most of them are liars. The character of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), however, is the exact opposite of this; he is characterized by truthfulness and trustworthiness.

As for the poets, the deviants follow them. The poets wander aimlessly in every valley and say what they do not do. Excepted, however, are those who believe, perform righteous deeds, remember Allah often, and defend themselves when they are wronged. Believing poets such as 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah and Hassan ibn Thabit are outside this scope. And those who do wrong will soon know what kind of end they will meet.
