The disjointed letters (huruf al-muqatta'at) such as Ta-Sin at the beginning of the surah are divine secrets known to Allah. These are the verses of the clear Quran. Sent down as guidance and good tidings for the believers, this Book describes the overturn that will befall the oppressors.

The believers establish prayer, give zakat, and firmly believe in the Hereafter. For them there is an excellent outcome. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their deeds have been made fair-seeming to them, and their hearts have become blind. They will suffer a terrible punishment both in this world and in the Hereafter.

The Quran is being sent down by Allah, the All-Wise, the All-Knowing. An example of this is the story of Moses (Musa): while traveling with his family, Moses saw a fire and told them that he would bring them news or a burning brand from it. When he approached the fire, he was called to and informed that the area had been blessed.

Moses was commanded to cast down his staff, and the staff moved like a snake. Moses fled in fear, but Allah told him not to fear. The prophets do not fear in the presence of Allah; except for those who do wrong, those who repent are forgiven. Moses was given nine signs (miracles), and Pharaoh and his people were destroyed.

Then the story of David and Solomon is recounted: Allah granted them knowledge, and they gave thanks for this blessing. Solomon inherited from David and declared that they had been taught the language of birds and had been given a share of everything. This is a manifest favor.

Solomon's army consisted of jinn, humans, and birds. When they arrived at a valley of ants, an ant warned the others to enter their dwellings lest they be crushed by Solomon and his army. Hearing these words, Solomon smiled and prayed to Allah to enable him to be grateful, to do righteous deeds, and to be admitted into His mercy.

While inspecting the birds, Solomon could not find the hoopoe (hudhud) and threatened to punish it severely or slaughter it. The hoopoe arrived shortly after and said that it had brought important news from Sheba (Saba'): the Queen of Sheba and her people were prostrating to the sun instead of Allah. Satan had led them astray.

The hoopoe related that the queen had a magnificent throne and that her people did not prostrate to Allah. Yet it is Allah who brings to light what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne. Solomon ordered the hoopoe to take his letter to Sheba in order to investigate whether it was speaking the truth.

The letter began with the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and called upon the queen and her people to submit to Solomon. The queen gathered the notables, consulted them about the matter, and sought their opinion.

The hoopoe comes to Solomon (peace be upon him), saying that it has learned something he did not know, and reports that it has brought important news from Sheba. It relates that a woman rules as queen in Sheba, that she has been granted everything, and that she possesses a magnificent throne. Solomon (peace be upon him) attaches importance not to this news, but to hearing that she and her people prostrate to the sun, and he writes and sends a letter to investigate whether the hoopoe is speaking the truth. For if the person who brings news is not trustworthy, its veracity must be investigated (al-Hujurat 49:6).

Upon receiving the letter, the queen gathers the notables and asks them to give her counsel on this matter. They reply that they are powerful and fierce in battle, but that the command belongs to her. Reminding them that when kings enter a land they ruin it and humiliate its noble people, the queen decides to send a gift to Solomon to avoid war.

Solomon (peace be upon him) rejects the gift sent to him, says that what Allah has given him is better, and threatens the envoys. Then, asking who could bring her throne before the queen and her people arrive in submission, an ifrit from among the jinn says he can bring it before Solomon rises from his seat. But a person who possessed knowledge from the Book brings the throne in the blink of an eye. It is narrated that this person was Asaf ibn Barkhiya or Solomon (peace be upon him) himself. The bringing of the throne is regarded as a favor from Allah, and Solomon (peace be upon him) gives thanks.

Solomon alters the appearance of the throne to test whether the queen will recognize it. When the queen sees the throne, she says that it is just like hers, noting that they had been given knowledge beforehand and had submitted. What she used to worship besides Allah had held her back. When the queen enters a palace paved with crystal, she mistakes the floor for a pool of water and pulls up her skirts; Solomon tells her that it is a transparent paved floor. Thereupon, the queen realizes that she has wronged herself and submits to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

Next, the story of Salih (peace be upon him), who was sent to the people of Thamud, is recounted. His people accuse him and those with him of being an evil omen. Salih replies that their omen is with Allah. A gang of nine persons in the city plots to kill Salih and his family, but Allah foils their plan and destroys them all, saving those who believed.

In the story of Lot (peace be upon him), his people commit shameful indecency. Lot warns them, but they seek to drive Lot's family out of their land. Allah saves Lot and his family, while his wife remains behind among those who are punished. A dreadful rain is poured down upon the people.

After these stories, Allah commands the Prophet to praise Him and send peace upon His chosen servants. The polytheists are asked: Is Allah better, or that which they associate with Him? Then the proofs demonstrating Allah's power are enumerated: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, sent down water and grew gardens, made the earth fit for habitation, caused rivers to flow, created mountains, responds to the distressed, guides in the darkness, sends the winds as glad tidings, originates creation and repeats it, and provides sustenance from the heaven and the earth. After each of these, it is asked, "Is there any deity alongside Allah?" thereby highlighting the ignorance of the polytheists.
Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah. Not only do they lack knowledge concerning the Hereafter, but they are also in doubt and blindness regarding it.

The particle 'am' (or) in verse 60 is explained: connected (muttasil) 'am' denotes two alternatives, while severed (munqati') 'am' carries the meaning of transition (like 'bal') and interrogation. Although 'or' is used in translation, it does not fully convey the sense; expressions like 'nay, rather' are sometimes preferred. Exegetes have interpreted the expression in the verse 'Or the One who created the heavens and the earth?' as meaning 'Is the Creator better, or that which they associate as partners?'

In verse 60, the final cause (illat al-gha'iyyah / teleological cause) is discussed: the sending down of water is for the benefit of humanity. Although philosophers deny a final cause in divine acts, this is accepted as an argument from wisdom. There is benefit and purpose in Allah's acts; creation is not in vain. The connection between water and life demonstrates Allah's wisdom.

In the continuation of verse 60, it is emphasized that beautiful gardens are grown with the water sent down, and that humans could not cause even a single tree to grow on their own. This is manifest proof that there is no deity besides Allah. With the question 'Is there any deity alongside Allah?', the deviation of the polytheists is exposed.

In verse 61, the power of Allah is described: He made the earth fit for dwelling, caused rivers to flow, set firm mountains, and placed a barrier between the two seas. These objective signs demonstrate His oneness. Most of the polytheists do not know these realities.

In verse 62, it is Allah Who answers the prayer of the distressed one and makes you successors on earth. This is glad tidings both individually and socially; it points to the future dominance of Islam. The question 'Is there a god besides Allah?' is repeated.

In verses 63-64, it is Allah Who guides in the darkness of land and sea, Who sends the winds as heralds before His mercy, Who originates creation and will then repeat it, and Who provides sustenance from heaven and earth. In this fifth question, it is emphasized that the order of creation necessitates a single deity. The polytheists are asked to bring their proof.

In verses 65-66, it is stated that only Allah knows the unseen (ghayb), and that although people have received successive knowledge concerning the Hereafter, they remain in doubt. The word 'iddaraka' signifies the continuous, uninterrupted arrival of information; yet, because they are blind, they do not wish to see.

In verses 67-75, the deniers' rejection of the resurrection and their dismissal of it as 'fables of the ancients' are recounted. Patience is advised to the Prophet; tidings are given that a portion of the punishment will come soon. Allah's grace and knowledge are emphasized, and it is stated that the Quran will settle the disputes of the Children of Israel.

Verses 76-79 declare that the Quran is guidance and mercy for the believers, that their Lord will deliver His judgment, and that since the Prophet stands upon the manifest truth, he should place his trust in Allah.

In verses 80-81, it is explained that calling out to the dead (the disbelievers) is of no avail, and that only those who submit wholeheartedly can hear. In verse 82, 'Dabbat al-Ard' (the Beast of the Earth), one of the signs of the Day of Judgment, is expounded upon. There are different interpretations as to whether this creature is a speaking beast or a human being; in the famous hadith, it is narrated that it will distinguish the believers with the staff of Moses (Musa) and the seal of Solomon in its possession.

In verses 83-86, the Day is depicted when those who denied the verses from every community will be gathered. Allah will question them, and because of the wrongdoing they committed, the word will be fulfilled against them, leaving them unable to speak. Attention is drawn to the lessons in the creation of night and day.

In verse 86, Allah Almighty draws attention to the creation of night and day, saying, 'Have they not seen?' What is meant here is seeing with the eye of the heart; for the fact that night and day were created with the wisdom of tranquility and activity can only be understood through reasoning. This order consists of clear signs pointing to Allah's existence, His oneness, prophethood, and the Hereafter. In terms of human life in particular, the creation of night for rest and day for labor demonstrates the existence of a Creator Who knows all things and does whatever He wills.

In verse 87, it is reported that on the Day the Trumpet (Sur) is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be stricken with terror, except those whom Allah wills. There are different views regarding the Sur: some interpret it as the plural of suwar (forms), meaning the breathing of souls, while others interpret it as a figurative horn. According to the majority, however, the Sur is a horn that will be blown by Israfil, and it will be blown three times: the first for terror, the second for death, and the third for resurrection. At the first blowing mentioned in this verse, everyone is shaken with dread, yet those whom Allah wills are safe. It is not certain who these are; it is most appropriate to explain them with 'those who are secure from fear' in verse 89.

In verses 88-89, it is described that while the mountains are thought to be stationary, they pass away like clouds. Commentators generally interpret this expression as referring to the Day of Judgment, yet in that case the expression 'you think' would not be fitting. Some scholars argue that this movement continues constantly in this world, and that the mountains are changing and being renewed at every moment. According to Elmalılı, this verse directs thought to the Day of Judgment and the resurrection by demonstrating the continuous coming into being and passing away of entities. In the particles of mountains there is a transformation like clouds, and through Allah's flawless artistry, this order operates with wisdom. Those who come with goodness on that Day will be secure from fear, whereas those who come with evil will be cast into the Fire.

In verse 90, it is stated that those who bring evil deeds will be cast into Hell, and it is said, 'Will you be recompensed for anything other than what you used to do?' This demonstrates that deeds will be requited with justice.

In verses 91-93, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is commanded: worship only the Lord of Mecca, be of the Muslims, and recite the Quran. Whoever accepts guidance does so for his own good, and whoever strays, he is only a warner. Then it is stated, 'Praise be to Allah; He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them.' This is the glad tidings of the triumphs promised in the Quran and the future victories of Islam. Indeed, from Badr to Mehmed the Conqueror (Fatih), Selim I (Yavuz), and Suleiman the Magnificent (Kanuni), these promises were fulfilled. The victories of Gallipoli (Çanakkale), Sakarya, and İnönü, as well as the liberation of Izmir, are also among the signs that Allah has shown in this century.

At the end of the surah, it is emphasized that although Islam experiences ups and downs like night and day, its future is bright. The hadith 'Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange, so glad tidings to the strangers' expresses glad tidings rather than despair. That is to say, Islam will not be extinguished but will be reborn. What falls upon the believers is to praise Allah, await His signs, and believe that their Lord is not unaware of what they do.

The Quran is introduced as a luminous book that clarifies all things. Tilawah (recitation) means to follow, to pursue, and specifically refers to reciting the books revealed by Allah or carefully observing the commandments and prohibitions within them. Here, tilawah is a metaphor for reciting and revealing through Gabriel (Jibril). When Pharaoh learned that a boy would be born from the Children of Israel who would overthrow his kingdom, he began killing the children.

Pharaoh was slaughtering innocent boys, seeking to leave the girls without men so he could exploit them as he wished. Allah made known to Pharaoh and Haman that He would bring upon them the very thing they feared, and that their kingdom would come to an end on account of the Children of Israel. He promised to make them leaders and inheritors—that is, to make the oppressed people inheritors of the eastern and western lands that He had filled with blessings.

Moses's mother was inspired through revelation (wahy). It has been stated that this revelation was not the revelation of prophethood, but rather inspiration or a dream. Allah gave her the glad tidings that He would return Moses to her and make him one of the messengers. This inspiration occurred after Moses was born and had been nursed for a time. The word Nile (Nil) conveys the sense of 'negligence' (taqsir), not 'error' (khata'). This event served as an occasion for testing Pharaoh's household.

The heart of Moses's mother became utterly empty in the morning, filled with distress at receiving no news of Moses. She had almost disclosed his identity, but Allah strengthened her heart. She told Moses's sister to follow him. She watched him from afar, and Pharaoh's household did not realize that she was his sister. Referring to her as 'his sister' here is more eloquent in emphasizing affection and compassion.

When Moses reached the age of full maturity, Allah granted him wisdom and knowledge. One day, upon entering the city, he found two men fighting, one from his own people and the other from his enemies. When the one from his people asked for help, Moses struck the enemy with a fist, causing his death, and said, 'This is of Satan's doing.' He then repented and sought Allah's forgiveness. The next day, the same man asking for help again prompted Moses to say, 'Indeed, you are clearly a troublemaker!' The people of the city plotted to kill Moses; a man warned him, and Moses departed from there, fearful and watchful.

Heading toward Midian (Madyan), Moses said, 'I hope my Lord will guide me to the right path.' When he arrived at the water of Midian, he found a crowd of people watering their flocks, and apart from them, two women keeping back their sheep. The women explained that they could not water their flocks until the shepherds had watered theirs and withdrawn, and that their father was an elderly man. Moses watered their flocks for them, then withdrew to the shade and said, 'My Lord! Truly, I am in need of whatever good You bestow upon me.' One of the women came walking shyly and said that her father was calling him. Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) consoled Moses, saying, 'Do not fear; you have escaped from that wrongdoing people.' One of his daughters suggested hiring Moses, stating that he was strong and trustworthy. Shu'ayb offered to marry one of his two daughters to him on the condition that he work for eight years, adding that if he completed ten years, it would be of his own accord. Moses accepted this offer.

When Moses completed the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire in the direction of Mount Tur and said, 'Wait here; perhaps I can bring you some news or a burning brand from the fire.' When he reached it, a voice called out to him from a tree on the right bank of the blessed valley: 'O Moses! Know that I am Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.' He was commanded to cast down his staff, and when it turned into a serpent, he turned away in fear and fled. Allah said, 'Draw near and do not fear.' He was instructed to place his hand into his garment so that it would come out shining white, and to draw his arms close to himself against fear. These two miracles were to be proofs against Pharaoh and his chiefs. Moses requested assistance, stating that he feared because he had killed a man previously and that his brother Aaron (Harun) was more eloquent in speech. Allah declared that He would strengthen him with his brother and that they would prevail.

When Moses came with clear signs, they said, 'This is nothing but invented magic; we never heard of such a thing among our forefathers.' Moses said that his Lord knows best who brings guidance from Him and who will have the best outcome in the end. Pharaoh said to his nobles, 'I know of no god for you other than myself,' and ordered Haman to fire bricks out of clay and build a tower for him. He and his soldiers grew arrogant, thinking they would not be returned to Us. So We seized them and threw them into the sea. We made them leaders who invite to the Fire; on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped, and in this world We pursued them with a curse.

After destroying the earlier generations, Allah gave Moses the Torah. It was given as clear proofs for people, a guide, and a mercy. O Messenger! You were not on the western side when We revealed the command to Moses. Rather, We brought forth many generations; nor were you dwelling among the people of Midian, reciting Our verses to them. Nor were you beside Mount Tur when We called out. We made these known as a mercy from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you. They used to wish that a prophet would be sent to them, but when the truth came, they said, 'Why has he not been given the like of what was given to Moses?' Yet had they not previously disbelieved in what was given to Moses? Say: 'Bring a book from Allah that is more guiding than these two, so that I may follow it.' If they do not respond to you, then know that they are only following their desires. And who could be more astray than one who follows his desires? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

That the Torah was given to mankind as guidance and mercy after the destruction of the earlier generations was so that they might reflect and take heed. Following this explanation, the wisdom behind the revelation of the Quran and the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are described.

When revelation was given to Moses, you were not on the western side, by Mount Tur; nor were you among the witnesses. But We brought forth many generations, a long time passed over them, their hearts hardened, and their religions became corrupted. For this reason, it became necessary to send a new prophet and book. This is a foundational basis for the legal maxim (qawa'id al-fiqh) that 'rulings change with the change of times.' The hadith stating that someone will be sent every hundred years to renew the religion also supports this verse. However, renewal does not mean introducing innovation (bid'ah) that has no basis in the religion; every innovation is misguidance (dalalah).

You were not beside Mount Tur, but you were sent as a mercy from your Lord, to warn a people to whom no warner had come before. This people was the Arabs; although earlier prophets had come to them, no prophet was sent during the intervening generations. When the Quran came to them, they said, 'If only we had been given the like of what was given to Moses,' and regarded both the Torah and the Quran as magic. Say: Bring a book from Allah that is more guiding than these two, if you are truthful. If they cannot bring it, know that they are following their vain desires. Who can be more astray than one who follows his desires? Allah does not guide the wrongdoers.

By oath, We have conveyed the word (revelation) to them continuously so that they might reflect and take heed. Those who were given the Scripture before (those among the Jews and Christians who believed) also believe in the Quran. They will be given their reward twice; they repel evil with good, and when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds.' This is a farewell greeting.

You cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. This verse was revealed concerning Abu Talib. The polytheists said, "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be torn away from our land." Did Allah not establish for them a secure sanctuary (Haram), to which the fruits of all things are brought? Yet most of them do not know. We have destroyed many a city that grew insolent in its prosperity. Your Lord would not destroy cities without sending a messenger. Whatever worldly goods you have been given are temporary; that which is with Allah is better and more enduring.

Is he to whom a good promise was made and who attains it like one who merely enjoyed the pleasures of the worldly life and then was subjected to punishment? On that Day, Allah will call to the polytheists: "Where are My partners?" Their leaders will say, "We led them astray; we dissociate ourselves before You." The partners will be called upon, but they will not answer. Those who repent and believe will attain salvation. Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses; they have no choice. Allah also knows what they conceal. The night and the day are from His mercy. On that Day, a witness will be brought forth from every nation, and their proof will be demanded; it is then understood that the truth belongs to Allah.

Qarun (Korah) was from the people of Moses (Musa) and transgressed against them. Allah had bestowed upon him such treasures that a company of strong men could scarcely bear their keys. His people warned him against arrogance: "Seek the home of the Hereafter through what Allah has given you, and do not forget your share of the world. Do good as Allah has been good to you, and do not cause corruption." Qarun claimed that his wealth was due to the knowledge he possessed. Did he not know that Allah had destroyed generations before him? In the end, We caused the earth to swallow Qarun and his dwelling; there was no one to help him. Those who had previously desired to be in his place realized that Allah grants provision to whom He wills.

The home of the Hereafter (Paradise) is for those who do not desire haughtiness or corruption on earth. Whoever brings good will be met with better than it; whoever brings evil will only be recompensed according to what they did. Allah, who has ordained the Quran upon you, will surely return you to the place of return (Mecca). You did not expect that this Book would be revealed to you; this is a mercy from your Lord. Never support the disbelievers, and do not let them turn you away from the verses of Allah. Invite to your Lord, and do not be of the polytheists. Do not invoke any other deity alongside Allah; there is no deity but Him. Everything will perish except His Essence; the judgment belongs to Him, and to Him you will be returned.

In this verse, the concept of the Face of Allah (wajh) is explained. There is no deity but Him, and everything will perish except His Face. That is to say, every entity other than the Essence of Allah is in reality deemed non-existent, because their existence does not originate from themselves, but depends upon Allah.

Since created beings are receptive to perishing at every moment, they are in truth as if non-existent, or they will perish one day. Yet Allah is Ever-Living in His Essence, eternal and everlasting; His existence is self-subsistent. This is the meaning preferred by the majority.

According to another interpretation, 'face' (wajh) means the intended direction. In this case, the verse conveys that everything is in destruction except the direction intended for Allah's pleasure and approval—that is, even the blessings of the Hereafter are not temporary.

A third interpretation is as follows: Everything has a face turned toward Allah, which is its true form in Allah's knowledge. The return of everything through this face is to Allah. That is, every being returns to Allah, who is the purpose of its creation.

Judgment belongs solely to Allah; the judgment of anyone else is invalid. The rule of those who attempt to legislate will be annulled, and only Allah's judgment will endure. In the end, all of you will be returned to Him and held to account. The conclusion of all the narratives is precisely this decree of return. No one can fail to submit to this judgment.

There are three different reports regarding the occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) for the opening verses of Surah al-Ankabut. One of these concerns Ammar ibn Yasir and his companions being tortured by the polytheists in Mecca. According to the second narration, the Muslims in Medina wrote to those in Mecca who had promised to embrace Islam that they must emigrate (hijrah); they set out, but the polytheists hindered them. The third report concerns Mihja' ibn Abdullah, who was martyred in the Battle of Badr. Regarding the expression that Allah 'will surely know,' it is emphasized that His knowledge does not change, but rather what is known changes. The purpose is to distinguish the believers from the liars through testing and to recompense them.

Let those who commit evil deeds not assume that they can outstrip Allah and escape. These evil deeds refer particularly to the oppression and torment inflicted upon the believers. Those who hope to meet Allah must persevere with patience until the time He has appointed and perform righteous deeds. Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing; He hears prayers and knows intentions.

Whoever strives (engages in jihad) does so only for his own benefit, because the reward of this effort belongs to himself, not to Allah. Allah is free of all needs from anything. It is probable that these verses were revealed in Medina, because the hypocrites were there. The believers have faith that there is no god but Allah, and they praise Him.

On the Day of Resurrection, everyone will bear their own sins, and they will also carry the sins of those whom they led astray. Noah (peace be upon him) remained among his people for nine hundred and fifty years, and ultimately they were destroyed by the flood. Noah and those aboard the ark were saved, and this event was made a lesson for all the worlds. Seeking protection from Allah's punishment through material means is also by His command.

Abraham (peace be upon him) called his people to worship Allah and stated that worshiping idols is a falsehood. Idols cannot provide sustenance; sustenance is with Allah. Abraham was saved from the fire by Allah against his people's threat to kill or burn him. Subsequently, Lot believed in him, and Abraham emigrated to his Lord. Allah granted him Isaac and Jacob, and bestowed prophethood and the scriptures upon his descendants.

Lot (peace be upon him) forbade his people from their indecencies, such as approaching men, highway robbery, and committing obscenities in their gatherings, but they demanded Allah's punishment instead. The messengers gave Abraham the tidings that the people of Lot would be destroyed; Lot and his family were saved, while his wife remained behind in the punishment. This event is a clear lesson for those who use their intellect.

Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) invited the people of Midian to worship Allah, to hope for the Last Day, and forbade them from causing corruption. When they rejected him, they were destroyed by a tremor. The peoples of 'Ad and Thamud were also destroyed, for Satan had made their deeds seem pleasing to them. Korah (Qarun), Pharaoh, and Haman also acted arrogantly despite the clear proofs brought by Moses, and each was seized by a different form of punishment.

The parable of those who take protectors (awliya) other than Allah is like that of a spider that builds a web. Just as the spider's web is frail, so too is what they rely upon frail. This parable also encompasses hidden polytheism (shirk); those who perform worship with ostentation (riya) have also taken a protector other than Allah. Allah knows whatever things are invoked besides Him. He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. These parables are understood only by those possessed of knowledge. The heavens and the earth were created in truth; in this there is indeed a sign for the believers.

Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer restrains from shameful and evil deeds. The remembrance of Allah is the greatest act of worship. Fulfilling the prayer properly is achieved by observing its boundaries; otherwise, it distances one from Allah. Dispute with the People of the Book in the fairest manner, yet be firm against those who do wrong. Say to them, 'We believe in that which was revealed to us and in that which was revealed to you, and our God is One.' The Quran is attested to by most of those who were given the Scripture. Because you are unlettered (ummi), this Book is a miracle. None reject Our verses except the wrongdoers.

In verses 50–51, it is explained that the wrongdoers and the People of the Book deny that the Quran is a miracle and demand other miracles from Allah. In response to them, it is emphasized that all miracles are with Allah and that the Messenger of Allah is only a clear warner. Then, it is stated that this Book revealed to an unlettered prophet is, on its own, a sufficient miracle. As the occasion of revelation for these verses, it is narrated that when some Muslims wrote down and brought things they had heard from the Jews, the Prophet warned them and this verse was revealed. However, it is noted that this narration does not entirely fit the context of the verse, because the verse addresses the disbelievers.

In verses 52–55, it is stated that Allah is sufficient as a witness between the Prophet and the disbelievers, and that He knows everything in the heavens and the earth. It is announced that those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve will be the losers. Then, the disbelievers' haste in demanding punishment is criticized, and it is stated that were it not for an appointed term, the punishment would have come immediately; however, it will surely strike them suddenly while they do not perceive it. It is described that Hell will encompass the disbelievers, that on that Day the punishment will envelop them from every side, and that Allah will say, 'Taste the consequence of what you used to do.'

Verse 56 reads: "O My servants who have believed! Surely My earth is spacious, so worship only Me." The expression "'ibadi" (My servants) mentioned here is an address of honor and does not encompass the disbelievers. The verse points out the path of emigration (hijrah) to the believers who cannot practice their religion properly under oppression. That is to say, believers who find themselves in hardship and distress should migrate to another place and continue to worship Allah alone, making every sacrifice for this cause.

In verses 57–59, it is recalled that every soul will taste death and will ultimately be returned to Allah. Those who believe and do righteous deeds are promised mansions in Paradise, wherein they shall abide eternally. These are the ones who are patient and rely only upon their Lord. These verses emphasize that those who emigrate should not step back out of fear of death, because death is inevitable everywhere and what truly matters is sincere devotion to Allah.

In verses 60–63, it is stated that Allah provides the sustenance of many creatures and human beings that do not carry their own provision. It is noted that if the polytheists were asked who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say, "Allah." Likewise, they acknowledge that it is Allah who sends down water from the sky and revives the earth after its death. Despite this, it is questioned how they turn away from the truth and stray into polytheism (shirk). It is recalled that Allah extends provision abundantly for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills. These verses teach that those who emigrate should not be overwhelmed by worries over livelihood, and that they must trust that provision comes solely from Allah.

In verses 64–69, it is stated that the worldly life is nothing but diversion and play, and that the true life is the abode of the Hereafter. It is recounted that when people board a ship, they call upon Allah with sincere devotion, but as soon as they reach dry land, they revert to polytheism. It is mentioned that although Mecca was made a secure sanctuary, people believe in falsehood and show ingratitude. It is declared that none is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth, and that Hell is the abode for the disbelievers. Finally, the glad tidings are given that Allah will guide those who strive in His cause to His ways, and that He is with those who do good.

The letters 'Alif, Lam, Mim' at the beginning of the surah point to the miraculous nature of the Quran. These letters represent sounds originating from three basic points of articulation—the throat, the tongue, and the lips—and emphasize the literary miracle of the Quran.

The occasion of revelation of Surah ar-Rum was the period when the Byzantine (Roman) Empire suffered a great defeat against Persia. Between 613 and 616 CE, Persia had seized Syria, Palestine, Egypt, and Anatolia, bringing the Eastern Roman Empire to the brink of collapse. The Meccan polytheists rejoiced at this news and assumed an air of superiority over the Muslims. Thereupon, Allah revealed the verses announcing that the Romans would become victorious again within a few years.

Allah Almighty informed that the Romans would certainly be victorious after their defeat, and that this victory would take place within a few years (between 3 and 9 years). Upon this news from our Prophet (peace be upon him), a wager was made between Abu Bakr and the polytheist Ubayy ibn Khalaf. At the indication of the Prophet (peace be upon him), Abu Bakr increased the wager to 100 camels and 9 years. Indeed, on the day of the Battle of Badr, as the Romans defeated the Persians, the Muslims also gained victory over the polytheists. Thus, this report of the unseen from the Quran was fulfilled as a miracle.

Allah's promise is certain; both the victory of the Romans and the joy of the believers will come to pass. The expression 'to Allah belongs the command before and after' mentioned in the verse also indicates that following their victory, the Romans would one day be defeated by the Muslims. Indeed, in history, after defeating Persia, the Romans began to suffer defeat before the armies of Islam. This is another miracle of the Quran.

The verses state that the disbelievers only know the outward aspect of the life of this world and are heedless of the Hereafter. Yet the creation of the heavens, the earth, and man shows that everything has an end and that an account will be given in the Hereafter. Allah, reminding of the destruction of past nations, emphasizes that they wronged themselves.

In the continuation of the surah, proofs of Allah's power are enumerated: the creation of man from dust, the placement of love and mercy between spouses, the diversity of languages and colors, the alternation of night and day, sleep, seeking sustenance, and phenomena like lightning and rain all point to Allah's existence. On the Day of Resurrection, everyone will be raised and brought into His presence; while the believers enjoy blessings in Paradise, the disbelievers will suffer punishment.

In the final section of the surah, the importance of the five daily prayers is indicated: evening, night, morning, late afternoon, and noon. Glorification and praise belong exclusively to Allah. He brings out the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and gives life to the dead earth. In the same way, human beings will be brought forth from their graves.

One of the verses pointing to Allah's existence and power is His creation of man from dust. Had nature operated on its own, an advanced being like man could not have emerged from inanimate dust. Likewise, His creating spouses from among their own kind and placing love and mercy between them are among the proofs of His mercy. This order shows that humanity is prepared for high morality and civilization, and that woman must be protected.

The creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of languages and colors are also among Allah's signs. This diversity demonstrates His power and knowledge. Moreover, different nations and tribes were created so that people may know one another. Differences in language and color hold significant lessons for people of knowledge; knowing multiple languages serves as a means to better understand Allah's signs.

Sleeping during the night and day and seeking sustenance are also among Allah's blessings. Sleep is rest, while work is seeking His bounty. While working, one must recognize that earnings come from Allah, seek progress every day, and hope for His grace. These verses contain lessons for communities that stay alert and listen.

Allah shows lightning to cause fear and hope, and sends down water from the sky to revive the dead earth. This is proof of His power to resurrect the dead. Furthermore, the heaven and the earth stand by His command; when He summons you, you will emerge from the earth. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him; all are obedient to Him.

It is Allah Who originates creation and then repeats it; and repeating it is even easier for Him. To Him belong the highest attributes; He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. Allah presents to you an example from yourselves: Would any of your slaves ever be your partners? Associating partners with Allah is just as baseless. The wrongdoers follow their desires without knowledge, and no one can guide the one whom Allah has led astray.

O Prophet! Set your face toward the religion as a hanif (an upright monotheist), toward the innate disposition (fitrah) upon which Allah has created mankind. There is no altering Allah's creation. That is the correct religion, but most people do not know. Fitrah is the primordial nature upon which every child is born; later, their parents make them Jewish or Christian. Human nature is inherently inclined to recognize Allah and worship Him.

When an affliction touches people, they cry out to their Lord, but once they taste mercy from Him, a group of them immediately associate partners with Him. They show ingratitude for the blessings granted to them. We have not sent down to them any authority justifying what they associate with Him. When We cause people to taste mercy, they rejoice in it, but if an evil befalls them, they fall into despair. Allah expands sustenance for whom He wills and restricts it. So give the relative, the poor, and the traveler their due; this is best for those who desire Allah's pleasure.

Usury (riba) does not increase with Allah; but zakah increases manifold. It is Allah Who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will bring you to life; can any of your associated partners do any of these things? Exalted is Allah far above what they associate with Him.

Religion rests on two sources: fitrah (innate nature) and acquisition. Fitrah is a divine inclination that Allah has placed in our creation, directing us toward Him. Acquisition, however, since it is shaped by our feelings and thoughts, can lead to desires contrary to fitrah. For this reason, Allah commands us to turn toward the religion as a hanif (one who affirms the oneness of Allah) and to cling to fitrah. We must not attempt to alter Allah's creation, for corrupting the fitrah cannot restore the capacity we have lost.

In verse 31, everyone is commanded to turn to Allah in repentance and sincerity. In verse 32, the polytheists who divided their religion and became sects are condemned. They abandoned the fitrah and, driven by narrow-mindedness, followed their desires and split into factions. Yet the true religion consists of uprightly following the fitrah upon which all human beings were created. However, most people do not know this and follow customs or their own desires.

When people fall into hardship, by their very nature they implore Allah alone. But once Allah causes them to taste His mercy, some of them associate partners with Him. For instance, our nation pleaded in this manner during the Battles of Çanakkale. Verses 36–37 describe those who become arrogant when blessing arrives, yet fall into despair in hardship. In the noble hadith, the believer is likened to a fresh crop; as the wind blows, it bends and rises again. The disbeliever, on the other hand, is like a pine tree: once knocked down, it cannot rise again. Allah extends sustenance to whom He wills and restricts it.

In verse 38, the practical aspect of religion is summarized: giving relatives, the poor, and travelers their due. Those who seek Allah's pleasure will attain salvation. In verse 39, the subject of usury is addressed. Some state that conventional usury is meant here, while others say it refers to gifts given with the expectation of receiving more in return. In any case, usury and similar transactions do not increase with Allah; true increase lies in zakah and charity. In verse 40, Allah's attributes of creating, sustaining, causing to die, and bringing to life are recalled, emphasizing that the associated partners can do none of these things.

In verses 41–53, it is stated that corruption has appeared on land and sea because of the sins people have committed. Allah makes them taste some of the punishment in this world so that they may turn in repentance. They are commanded to travel through the earth to take a lesson from the end of past nations. The duty of the Prophet (peace be upon him) is to warn; however, he cannot make the disbelievers, who are like the dead, or the deaf hear. The winds, rain, and the revival of plants are signs of Allah's power. Likewise, He is capable of raising the dead.

In verses 54–60, it is recalled that man is created in a state of weakness, then gains strength, and then becomes weak again. On the Day of Resurrection, the sinners swear that they remained in the world for only a short while. The believers, however, tell them that the true duration extends until the Day of Resurrection. On that day, excuses will be of no avail. The Quran has set forth every kind of parable; yet the disbelievers still consider it a lie. Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know. The Prophet is commanded to be patient and to trust in Allah's promise, lest those who lack firm faith sway him toward laxity.

In the opening verses of Surah Luqman, it is stated that the Qur'an is a guidance and mercy for the doers of good (muhsinun). In Surah al-Baqarah, it was described as guidance for the God-fearing; here, because the degree of ihsan (excellence) is higher, mercy has also been added. Our Prophet (peace be upon him) explained ihsan as "worshiping Allah as if you see Him." Furthermore, the omission of the qualification of believing in the unseen in these verses demonstrates the elevated status of the muhsinun.

In verses 6–10, "idle talk" (lahw al-hadith) is condemned. This refers to things such as amusing tales, fables, and songs that divert people from the path of Allah. As the occasion of revelation for this verse, it is narrated that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith distracted people from the Qur'an with Persian tales and acquired a singing slave girl to entertain those who were inclined to become Muslims. Scholars differed over whether this verse also encompasses singing, yet the correct view is to take it in its general meaning. The expression "without knowledge" mentioned in the verse is linked, according to variant readings (qira'at), either to the verb "purchases" or considered a qualification of leading astray.

In verse 11, Allah's creation is pointed out, and people are asked to show what those besides Him have created, if indeed there are other creators. Worshiping entities that create nothing is a grave injustice. Here, a question may come to mind: Do humans not produce things through science and crafts? In response, it is emphasized that wisdom is a gift from Allah; therefore, the ultimate creator of what is made is Allah, and gratitude must be shown to Him. Polytheism (shirk) is the greatest injustice.

In verses 12–13, it is reported that wisdom (hikmah) was given to Luqman and that he was commanded to be grateful. Wisdom is reaching the correct goal by combining knowledge and action. Whether Luqman was a prophet is disputed; the majority hold the view that he was a sage. Wisdom was granted for gratitude; whoever is grateful is grateful for his own good, and whoever is ungrateful is ungrateful only to his own detriment. Then, Luqman's counsel to his son is recounted: "O my dear son! Do not associate partners with Allah, for polytheism is indeed a grave injustice."

Verses 14–15 command human beings to show goodness to their parents and to be grateful to them. However, if the parents compel one to associate partners with Allah, they must not be obeyed, though one should still maintain good companionship with them in worldly life. It is narrated that these verses were revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother. His mother opposed his becoming a Muslim and went on a hunger strike, whereas Sa'd risked everything for the sake of his religion. The verse defines the boundary of obedience to parents: obedience in matters that do not involve sin, and disobedience when it comes to polytheism.

In verses 16–19, Luqman's counsels to his son continue: Every deed, whether good or evil, even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, Allah will bring it forth. Establish the prayer, enjoin good, forbid evil, and bear patiently whatever befalls you. Do not be arrogant, do not walk swaggeringly upon the earth; maintain a moderate pace in your walking, and lower your voice. For indeed, the harshest of all sounds is the braying of donkeys. These counsels emphasize the transformation of wisdom into action and the importance of noble character.

In verses 20–30, Allah's blessings in the heavens and on the earth are recalled. Among people are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge and blindly follow their forefathers. Yet whoever turns to the truth has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. Even if the seas were ink and the trees were pens to write the words of Allah, they would not be exhausted. Creation and resurrection are as easy as the creation of a single soul. The merging of the night and day, and the sun and the moon running their courses for a specified term, demonstrate Allah's supreme power. Whatever is worshiped besides Him is falsehood.

In verses 31–33, the sailing of ships upon the sea is a blessing from Allah. When engulfed by waves, people plead with Allah in sincere devotion, but once saved, they show ingratitude. On the Day of Resurrection, neither a father can avail his child, nor can a child avail his father in any way. The life of this world must not deceive humanity, nor should Satan mislead them through Allah's forgiveness.

In verse 34, it is stated that knowledge of the Hour of Resurrection belongs solely to Allah, that He sends down the rain, that He knows whatever is in the wombs, and that no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die. These five matters are the keys to the unseen. The Prophet (peace be upon him) recited this verse and stated that the keys to the unseen are five. However, Allah's granting a portion of this knowledge to whichever prophet or angel He wills does not contradict this exclusivity. This is because Allah's knowledge encompasses all things, whereas the knowledge of others is limited and based on evidence.

The surah was revealed to warn a people to whom no warner had come before. This points to the inter-prophetic period (fatrah). Allah's creating the heavens and the earth in six days and then establishing Himself over the Throne (istiwa') does not signify resting, but rather exercising judgment and dominion.

Allah regulates affairs from the heavens, sending them down to the earth, and then those affairs ascend back to Him. This descent and ascent takes place in a day equal to a thousand years of what you count. This expression of a thousand years figuratively conveys a long span of time; it does not preclude it being less or more.
Allah has made everything He created good. As for man, He created him from an extracted quintessence, from a despised fluid. This points to the beginning of his creation.

On the Day of Resurrection, the sinners, with their heads bowed down, say: 'Our Lord! We have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteous deeds; we now believe with certainty.' Allah, however, decrees: 'Had I willed, I would have given guidance to everyone, but the word that I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humans together has come true.' It is said to them: 'Taste the punishment for having forgotten this day of yours; indeed, We too have forgotten you.'

Those who believe in Allah's verses fall down in prostration when they are reminded, glorify and praise their Lord, and do not act arrogantly. Their sides shun their beds, they pray to their Lord in fear and hope, and spend benevolently from the provision given to them. No soul knows what reward is prepared for them; these are things that will be a delight to the eyes.

While showing Mu'adh ibn Jabal the gates of goodness, our Prophet (peace be upon him) emphasized that fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sins, and highlighted the importance of the night prayer, then recited the verses, 'Their sides shun their beds...'

The believer and the transgressor (fasiq) are not equal. For those who believe and do righteous deeds, there are the Gardens of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa). As for the transgressors, their abode is the Fire. Every time they wish to come out of it, they are turned back into it and told: 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.' Before the greatest punishment, they are also made to taste a nearer punishment in this world so that they might perhaps return.

Just as Moses (Musa) was given the Scripture, you too have been given the Scripture; have no doubt about it. And it was made a guide for the Children of Israel. From among those who were patient, We raised leaders. Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding the matters wherein they differed. While the destruction of previous generations is a cautionary lesson, do they still not see that We send down water upon barren land and bring forth crops? And they ask, 'When is that conquest?' Say: 'On that day, faith will not benefit those who disbelieve.' So turn away from them and watch, for they too are watching.
O Prophet! Fear only Allah, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord and put your trust in Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise.

Allah has not placed two hearts inside any man. The custom of zihar has been abolished; declaring to your wives 'You are to me like my mother's back' does not make them your mothers. Nor should you regard your adopted sons as your real sons.

Call adopted children by their biological fathers' names. If you do not know who their fathers are, they are your brothers in religion and your wards. There is no sin upon you in what you do by mistake, but only in what you do with premeditation in your hearts. Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. His command takes precedence over the command of one's own desires. The Prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers. In the Book of Allah, blood relatives are closer to one another in inheritance than the other believers and the Emigrants (Muhajirun), except that you may make a bequest to your close friends.

A solemn covenant was taken from the prophets—from Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and especially from Muhammad. This was so that He might question the truthful about their truthfulness, and He has prepared a painful punishment for the disbelievers.

Remember Allah's favor upon you during the Battle of the Ahzab (the Confederates). Armies marched upon you, whereupon Allah sent against them a wind and unseen hosts. The cowardice of the hypocrites, their excuses, and their breach of covenants are recounted. Ultimately, Allah repelled the disbelievers in all their rage.

There is indeed an excellent example for you in the Messenger of Allah. When the believers saw the confederate armies, they said, 'This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us; Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.' The faithful remained true to their covenant; some have fulfilled their vow and achieved martyrdom, while others are still waiting. As for the hypocrites, Allah punished them or accepted their repentance. Allah struck terror into the hearts of the People of the Book and brought them down from their fortresses, granting their lands as an inheritance to the believers.

Some of the sincere believers who remained true to the covenant they made with Allah were determined to fight until they fell as martyrs. Figures such as Hamzah, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, and Anas ibn al-Nadr fulfilled their pledge and were martyred, while others, like Uthman and Talhah, await martyrdom. Allah spared the believers from fighting and repelled their enemies. Following this, the Banu Qurayzah from among the People of the Book—who had broken their treaty and supported the Confederates against the Muslims—were confronted. By the command of Gabriel, our Prophet marched upon the Banu Qurayzah, and after a siege of twenty to twenty-five days, according to the judgment rendered by Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, the men who took part in the hostilities were executed, and the women and children were taken captive.

When the wives of our Prophet requested an increase in their maintenance and finer garments, Allah Almighty granted them the choice between the life of this world and its adornment, or Allah, His Messenger, and the abode of the Hereafter. Beginning with Aisha, all of his wives chose Allah and His Messenger. The question arose whether this incident was a delegation of the right to divorce (tafwid al-talaq) or merely presenting them with a choice. According to the narration of Aisha, this was not deemed an act of divorce.

The Prophet's wives are not like any other women; any misconduct from them entails a double punishment in proportion to their honor and elevated status. Likewise, their obedience is rewarded twofold. Addressing them, it was commanded that they not speak in soft, flirtatious tones, lest anyone in whose heart is a sickness be moved with desire. Furthermore, they were commanded to abide settled in their homes, not to display their charms as was done in the times of former ignorance (Jahiliyyah), to establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. These verses made obligatory upon the Prophet's wives not only the standard veil (hijab), but also complete seclusion (khidr), meaning not appearing before non-mahram men at all. The expression 'O Ahl al-Bayt (people of the household)' encompasses the Messenger of Allah's wives, children, and close household members. The Shia's restriction of Ahl al-Bayt to Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn alone contradicts the explicit wording of the verse.

Allah has prepared forgiveness and an immense reward for Muslim men and Muslim women, believing men and believing women, the devout, the truthful, the patient, the humble, the charitable, the fasting, the men and women who guard their chastity, and the men and women who remember Allah frequently. This verse was revealed following the commandments directed at the Prophet's wives, when the believing women asked, 'Will nothing be revealed concerning us?' or when the Prophet's wives expressed concern, wondering, 'Will our obedience not be accepted?'

When Allah and His Messenger decree a matter, no believing man or believing woman has any choice remaining in their affair. This verse was revealed because our Prophet wished to arrange the marriage of his paternal aunt's daughter, Zaynab, to his freed slave, Zayd, but both initially objected. Zayd ibn Harithah had been captured in his childhood, presented as a gift to our Prophet, and was subsequently freed and adopted by him as a son. When his father and uncle arrived to take him back, Zayd chose to remain with our Prophet. Later, he was married to Zaynab, but because Zaynab looked down on him, he eventually sought a divorce. Our Prophet kept saying to him, 'Retain your wife and fear Allah,' while concealing within himself that Allah would marry Zaynab to him. When Zayd ultimately divorced her, Allah gave her in marriage to our Prophet, thereby removing any restriction for the believers regarding marrying the divorced wives of their adopted sons. This incident abolished the pagan practice of legal adoption and demonstrated that, in accordance with the established Sunnah of the prophets before him, there is no restriction upon our Prophet in that which Allah has ordained for him. Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not the father of any of your men; he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.

Regarding the story of Zaynab and Zayd, it has been discussed whether this incident took place in the manner often sensationalized. According to Elmalılı, there is nothing objectionable in the occurrence of this event, as it in no way compromises the prophets' inherent sinlessness and immunity from sin (ismah). However, from the perspective of hadith scholarship, the romanticized details are not found in authentic sources. Moreover, it is rationally impossible that the Messenger of Allah was seeing Zaynab's beauty for the first time, as Zaynab was his close relative and he had known her well beforehand. In truth, Zaynab had been reluctant from the outset because she did not consider Zayd her equal, entering the marriage solely in compliance with the Messenger of Allah's command. When Zayd could no longer endure this strained relationship and wished to separate, the Prophet advised him to keep his wife and to fear Allah.

The phrasing in the verse, 'You were concealing within yourself what Allah would bring to light,' points to the fact that while the Prophet recognized the suitability of Zaynab's divorce, he hid this thought out of concern for public gossip and people's reactions. Aisha remarked that if the Prophet were ever to conceal any part of the revelation, this verse would have been the one he would have hidden. This demonstrates the Prophet's profound piety, honesty, and uncompromising truthfulness. Once Zayd dissolved the marriage and her waiting period (iddah) expired, Allah contracted the marriage between them, establishing an important legal precedent for the ummah: that it is entirely permissible to marry women divorced by one's adopted sons, because adopted sons are not biological sons.

In reply to the Christians who raised objections against the Prophet's marriage, it was declared that there is no reproach or hardship upon the Prophet in what Allah has made lawful for him. Previous prophets also married; that John (Yahya) and Jesus (Isa) did not marry was not due to a prohibition, but was rather their personal circumstance. The command of Allah is a decree definitively determined and does not exceed the capacity of those bound by religious duty. The prophets conveyed the messages of Allah and feared none besides Him. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner.

Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not the father of any of your men. Even though he had sons, because they did not survive to adulthood, they do not fall under the category of mature men (rijal). He is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets. The term 'khatam' denotes both that which concludes and that which seals. He is a divine seal attesting to the truth of all preceding prophets; it is through his prophethood that the true reality and missions of earlier prophets are definitively confirmed.

The believers are commanded to remember Allah frequently and to glorify Him morning and evening. Allah and His angels shower mercy upon the believers. The Prophet was sent as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, a warner, a caller to Allah, and an illuminating lamp. One must not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, must pay no heed to their harassment, and must place trust in Allah.

The believers are informed that if they marry believing women and divorce them before touching them, no waiting period ('iddah) is required, and they must grant them a provision (mut'ah). Exclusively for the Prophet, the wives to whom he gave their bridal due (mahr), the concubines from the spoils of war, the relatives who emigrated, and believing women who offer themselves have been made lawful. Furthermore, he is free to defer whichever of his wives he wishes or take to himself whichever he wishes. This regulation is to please their hearts and bring them comfort.

After this, it is not lawful for the Prophet to marry other women or to exchange his current wives for others; only concubines are an exception. The believers are also commanded not to enter the houses of the Prophet before the proper time, but to enter when invited for a meal and then disperse. If they ask the wives of the Prophet for something they need, they should ask from behind a screen (hijab). This is purer for their hearts. It is forbidden to cause distress to the Prophet and to marry his wives after him.

In the 53rd verse, Allah Almighty commanded the believers not to enter the Prophet's house without permission and unseasonably. Two situations are at issue here: The first is the private state when one is alone with the Prophet, in which it is obligatory not to disturb him. The second is the moment when he is in public, in which respect must be shown to him. The occasion of revelation of the verse was that during the wedding feast for the marriage with Zaynab, some individuals arrived uninvited and sat for a long time, disturbing the Prophet. This verse also commands the hijab (veiling) for the Prophet's wives and explains the meaning of their being the mothers of the believers.

In verse 54, Allah states that He knows everything, whether you disclose it or conceal it, and that nothing remains hidden from Him. In verse 55, it is emphasized that the Prophet's wives are under no obligation to veil in the presence of their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the children of their brothers and sisters, their own women, and their slaves, but that they must still fear Allah. Because paternal and maternal uncles are not explicitly mentioned among these exceptions, some scholars considered it disliked (makruh) to sit unveiled in their presence.

In verse 56, it is stated that Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet, and the believers are called upon to send blessings and peace upon him as well. This shows that sending blessings (salawat) upon the Prophet is obligatory (fard). In the hadiths, it is stated that whoever does not send blessings when the Prophet's name is mentioned is reproached. In verses 57–58, it is stated that those who abuse Allah and His Messenger are cursed in this world and the hereafter, and those who harm believing men and believing women for what they have not done have burdened themselves with slander and a manifest sin.

In verse 59, the Prophet's wives, his daughters, and all believing women are commanded to draw their cloaks (jilbabs) closely around themselves. This is so that they may be recognized and not harassed. The jilbab refers to garments that cover from head to toe, such as the chador and ferace (loose cloak). This verse reinforces the modest covering (hijab) of free women and aims to protect their chastity and dignity. In verses 60–62, the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and those who spread false rumors in the city are warned that if they do not desist, the Prophet will be incited against them, and they will be cursed, seized, and slain.

Verses 63–68 recount that knowledge of the Hour of Resurrection is with Allah alone, that a blazing fire has been prepared for the disbelievers, and that they will say in regret, "If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger." In verses 69–71, the believers are commanded not to be like those who abused Moses (Musa), to fear Allah, and to speak words of appropriate justice and soundness. In verses 72–73, the concept of the Trust (amanah / moral responsibility) is explained: Allah offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they refused to bear it, while humankind undertook this heavy responsibility. Humankind is indeed very unjust and ignorant; yet Allah, who accepts the repentance of the believers, is Forgiving and Merciful.

The wisdom of the earth and the outcome of undertaking the Trust is this: Allah will certainly punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, requiting them for their betrayal of the Trust and their wrongdoing.

As for the believing men and believing women—that is, the believers who strive to fulfill the Trust—Allah will accept their repentance and show them His Divine Countenance through His mercy and forgiveness. Allah is Forgiving and deeply Merciful.

If the hypocrites and polytheists also repent and embrace faith, Allah will accept their repentance and forgive them as well. That is to say, just as the end of those who do not fulfill the Trust is terrible, those who obey Allah and His Messenger and fulfill the Trust with faith attain the greatest triumph and achieve the Divine Countenance.

This blessing and mercy are worthy of praise and gratitude. For this reason, how fitting it is that Surah Saba, which follows immediately after, begins with "praise to Allah": "Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds."

This, then, is the outcome of the Trust: those who betray it meet with punishment, while those who remain faithful attain Allah's mercy and His Divine Countenance. This is a manifestation of Allah's justice and mercy.

There are five surahs in the Quran that begin with praise (hamd): al-Fatihah, al-An'am, al-Kahf, Saba', and Fatir. Allah's blessings are of two kinds: origination (ijad) and continuation (ibqa). In each surah, reference is made to these two blessings. In Surah Saba', by recalling the blessing of the Hereafter and the recreation of life, it is emphasized that all praise belongs to Allah. He is the owner of whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Both the blessings of this world and the blessings of the Hereafter are of His bestowal.

Allah knows whatever enters into the earth and whatever comes out of it, and whatever descends from heaven and whatever ascends into it. He is the All-Wise (al-Hakim) and the All-Aware (al-Khabir). Those who deny the Resurrection do not deem it possible because they do not know the unseen (ghayb). Yet Allah's knowledge encompasses all things; everything is clear in the Manifest Book (Kitab al-Mubin). This knowledge and power necessitate the coming of the Day of Resurrection. That Hour will surely come in order to reward those who believe and do righteous deeds.

The disbelievers mock prophethood. Yet those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in pangs of conscience even in this world. Allah warns them: Do they not look at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them up or cause pieces from the sky to fall upon them. Indeed, in this is a lesson for every servant who turns to Allah.

The virtue bestowed upon David (Dawud): The mountains and the birds glorified Allah along with him, and iron was made pliable in his hands. He used to make coats of armor. The melodious voice of David and the miracle of the Psalms (Zabur) are recounted. The spiritual value of a beautiful voice and melody is not merely physical. The essential point is to convey the meaning. This art is intended for beneficial endeavors, just as crafting protective armor for battle.

To Solomon (Sulayman) were given the wind and a spring of molten copper. The jinn also worked under his command. They made for him sanctuaries, statues, basins like reservoirs, and cooking pots fixed into the ground. Solomon's death was only realized through a wood-boring creature that ate away his staff. Thus, it became evident that the jinn do not know the unseen.

The cautionary tale of the people of Saba': Two gardens—while gratitude was demanded of them, they turned away. Thereupon, the flood of 'Arim was sent upon them, and their gardens were transformed into ruined gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisks, and a few lote trees (sidir). This was the recompense for their ingratitude. Thus does Allah penalize the persistently ungrateful.

The people of Saba' possessed towns close to one another between blessed lands. They used to travel in safety. However, they asked for the distance between their journeys to be lengthened and wronged themselves. Allah turned them into legendary tales and scattered them completely. Iblis's assumption about them proved true; most of them followed him. Yet Iblis had no real authority over them; the purpose was to distinguish the one who believes in the Hereafter from the one who is in doubt concerning it. And Allah is watchful over all things.

The people of Saba' lived in the city of Ma'rib in Yemen. There were for them two lush gardens that served as a sign. These gardens were vineyards and orchards flanking them on the right and on the left. It was said to them, 'Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him.' Their land was fair and their Lord was Oft-Forgiving. But they turned away and did not show gratitude.

Thereupon, Allah unleashed upon them the flood of 'Arim.' Arim was a great dam built by Bilqis. The gap between two mountains had been closed with stones and pitch, and waters were collected. According to various narrations, the dam may have been built by Saba', Himyar, Luqman, or Bilqis. All of them may have carried out construction and repair in succession. When the dam collapsed, their gardens turned into bitter tamarisk, tarfa, and thorny trees.

We replaced their two gardens with trees bearing bitter fruit. Because of their ingratitude, their gardens were ruined. Furthermore, We had placed between them and the towns We had blessed visible towns situated side by side. Travel was safe and easy. But they did not want this blessing, saying, 'Our Lord, make the distance between our journeys longer.' So We scattered them utterly; the tribes were dispersed.

Iblis proved his assumption about them to be true. Except for the sincere believers, most of them followed Iblis. This was not due to any power of Satan, but rather due to their lack of faith in the Hereafter. Allah's command is supreme. Your Lord is watchful over all things.

Those who invoke idols besides Allah should know that they have no power over anything. Intercession is only for those who are permitted. On the Day of Resurrection, when terror is removed from their hearts, the intercessors say, 'What did your Lord say?' And they reply, 'He spoke the truth.' Allah is exalted above all things.

The disbelievers said that they did not believe in the Quran nor in the scriptures before it. On the Day of Gathering (Mahshar), they will blame one another. Those who were arrogant will deny having led the weak astray. Yet they used to plot day and night. When they see the punishment, they will regret it, but it will be of no avail.

Neither wealth nor children will bring you closer to Allah; only faith and righteous deeds bring one closer. The believers are in safety in Paradise. Those who strive against Our verses to invalidate them will be subjected to punishment. Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it.

Our Prophet was told: 'Stand up for Allah in pairs, in threes, and individually, and reflect.' There is no madness in him. He is only a warner. The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Those who do not believe will regret, but it will be too late. A barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, just as was done with their predecessors.

The word "Fatir" mentioned in the first verse of Surah Fatir means to split open and is used in the sense of originating creation. Elmalılı states that this word expresses both the initial creation and the recreation on the Day of Resurrection. Furthermore, it is explained that the angels are messengers and were created with two, three, and four wings. These numbers of wings are not meant for restriction, but to indicate abundance; indeed, Gabriel was seen with six hundred wings. Allah adds to creation as He wills.

In the second verse, it is emphasized that whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold, and whatever He withholds, none can release. He is the Almighty and the All-Wise. The third verse calls people to reflect upon Allah's blessings. The fourth verse offers comfort to the Prophet. In the fifth and sixth verses, warnings are given regarding the deceptive nature of worldly life and Satan's deception in the name of Allah. In the seventh verse, it is announced that there is a severe punishment for the disbelievers, and forgiveness and a great reward for the believers.

In the eighth verse, it is understood that the person whose evil deeds are made appealing to him is not like those who believe and perform righteous deeds. Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. In the ninth verse, the resurrection after death (nushur) is described through the winds lifting the clouds and giving life to a dead land. In the tenth verse, it is stated that whoever desires honor can only attain it through good words that ascend to Allah and the righteous deeds that elevate them.

In the eleventh verse, it is recounted that man was created from dust, then from a drop of sperm (nutfah), made into pairs, and that everything is recorded in a Book. In the twelfth verse, it is conveyed that the two seas are not equal, and from each—both fresh and salt water—fresh meat and ornaments are extracted. The thirteenth verse demonstrates the sovereignty of Allah's kingdom through the merging of night and day, and the subjugation of the sun and the moon. It is emphasized that the idols cannot manage even something as trivial as the thin membrane of a date stone ("qitmir").

In the eighteenth verse, it is explained that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that everyone will carry their own responsibility. It is described that even if a heavily laden soul calls out, none of its load will be carried, and close kinship will be of no avail. Only those who fear their Lord in the unseen (ghayb) and establish prayer are purified. In verses nineteen through twenty-two, it is expressed that the believer and the disbeliever are not equal, using the analogies of the blind and the seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and the dead and the living. The Prophet is only a warner.

Starting from the twenty-seventh verse, examples are given of Allah sending down water from the sky, producing fruits of diverse colors, and mountains having tracks of various hues. In the twenty-eighth verse, it is stated that humans, beasts, and cattle are likewise of diverse colors, and that only those with knowledge truly fear Allah. In verses twenty-nine and thirty, it is explained that those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what they have been provided secretly and openly hope for an unperishing trade, and will receive their rewards in full. In the thirty-second verse, it is stated that the Book was inherited by the chosen servants, and that these servants fall into three classes: those who wrong themselves, those who follow a middle course, and those who are foremost in good deeds. Following this, the blessings of Paradise and the torment of Hell are depicted.

The diversity of colors in the mountains is proof of Allah's divine power. Among humans, beasts, and cattle, there are likewise those of diverse colors. Reverence and fear of Allah are found only in those who possess knowledge. Scholars are the ones who fear Him the most because they know Allah's majesty and forgiveness.

Those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer properly, and spend secretly and openly from the sustenance given to them hope for a trade that will never perish. Allah will grant them their rewards in full and bestow upon them even more from His bounty. He is Forgiving (Ghafur) and Appreciative (Shakur); He pardons sins and does not leave righteous deeds unrewarded.

The Book revealed to you is the Book that confirms what came before it and distinguishes truth from falsehood. Then We made that Book an inheritance for those whom We chose among Our servants. Among them are some who wrong themselves, some who follow a middle course, and some who take the lead in good deeds. Indeed, being foremost in good deeds is the great favor.

The chosen servants will enter the Gardens of Eden ('Adn) and will be adorned with bracelets of gold. There, they will be greeted with "Peace." While in the world, Allah had granted them enough of a lifetime to reflect and sent them a warner. They no longer have any excuse.

Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; He sees what is within the hearts. It is He who made you successors upon the earth. Whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is against himself.
